body:
SCOTUS Declines to Revive USPS Election-Mail Rule

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/grantdemocracy/grant-report-july-16-12775215?e=c16f400a56)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/fa4IunCrkCs?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a)
| | **Supreme Court Declines to Revive USPS Election-Mail Rule****By Justin Riemer, President, USGI** On Monday, September 14, the Supreme Court effectively closed the door on pre-election implementation of a key component of President Trump’s Executive Order 14399, the administration’s directive on citizenship verification and mail-in voting in federal elections. At issue was a recently finalized U.S. Postal Service rulemaking that would require states to use standardized, barcoded ballot envelopes, submit voter-level mailing data to a new federal portal, and obtain USPS clearance before ballots go out. A coalition of states and progressive interest groups sued, and a Massachusetts federal district court preliminarily enjoined its enforcement. After the First Circuit did not immediately act on the government’s stay request, the Department of Justice asked the Supreme Court for a stay.For election officials and observers, the immediate takeaway is that the USPS requirements will not govern this election cycle, but the legal fight over how far federal agencies may go in setting election-mail rules is likely to continue.This was the second time the dispute had reached the Court. On August 24, before the USPS finalized the rule, the Court had granted the government a [stay](https://us.list-manage.com/151HsHtzFhW?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) of an earlier injunction by the district court in a 6-3 vote on standing and ripeness grounds, without reaching the merits. This time, the Court denied relief in a [per curiam ruling](https://us.list-manage.com/YPtn_IJilMW?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a), concluding that the government was unlikely to succeed on the merits and that the balance of equities did not favor a stay. Justice Kavanaugh concurred in the denial but wrote separately that the USPS rule had “at least a fair prospect” of being lawful. Justice Alito, joined by Justice Thomas, dissented and would have granted the stay.Given their dissent when the Court granted the first stay, Justices Kagan, Sotomayor, and Jackson almost certainly voted to deny the later stay. That means at least one of Chief Justice Roberts and Justices Gorsuch and Barrett joined the denial, and probably more than one given none of them issued a dissent or joined Justice Alito’s.The case will now continue in the district court, where the final outcome appears predictable. Still, DOJ is likely to ask the Supreme Court to review the dispute again in a less expedited posture. A related consolidated case is pending in the D.C. District Court, which preliminarily enjoined the rule on September 13.Justice Alito’s dissent outlines one path by which the Court could eventually uphold the rulemaking. In addition to raising standing concerns for some plaintiffs, he framed the dispute as a tension between the plaintiffs’ argument that the rule intrudes on state and congressional authority under the Elections Clause and the USPS’s statutory authority “to provide for the collection, handling, transportation, delivery, forwarding, returning, and holding of mail, and for the disposition of undeliverable mail.” 39 U.S.C. § 404(a)(1).The dissent’s more technical point is that the plaintiffs may have a cause-of-action problem. Congress has “broadly exempted” USPS from Administrative Procedure Act review, and the dissent concluded that exemption applied here. On that view, the plaintiffs would be left with only an equitable ultra vires claim, which requires showing that the agency acted “entirely in excess of the agency’s delegated powers and contrary to a specific prohibition in the statute.” The dissent described that kind of claim as “essentially a Hail Mary pass.”It is unclear, maybe even unlikely, that a majority of the Court will adopt that framework. But at least three justices appear open to it. If the case returns to the Court in a more traditional posture, watch Chief Justice Roberts and Justices Kavanaugh, Gorsuch, and Barrett—especially once the Court no longer has to weigh the potential near-term disruption to election officials and voters that shaped the emergency stay posture.
---
| | | | |
---
| | **Alaska** The Department of Law [dropped charges](https://us.list-manage.com/e1WUucO71Q9?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) against 11 American Samoan residents of Whittier accused of voting illegally, after the Alaska Court of Appeals held that a conviction requires proof the voter intended to deceive election officials.The Division of Elections [changed its delivery policy](https://us.list-manage.com/2yuz4BNoOV7?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) for the general election, rerouting absentee ballots cast at in-person rural polling stations to its Anchorage office, after 75 such ballots reached the Nome regional office too late to be counted in the August primary.**California** Governor Gavin Newsom [signed](https://us.list-manage.com/3jxmT2Jo3YS?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a package of election-related bills that creates new criminal penalties for interfering with ballots, election records, voting technology, and the delivery of vote-by-mail ballots. The package also addresses election cybersecurity, language access, drop-off locations, deceptive election communications, and procedures for voting by mail ballot at polling places.**Florida** A Russian national [was sentenced](https://us.list-manage.com/Lm6X62HOZsL?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) to six years in federal prison for a synthetic identity fraud scheme that included submitting more than 100 fraudulent voter registration applications to the Pinellas County Supervisor of Elections to create fake identities to obtain fraudulent credit cards and loans.**Minnesota** Federal prosecutors [charged](https://us.list-manage.com/Vl_b7Ir3KW9?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) an Indian national with making a false claim of U.S. citizenship to vote in the 2024 general election. Prosecutors allege the man knowingly made a false citizenship statement to vote.**New Hampshire** Secretary of State Scanlan [directed local officials](https://us.list-manage.com/10WqvqXo6Jf?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) to preserve all ballots and records from the 2024 general election, which had become eligible for destruction under the 22-month retention period, after the U.S. Department of Justice instructed the state in writing to retain them.**Ohio** Secretary of State Frank LaRose [published](https://us.list-manage.com/6rHlO1_OWF0?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a list of 208,856 inactive voter registrations scheduled for removal from the state’s voter rolls in January 2027 under Ohio’s General Voter Records Maintenance Program. No registrations on the list will be canceled before the November 3 general election, and voters can keep their registrations active by voting, updating or confirming their information, submitting an absentee ballot application, or engaging in another qualifying activity.**Pennsylvania** The U.S. Department of Homeland Security [told](https://us.list-manage.com/Nk6DbNG4tYj?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) Pennsylvania officials that it identified 14,576 potential noncitizen registrants by comparing the state’s publicly available voter roll against internal immigration databases using personally identifiable information such as names, dates of birth, addresses, and phone numbers. DHS said it would provide the state with the list for review. **Texas** State and federal prosecutors [charged seven people](https://us.list-manage.com/18nBdY0HOaY?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) in Tarrant County with voting-related offenses, including illegal voting in the 2024 general election and false claims of citizenship to register.The Secretary of State’s Office [referred](https://us.list-manage.com/UVkAvT_jCFh?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) 117 potential noncitizen voting cases to the Attorney General and directed county registrars to reinstate 578 registrants flagged through SAVE whose citizenship the state has since confirmed.**Utah** Legislative auditors [found compliance errors](https://us.list-manage.com/gHg14NYKISl?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) in Utah, Wasatch, and San Juan counties, including a double vote counted in Wasatch County when in-person vote credit was not uploaded to the separate mail ballot processing system, and recommended stronger compliance oversight by the Lieutenant Governor’s Office. A link to the audit materials is available [here](https://us.list-manage.com/5MJnkxtv1mZ?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a).Federal prosecutors [charged](https://us.list-manage.com/rx2QNgMXlKH?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a former U.S. Postal Service worker with unlawfully disposing of approximately 300 mail-in ballots to registered voters in Utah during the state’s June 23 primary election. Prosecutors allege the ballots and other mail were thrown into a church parking [lot]() dumpster.**Virginia** The Department of Elections [issued guidance](https://us.list-manage.com/TGJJ7iwhh4P?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) limiting disqualification of voters with felony convictions who are no longer incarcerated to those convicted of murder or voluntary or involuntary manslaughter, implementing a federal court ruling under the Virginia Readmission Act.Virginia election officials are [reviewing](https://us.list-manage.com/w2sJp17cbOy?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a misleading online ballot image posted by the state senate majority leader that appeared to list the wrong candidate for the Eighth Congressional District. According to the article, the image was not an official ballot but circulated widely enough to raise questions. The Department of Elections said it is examining the issue and emphasized that official ballots must accurately present candidates’ names and party labels.
---
|
---
| | **New York** The New York State Board of Elections unanimously [approved](https://us.list-manage.com/QkN_LLyMb_s?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) regulations establishing procedures for local boards that use ballot drop boxes. The rules address dropbox design and labeling, video surveillance, bipartisan ballot retrieval teams, and locations. Local boards are not required to use drop boxes.
---
|
---
| | **Colorado** _**Peters v. People**_**, No. 26SC332 (Colo.)** The state Supreme Court [declined](https://us.list-manage.com/evbK_e4ILEw?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) review of former Mesa County clerk Tina Peters’ prosecution for permitting unauthorized access to voting equipment. Governor Jared Polis had previously commuted her sentence, but Peters had petitioned the Supreme Court to overturn her trial court conviction based on its refusal to instruct the jury on affirmative defenses and by excluding evidence.**Delaware** _**Hocker v. Albence**_**, No. 2026-1021-BWD (Del.)** On September 16, the state Supreme Court [heard](https://us.list-manage.com/TutAaSiMHxD?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) arguments in an expedited appeal challenging the state’s permanent absentee voting law. The challengers [argue](https://us.list-manage.com/XcXYgyEAp6x?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that the Delaware Constitution [requires]() absentee voters to establish their eligibility anew for each election. **District of Columbia** _**League of United Latin American Citizens v. U.S. Department of Homeland Security**_ , **No. 1:26-cv-03157 (D.D.C.)** On September 10, the League of United Latin American Citizens, Common Cause, UnidosUS, and the City and County of Denver [filed suit](https://us.list-manage.com/4JsSj_pS4Ct?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) seeking to enjoin what plaintiffs describe as a federal “Polling Place Policy” and a declaration that 18 U.S.C. § 592 bars armed federal officers at polling sites._**NAACP v. U.S. Department of Homeland Security**_**, No. 1:26-cv-03263 (D.D.C.)** On September 18, the NAACP and eight other organizations [filed suit](https://us.list-manage.com/SwIkAz6LPWs?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) against the Department of Homeland Security and other federal officials, alleging that deploying armed federal agents at or near polling places would violate Section 11(b) of the Voting Rights Act, and seeking to bar deployments that intimidate voters or those assisting them. _**DSCC v. Trump**_**, No. 1:26-cv-01114 (D.D.C.)** On September 13, a federal court [granted a preliminary injunction](https://us.list-manage.com/Jye2XlbQgvo?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) barring enforcement of the U.S. Postal Service’s ballot mail rule in three consolidated suits, holding that plaintiffs are likely to succeed on their claim that the rule’s Federal Ballot Mail Portal enrollment and verification requirements exceed the Postal Service’s authority under the Postal Reorganization Act._**League of Women Voters v. U.S. Department of Homeland Security**_**, No. 1:25-cv-03501 (D.D.C.)** On September 15, the League of Women Voters and the Electronic Privacy Information Center (EPIC) [urged](https://us.list-manage.com/rGK99gpLRgi?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the U.S. Supreme Court to deny the federal government’s application to stay an order barring use of the modified SAVE citizenship verification system._**American Oversight v. U.S. Postal Service**_**, No. 1:26-cv-03223 (D.D.C.)** On September 15, American Oversight [filed suit](https://us.list-manage.com/ffbm9BN70wJ?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) under FOIA to compel the U.S. Postal Service to produce records on the development of the Federal Ballot Mail Portal.**Illinois** _**Lopez v. Illinois State Board of Elections**_**, No. 1:26-cv-9156 (N.D. Ill.)** On September 21, a federal district court [dismissed](https://us.list-manage.com/8ewyldRY1av?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) without prejudice a constitutional challenge to Illinois’s ballot-access requirements for independent congressional candidates. The court held that Illinois’s 5% signature requirement, even when considered together with the state’s other ballot-access restrictions, imposed a reasonable, nondiscriminatory burden justified by the state’s asserted interests.**Indiana** _**In re Election Recount: Deery v. Copenhaver**_**, No. 26S-EX-293 (Ind.)** On September 10, the Indiana Supreme Court [set aside](https://us.list-manage.com/MWXSPi8DwUx?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the Indiana Recount Commission’s determination that Paula Copenhaver had won the Republican primary for State Senate District 23. The court held that Indiana law requires counting a qualifying ballot despite a defect caused by an election officer and ordered the Commission to recertify the results showing Spencer Deery ahead by three votes. _**League of Women Voters of Indiana v. Morales**_**, No. 1:25-cv-02150 (S.D. Ind.)** On September 10, a federal court [dismissed](https://us.list-manage.com/13a5MmdhKy7?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) without prejudice a challenge to Indiana’s citizenship verification statutes, holding the plaintiff organizations failed to allege standing, granted them 28 days to amend, and denied the pending motion for a preliminary injunction.**Massachusetts** _**California v. United States Postal Service**_**, No. 1:26-cv-13917 (D. Mass.)** On September 10, the First Circuit [denied](https://us.list-manage.com/6F80Xa5zVtd?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the federal government’s motion to stay the preliminary injunction barring enforcement of the U.S. Postal Service’s ballot mail rule for the November 3 election.As discussed above, on September 14, the U.S. Supreme Court [denied](https://us.list-manage.com/yai2erWanqd?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the federal government’s application to stay the injunction, concluding that it was unlikely to succeed on the merits and that the balance of equities also weighed against a stay.**Minnesota** _**City of Oak Grove v. Simon**_**, No. A26-0910 (Minn.)** On September 11, the Minnesota Supreme Court [granted](https://us.list-manage.com/10S4wChQPCL?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the City of Oak Grove’s petition under Minn. Stat. § 204B.44, holding that Minn. Stat. § 201.225 gives the city, not Anoka County, authority to choose paper voter rosters for precincts within its boundaries in the November general election.**Missouri** _**Onder, et al. v. Missouri, et al.**_**, No. 26-2797 (8th Cir.)** On September 21, the Eighth Circuit issued a permanent injunction [ordering](https://us.list-manage.com/15wKhYPn91X?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) Missouri to use the congressional map employed in its August primary rather than the 2022 map reinstated by the Missouri Supreme Court, concluding that switching maps between the primary and general elections would violate the Constitution. Consequently, the Eighth Circuit ordered the district court to administratively stay the permanent injunction for seven days to allow the parties to seek review from the U.S. Supreme Court. Intervenor-defendants immediately sought a [stay](https://us.list-manage.com/R1rgvDueFAJ?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) with the Supreme Court and Justice Kavanaugh ordered a response by 2 p.m. on Wednesday. The Supreme Court has not taken action as of the time of this release._**La Strada v. Hoskins**_**, No. 26AC-CC00592 (Mo. Cir. Ct., Cole Cnty.)** On September 14, Nick La Strada, whom Secretary of State Hoskins dismissed as director of election integrity in May, [filed suit](https://us.list-manage.com/_nnyxzKrWSe?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) in state court alleging he was fired for reporting a discussion among office staff about fabricating evidence for a federal HAVA proceeding and for objecting to other actions by the office._**Bermudez v. Hoskins**_**, No. 26AC-CC00591 (Mo. Cir. Ct., Cole Cnty.)** On September 11, five voters [filed suit](https://us.list-manage.com/1BFkcMVN_Xm?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) in state court seeking class certification and about $80 million in statutory damages from Secretary of State Hoskins, alleging he neglected his duties by declaring the congressional map referendum petition insufficient and by directing local election officials to use the 2025 map contrary to a Missouri Supreme Court order._**Dennis v. Hoskins**_**, No. 26AC-CC00610 (Mo. Cir. Ct., Cole Cnty.)** On September 16, two voters [filed](https://us.list-manage.com/vmh1PsTesmK?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a second proposed class action against Secretary Hoskins in state court, seeking $500 per member plus compensatory damages for voters who cast August primary ballots in one congressional district but will vote in another on November 3, alleging his delay in ruling on the referendum caused the primary to run under the 2025 map._**Missouri v. U.S. Department of Commerce**_**, No. 4:26-cv-00131 (E.D. Mo.)** On September 18, Missouri [voluntarily dismissed](https://us.list-manage.com/YPie5Kiryl7?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) its federal lawsuit [challenging](https://us.list-manage.com/8W5dsohWkt0?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the Census Bureau’s inclusion of undocumented immigrants and temporary visa holders in the population count used for congressional apportionment. Missouri had sought to require the federal government to revise the 2020 Census methodology and prohibit those populations from being counted in the 2030 Census.**New Jersey** _**Republican National Committee v. Caldwell**_**, No. TBD (D. N.J.)** On September 22, Republican committees and elected officials [filed](https://us.list-manage.com/lZBIoLEnK3N?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) suit against Secretary of State Caldwell and election officials in five counties, alleging they failed to produce federally mandated voter roll maintenance records requested under the National Voter Registration Act. The plaintiffs seek an order requiring production of records concerning the state’s voter-list maintenance practices.**New York** _**Matter of Hansen v. Suffolk County Bd. of Elections**_**, No. 2026-04740 (N.Y. App. Div.)** On September 14, a New York appellate court [dismissed](https://us.list-manage.com/Du4o1QmIrcz?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) as untimely a proceeding seeking to validate a designating petition for a Suffolk County Republican committee position. The court held that the candidate had to comply with Election Law § 16-102’s short filing deadlines and could not rely on the longer limitations period under CPLR Article 78.**North Carolina** _**Stein v. Hall**_**, No. 23CV029308-910 (N.C. Ct. App.)** On September 16, the North Carolina Court of Appeals [reversed](https://us.list-manage.com/MhRatl2cvzZ?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a trial court’s ruling that had invalidated provisions of Senate Bill 382 transferring appointment authority over the State Board of Elections from the governor to the state auditor. In a 2–1 decision, the court held that the transfer did not clearly violate separation of powers because North Carolina's executive authority is divided among specialized members of the Council of State._**North Carolina Alliance for Retired Americans, et al. v. North Carolina State Board of Elections et al.**_**, No. 1:26-cv-965 (M.D.N.C.)** On September 22, several voting rights organizations and individual voters [filed suit](https://us.list-manage.com/N13omhM0f2V?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) challenging new absentee ballot procedures adopted by the North Carolina State Board of Elections. The plaintiffs allege that the rules unlawfully reject ballots with unsealed inner envelopes and require signatures without a verification standard. They seek to enjoin those policies for the 2026 election and future elections.**South Carolina** _**ACLU of South Carolina Foundation v. State Election Commission**_**, No. 2026-CP-40-06706 (S.C. Ct. of Common Pleas)** On September 17, the ACLU of South Carolina [filed](https://us.list-manage.com/o5iMCTG7MAt?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) suit alleging that the State Election Commission violated the South Carolina Freedom of Information Act during the 2025 removal of Executive Director Howard Knapp. The complaint alleges that the Commission conducted official business outside a public meeting, failed to provide proper notice before a closed executive session, and secretly polled commissioners. The ACLU seeks disclosure of records relating to the session in which Knapp’s removal was discussed.**South Dakota** _**League of Women Voters of South Dakota v. Johnson**_**, No. 4:26-CV-04162-ECS (D.S.D.)** On September 11, the district court [heard](https://us.list-manage.com/7b1gQo5bxJE?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) argument on a preliminary injunction motion challenging South Dakota’s notices to voters designated as “federal only.” The court denied the motion after Secretary of State Johnson corrected form letters for voters registered as federal-only, instructed them to notify affected voters how to restore full voter status before the October 19 registration deadline, and asked the state’s voter registration vendor to disable the feature that generated the inaccurate letters**Texas** _**In re Rose**_**, No. 26-0916 (Tex.)** On September 11, the state Supreme Court [barred](https://us.list-manage.com/KbF4puB2_e7?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) Galveston County from using commissioner, constable, and justice of the peace precinct lines adopted in June for the November general election, holding that a county may not change precinct lines between a primary and the corresponding general election.**Vermont** _**United States v. Hanzas**_**, No. 2:25-cv-00903 (D. Vt.)** On September 17, a federal district court [dismissed](https://us.list-manage.com/yWddJL5GGHf?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the U.S. Department of Justice lawsuit seeking Vermont’s unredacted state voter file. Wash.)** On September 22, the district court [dismissed](https://us.list-manage.com/K4O_0h1Xnnz?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the DOJ’s lawsuit seeking Washington’s unredacted voter rolls.**Wisconsin** _**Gavery v. Harris**_**(Wis. The cases include two noncitizens accused of voting in federal elections, a Louisiana mayoral candidate accused of registering an ineligible voter, and three California defendants accused of using stolen voter identities to obtain signatures for ballot petitions. Kambli contends that the state court created an untenable conflict by providing little guidance on how election officials could comply. In contrast, subsequent federal court orders pointed in the opposite direction, leaving officials caught between competing state and federal commands.M.D. Kittle [argues](https://us.list-manage.com/zFSKFJZBpae?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that New Jersey’s discovery of thousands of noncitizens on its voter rolls points to a broader vulnerability in states that combine automatic voter registration with driver’s license access for noncitizens. The piece argues that clearer shared terminology and comparable measures would help administrators, researchers, policymakers, and the public better evaluate list-maintenance systems and distinguish routine registration updating from improper voter removal.Professor Charles Stewart [argues](https://us.list-manage.com/4SAI0d0JNFU?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that the available evidence does not support broad claims that mail-ballot transmission problems are systematically disadvantaging one party. Reviewing recent data on mail-ballot return rates and rejected ballots, Stewart notes that while mail voting remains vulnerable to ordinary delivery delays, voter error, and administrative variation, the patterns do not show a clear partisan skew large enough to substantiate claims of a targeted or structurally biased mail-ballot problem.

clean_body: SCOTUS Declines to Revive USPS Election-Mail Rule | | | | | | | | | Supreme Court Declines to Revive USPS Election-Mail RuleBy Justin Riemer, President, USGI On Monday, September 14, the Supreme Court effectively closed the door on pre-election implementation of a key component of President Trump’s Executive Order 14399, the administration’s directive on citizenship verification and mail-in voting in federal elections. At issue was a recently finalized U.S. Postal Service rulemaking that would require states to use standardized, barcoded ballot envelopes, submit voter-level mailing data to a new federal portal, and obtain USPS clearance before ballots go out. A coalition of states and progressive interest groups sued, and a Massachusetts federal district court preliminarily enjoined its enforcement. After the First Circuit did not immediately act on the government’s stay request, the Department of Justice asked the Supreme Court for a stay.For election officials and observers, the immediate takeaway is that the USPS requirements will not govern this election cycle, but the legal fight over how far federal agencies may go in setting election-mail rules is likely to continue.This was the second time the dispute had reached the Court. On August 24, before the USPS finalized the rule, the Court had granted the government a of an earlier injunction by the district court in a 6-3 vote on standing and ripeness grounds, without reaching the merits. This time, the Court denied relief in a , concluding that the government was unlikely to succeed on the merits and that the balance of equities did not favor a stay. Justice Kavanaugh concurred in the denial but wrote separately that the USPS rule had “at least a fair prospect” of being lawful. Justice Alito, joined by Justice Thomas, dissented and would have granted the stay.Given their dissent when the Court granted the first stay, Justices Kagan, Sotomayor, and Jackson almost certainly voted to deny the later stay. That means at least one of Chief Justice Roberts and Justices Gorsuch and Barrett joined the denial, and probably more than one given none of them issued a dissent or joined Justice Alito’s.The case will now continue in the district court, where the final outcome appears predictable. Still, DOJ is likely to ask the Supreme Court to review the dispute again in a less expedited posture. A related consolidated case is pending in the D.C. District Court, which preliminarily enjoined the rule on September 13.Justice Alito’s dissent outlines one path by which the Court could eventually uphold the rulemaking. In addition to raising standing concerns for some plaintiffs, he framed the dispute as a tension between the plaintiffs’ argument that the rule intrudes on state and congressional authority under the Elections Clause and the USPS’s statutory authority “to provide for the collection, handling, transportation, delivery, forwarding, returning, and holding of mail, and for the disposition of undeliverable mail.” 39 U.S.C. § 404(a)(1).The dissent’s more technical point is that the plaintiffs may have a cause-of-action problem. Congress has “broadly exempted” USPS from Administrative Procedure Act review, and the dissent concluded that exemption applied here. On that view, the plaintiffs would be left with only an equitable ultra vires claim, which requires showing that the agency acted “entirely in excess of the agency’s delegated powers and contrary to a specific prohibition in the statute.” The dissent described that kind of claim as “essentially a Hail Mary pass.”It is unclear, maybe even unlikely, that a majority of the Court will adopt that framework. But at least three justices appear open to it. If the case returns to the Court in a more traditional posture, watch Chief Justice Roberts and Justices Kavanaugh, Gorsuch, and Barrett—especially once the Court no longer has to weigh the potential near-term disruption to election officials and voters that shaped the emergency stay posture. | | | | | | | Alaska The Department of Law against 11 American Samoan residents of Whittier accused of voting illegally, after the Alaska Court of Appeals held that a conviction requires proof the voter intended to deceive election officials.The Division of Elections for the general election, rerouting absentee ballots cast at in-person rural polling stations to its Anchorage office, after 75 such ballots reached the Nome regional office too late to be counted in the August primary.California Governor Gavin Newsom a package of election-related bills that creates new criminal penalties for interfering with ballots, election records, voting technology, and the delivery of vote-by-mail ballots. Justice Brett Kavanaugh argued there’s “at least a fair prospect” that the U.S. Postal Service is not overreaching its power but supported leaving the rule ineffective for 2026 because election officials lacked sufficient time to implement it before the midterms. | | | Christopher Mann, April Tan, and Kira Flemke of the Center for Election Innovation & Research interim findings from a 50-state review of the conditions that trigger inactivation of a voter registration record.The MIT Election Data + Science Lab outlined a proposed for voter list maintenance, emphasizing that states face recurring challenges in keeping rolls accurate because of population mobility, decentralized election administration, privacy constraints, and varied state practices. The piece argues that clearer shared terminology and comparable measures would help administrators, researchers, policymakers, and the public better evaluate list-maintenance systems and distinguish routine registration updating from improper voter removal.Professor Charles Stewart that the available evidence does not support broad claims that mail-ballot transmission problems are systematically disadvantaging one party. Reviewing recent data on mail-ballot return rates and rejected ballots, Stewart notes that while mail voting remains vulnerable to ordinary delivery delays, voter error, and administrative variation, the patterns do not show a clear partisan skew large enough to substantiate claims of a targeted or structurally biased mail-ballot problem. | | | The Grant Institute has potential openings for junior-level attorneys and others interested in the study of election administration and voting issues. subject: I've got something to say about our Navy…
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Elaine Luria for Congress
body:
What we owe the people still standing watch.

---
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139874530/648803716/1363234093?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_260924_FR_Sailors_A0_na_U1_X2_M1&amount=15&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZDJlNDQxNi0zM2I4LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=SpqKEpoETELH9ooj3g2p4fHHaXJA6p7yicJ8QkbUI6M=) Folks, twenty-five years ago, I was a junior officer in the United States Navy. I stood watch plenty of times in twenty years — in the Middle East, the Western Pacific, and the Strait of Hormuz. Sailors stand watch for people they will never meet, in a town they’ve never visited, on a night nobody will remember. They do it on the assumption that somebody, somewhere, is looking out for them too. Right now, I'm not sure we're holding up our end.
* The USS Gerald R. Ford deployed for eleven months, the longest carrier deployment since Vietnam.
* The USS Abraham Lincoln was at sea for roughly nine months and went over 200 days without pulling into port.
* The USS George Washington has been pulled out of the Western Pacific to relieve the Lincoln. That’s _supposed_ to be our naval deterrent against China and North Korea.

Hampton Roads has the largest concentration of Navy families in America. This is more than just a status report. It’s an empty seat at a kitchen table in Virginia Beach. It’s a spouse doing the work of two people since winter. It’s a kid in Norfolk who’s seen their parent on screen rather than in person for most of the year. Those families are standing a watch of their own, and **we’re all paying a price for this sloppy, poorly-planned war.** I’ve been a Sailor, I served on the House Armed Services Committee, and I’m still fighting for our Sailors in every way I can. They defend us, so defending them is a moral obligation. That means someone in Congress actually reading the readiness reports. Asking why our troops are being deployed and when our troops are coming home. Making sure the pay and the housing and the healthcare and the childcare hold while they're gone. Asking the hard questions. **So I’m reporting for duty.** Sailors don't get to opt out of the hard part. Neither will I. A watch only ends when someone shows up to relieve you. Our FEC end-of-quarter deadline is midnight on September 30th, the last full report before Election Day, and everyone watching VA-02 will read it as a verdict on whether we can win this seat back. We're still running short. **[Will you chip in $15 before midnight to help me flip VA-02 and show up for the Sailors and families of Hampton Roads?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139874531/648803717/1363234093?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_260924_FR_Sailors_A0_na_U1_X2_M1&amount=15&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZDJlNDQxNi0zM2I4LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=SpqKEpoETELH9ooj3g2p4fHHaXJA6p7yicJ8QkbUI6M=)** | | | [Contribute](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139874532/648803718/1363234093?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_260924_FR_Sailors_A0_na_U1_X2_M1&amount=15&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZDJlNDQxNi0zM2I4LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=SpqKEpoETELH9ooj3g2p4fHHaXJA6p7yicJ8QkbUI6M=)

Both Sides Walked Out at the UN. Behind the Scenes, Talks Were 'Very Productive.'

A defiant UN speech, a mutual walkout, and a claimed breakthrough in private talks all happened within 24 hours -- while a new oil-supply risk emerged in Libya, far from the Middle East war driving this month's coverage.

|
---

Wednesday delivered a genuinely rare combination: the harshest public exchange of this newsletter's UN coverage, alongside the first confirmed report of substantive private talks. **Verified fact:** Iranian President Pezeshkian told the General Assembly, "the US president called us terrorists but we are the victims of terrorists," and that Iranian resistance "will only grow in the face of sanctions," while U.S. and Israeli delegations walked out during his remarks -- a mirror of Iran's own walkout during Trump's speech a day earlier. Yet Trump separately described U.S.-Iran negotiations as "very productive," and Pezeshkian himself said "Iran extends its hands towards the world." Markets fell broadly -- the S&P 500 down 0.73%, the Nasdaq down 1.11%, the Russell 2000 down 1.60% -- as the 5-year Treasury yield breached 5% intraday for the first time since 2007.

| | Regime Signal 01 -- Public Theater and Private Substance Are Now Visibly Decoupled
---|---

**Our interpretation:** mutual walkouts at the podium alongside a claimed "very productive" back-channel is the clearest evidence yet that this conflict's public rhetoric and its actual negotiating track are running on separate, only loosely connected paths -- a pattern this newsletter also observed in the Trump-Warsh dynamic, where personal rhetoric and substantive policy diverged. **What remains unknown** is which track markets should weight more heavily; Wednesday's broad selloff suggests investors leaned toward the harsher public signal despite the private-talks claim.

| | Regime Signal 02 -- A New, Unrelated Oil Risk Entered From a Different Continent Entirely
---|---

**Verified fact:** an unidentified armed group shut a pipeline valve connecting Libya's Al-Sharara oil field -- the country's largest -- to its Zawiya export terminal, with Libya's National Oil Corporation warning it could be forced to declare force majeure if the disruption continues. **Our interpretation:** this is a genuinely separate supply risk, unconnected to the Middle East war this newsletter has tracked for a month, arriving at the exact moment markets were pricing sustained de-escalation on the Iran front -- a reminder that oil's risk premium has more than one active source right now.

| | Regime Signal 03 -- The Yield Curve Kept Climbing Regardless of Any Diplomatic News
---|---

**Verified fact:** the 5-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since 2007, with new 52-week highs across the 3-, 5-, 7-, 10-, and 20-year maturities. **Our interpretation:** this broad-based, cross-maturity move looks more like a structural repricing of fiscal and rate expectations than a reaction to any single day's headlines -- consistent with this newsletter's earlier finding that the bond market has been running ahead of, not reacting to, the news cycle.

| | Today's Confirmation Point
---|---

Thursday's Trump-Xi summit in Washington, Xi's first White House visit in a decade, with expectations already tempered by analysts predicting "little movement on trade, less on Taiwan." Watch whether any concrete outcome beats those lowered expectations.

I about threw my phone across the room last night.
An ad came on that, at first glance, looked like a yet another absurd campaign ad for Donald Trump. It accused every Democrat in America of being a communist, a Marxist, a socialist. It promised America will never become a communist country. It praised Trump's second-term agenda: his tax cuts, and how we're apparently bringing manufacturing jobs back, which isn't even remotely true. It was weird, but it was more or less exactly the kind of bullshit political ad we've all seen a thousand times. Then came the kicker: It wasn't a campaign ad at all. It was paid for by the United States government.
Paid for by _you_. Paid for by _me_. They used _our_ tax dollars to pay for it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/86387c45-b11c-4f3d-b1bb-c966caf84377?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I am filled with rage at the way these people waste our money on garbage like this. Think about it for a second. The average American can barely afford to fill up their gas tank right now. They're kicking people off their health care en masse. Rural hospitals are closing. People are giving up on the American dream - the basic promise that if you work hard and do everything you're supposed to do, you should be able to afford a home, to retire with some dignity, to raise a family, and build a life that feels a little more secure than the one you started with. And meanwhile, Donald Trump is stealing billions and billions of dollars from the American people and spending your money to prop up his own political party - or, really, himself - in the midterms, to build his stupid ballroom, to bankroll his stupid golf trips, to fund a slush fund to bail out January 6 insurrectionists.
We've never seen anything like this. It is a staggeringly disgusting abuse of taxpayer money. As far as I'm concerned, lock them all up and throw away the key.
But here's the thing. When the rage finally subsided, a new sensation took its place. I started to think about what I had just watched. And underneath all that anger, I noticed something else. I could smell their fear. I could smell their desperation.
Think about what it takes to get to this point. Trump and the Republican Party are already spending hundreds of millions in campaign funds, money they've taken from corrupt billionaires like Elon Musk, trying desperately to save Ken Paxton in Texas, Roger Marshall in Kansas, and candidates in all the other stretch states where Democrats are seriously competing right now. These are places where I think we have a real opportunity to elect Democrats at the federal level for the first time in a very long time. And on top of all that, they're now running taxpayer-funded ads on Fox News. That's the part I can't shake. You don't do that when you feel good about where you stand. You do that when you are truly, spectacularly desperate.
Maybe it'll work. I doubt it, but maybe.
I think the American people are onto their shit. More than that, I think they're exhausted by it. People are tired of the standard Republican move of calling anybody who disagrees with them a communist or a traitor. They're tired of MAGA talking heads on cable news attacking trans kids. They're tired of hearing about Hasan Piker. They're tired of this whole era of our politics. I know I am. It's been crass and disgusting and exceedingly stupid. But underneath all of that stupidity and outrage, something much darker has happened: It has robbed so many people of their fundamental dignity.
* * *

Just $8/month makes a huge difference:](https://substack.com/redirect/0afa58fc-7eea-41cc-955a-5d5ea77ff181?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

* * *
It's taken so much from us. How many families have been shattered by the way we've done politics over the last ten years? How many lives have been ruined by the callous, careless decisions Donald Trump made in his first term and is making again in his second? How many people are barely scraping by? How many have given up on the American dream, gone cold, and stopped showing up for their communities? How much of ourselves have we surrendered to being angry all the damn time?
This can't go on. I don't want to live this way anymore. I don't think any of us do.
Now we're seeing polling that shows Trump's approval rating under 30 percent, the first time we've ever seen that. He's more unpopular now than he was after the insurrection on January 6th. That's depressing to say out loud, but it's heartening in its own right. People know. People are tired. People are over this.
And yes, 25 percent of this country is never going to abandon their king. I understand that. And I love them just as much as I love any of my other fellow countrymen, even if they're lost in the MAGA whirlpool. I don't want to spend the rest my life resenting my neighbors. Because if I do, they win.
It's time to turn the page. Hell, it's time to close the book, toss it in the incinerator, and write a new American chapter. I know that sounds cheesy. It's the first thing that came to mind when I sat down to write this, and I'm not one for revising away my own naivete. I still believe that we are capable of something better than _this_. Sue me.
The next month is going to be challenging on every level. They're going to try to stretch us thin. They're going to abuse their power. They're going to meddle in the midterms. They're going to lie, cheat, and steal.
And they are going to fail.
They're going to fail because of the wave coming for them. We built that wave together, in lockstep with our brothers and sisters and friends all across this country, in solidarity with one another, to build a better America. It's too big for them to rig. It's simply too big. I don't believe there's anything they can do to stop the freight train that's headed their way.
But there's still a lot of work to do.
And that means we can't just sit around being pissed off. I wrote last week about the fear I've been carrying into this election and about something I've had to learn the hard way: fear is energy. If you sit with it long enough, scrolling for hours, imagining everything that could go wrong, it doesn't protect you or prepare you. It just eats you alive. But give that energy somewhere to go - into the work, into organizing, into preparing for the thing you're afraid of - and suddenly fear becomes useful.
I think rage works the same way. It needs somewhere to go.
A little bit of mine went into this piece. The next bit is going into my YouTube videos and into the work I do with my clients. And yes, some of it is going into taking my son to the Cubs' last home game this afternoon. Sometimes your best act of resistance is just being a good dad for an afternoon. Being present. Loving your family. Remembering that there is an entire world outside the glowing rectangle in your hand. These people already take enough from us. I'm not giving them an afternoon with my son, too.
So take that rage, or whatever it is you're feeling, give it somewhere to go. Make it useful. Don't let these pricks get away with the theft, the corruption, and the depravity they've put on display over the last two years.
Send them a message. Let's elect a Democratic House. Let's elect a Democratic Senate. Let's win a whole lot of governor's races. And then let's show people what a functioning government that actually works and fights for them looks like.
We're going to keep fighting to build a better Democratic Party, too. That fight doesn't end on Election Day. It's only beginning. But right now, we have a major opportunity to deliver a blow to Trump's MAGA movement and show them that there are consequences for what they have done.
Let's fucking go.
With urgency,
-Mike

We believe the majority in the Senate and Congress will be dangerously narrow. The media is doing everything in their power to sabotage America First candidates up and down the ballot. Turning Point PAC is funding over 600 ballot chasers in critical battleground states... But we are afraid this may not be enough to secure a conservative majority in Congress. The Radical Left's fake news machine and their fear-mongering threaten to hand Democrats control of the House and Senate in 2026. We are optimistic over here and have chosen to ultimately release control of this to God. However, we have also decided to campaign as if we are 10+ POINTS DOWN and work endlessly until we've secured a conservative majority in both chambers. But we must admit... #
Peter,
There’s no point wasting your time here, so we’ll be direct.
Things aren’t looking good right now.
We’ve got a long way to go to meet our goals, and with an official FEC deadline on September 30th, the timing couldn’t be worse.
The goals VoteVets sets aren’t arbitrary numbers. They are what we need to raise to accomplish our goals this year: elevating Veteran candidates, winning independent and undecided voters in states we can’t afford to lose, and retaking the House and Senate this November.
Democrats are getting pummeled, relentlessly, day-in and day-out. Republicans have virtually no limit to the amount of money they can spend to defend their majorities, and they’ll use every trick in the book to do it. They’ve been stacking the deck with gerrymandering for decades — an insurance policy for years exactly like this one.
That’s why this FEC deadline — and what we raise before it hits — is so important. We have to be able to match their spending, if not dollar for dollar, then with candidates and ads that punch above their weight. We have to compete everywhere we can, or we’re going to come up short.
So, please. If you can afford to make a donation, and you’ve been waiting for the right time to do it:

subject: Senator Alsobrooks Newsletter -- September 24, 2026
body:
|

---
Dear Friends and Neighbors, 13 times, I have voted to end this war. 13 times, I have voted to bring our servicemembers home, stop spending billions of taxpayer dollars on a war without a clear end, and refocus our attention on the challenges facing American families here at home. But this President has refused to change course. Now, American families are paying the price. Diesel prices have climbed to record levels, driving up the cost of moving the food we eat, the products we buy, and nearly everything else Americans depend on. Families who were already struggling with the cost of groceries, housing, health care, and other everyday necessities are being squeezed even harder. This President promised to lower costs. Instead, this war has compounded the economic pressures families are already facing. What began as a distraction from this Administration's failed policies at home has become a costly war with no clear end, and American families are being left to shoulder the financial consequences. Meanwhile, as this Administration remains consumed by a war overseas, we are facing serious challenges right here at home. Measles--a disease that was declared eliminated in the United States more than 25 years ago--is surging again. More than 3,200 cases have been confirmed nationwide this year. Here in Maryland, we now have outbreaks among unvaccinated individuals in Carroll, Cecil, and St. Mary's counties. Maryland has already reported 41 cases this year, compared with just three cases in all of 2025. These are the challenges that demand the attention of our federal government: protecting the health of our children and our communities, lowering costs for working families, strengthening our economy, and making sure Americans can afford their groceries, their health care, and the gas they need to get to work. Instead, this President and his enablers in Congress have embroiled our country in a costly war with no clear end or purpose, while American families are being squeezed from every direction. I have voted 13 times to end this war, and I will continue fighting to bring our servicemembers home, lower costs, protect the health and safety of our communities, and put the needs of Maryland families first. **Fighting Through Legislation **
It has been a busy couple of weeks here on Capitol Hill, and I continue to fight for legislation that will help Maryland families thrive. I have worked on legislation from helping seniors age in place to providing greater support for family caregivers to addressing maternal health outcomes.

These are the bills I have introduced:

Senior Accessible Housing Tax Credit Act of 2026: This bill would create a nonrefundable tax credit for taxpayers aged 60 or older for expenses related to certain residence modifications on their principal residence or a qualifying second home. The credit would be equal to the cost of eligible expenditures, with an annual credit limitation of $10,000. Qualifying expenditures would also include certain labor costs related to the preparation, assembly, or installation of an eligible modification. Back-to-School Summer Tariff Exemption Bill: This bill would exempt school supplies and educational materials from most tariffs, including the latest Section 301 tariffs raising prices on goods from much of the global economy. The legislation directs the Secretaries of Commerce and Education to work together to create a list of tariff-free school supplies.

These are the bills I cosponsored: End Trump's Tariff Tax Act: This bill would revoke and refund President Trump's newest tariffs and rein in the President's tariff authority by repealing the authorities he has used to continue his trade war. This legislation would apply to Trump's newest global tariffs of 10-12.5 percent and the 50 percent tariff on $20 billion worth of imports from Canada. Venezuela Oil Proceeds Transparency Act: This legislation would direct the Comptroller General of the nonpartisan Government Accountability Office (GAO) to conduct an independent audit of the Trump Administration's financial arrangement using offshore accounts for Venezuelan oil revenue. Lainie Jones Comprehensive Cancer Survivorship Act: This legislation would strengthen survivorship care by improving care coordination, expanding supportive services, advancing research, and addressing the long-term needs of people living with and beyond cancer. American Battlefield Protection Program Amendments Act of 2025: This legislation would reauthorize the American Battlefield Protection Program (ABPP) through 2035 at $20 million per year and increase federal support for nonprofit preservation efforts by increasing the federal cost-share from 50 percent to 75 percent.
Ending Presidential Corruption in Banking Act: This bill would ensure that no President, Vice President, their immediate families, or other senior government officials can exploit their positions to own or control a bank, which could serve as a vehicle for corrupt dealings. Strengthening Coast Guard Communities Act of 2026: This bipartisan bill would allow the U.S. Coast Guard to collaborate with state and local governments through intergovernmental support agreements (IGSAs). HCBS Access Act: This legislation would make home- and community-based care a mandatory Medicaid benefit, gradually eliminate waiting lists for services, strengthen the home- and community-based care workforce, and provide greater support for family caregivers. Fit to Serve Act: This bill would support military readiness and national security by prohibiting discrimination against transgender service members.
Insider Trading Prohibition Act: This bill would create a new federal ban on insider trading under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. It would make it illegal for a person to buy, sell, or otherwise trade certain financial instruments when they have material, nonpublic information and know, or deliberately avoid knowing, that the information is confidential and obtained or used wrongfully. Fairness for Farm Workers Act: This legislation aims to create a level playing field for farmers and consumers by weakening the hold consolidated interests have on the agricultural economy. The bill would require major food companies to provide decent wages and safe working conditions to do business with the federal government. Honoring the Sacrifice of Troops in War Act of 2026: This legislation would prohibit the Secretary of Defense from manipulating casualty records and jeopardizing benefits for military families. The bill would ensure accurate public statistics on casualties, prohibit unjustified recategorization of designated contingency operations, prevent the manipulation of casualty records, restore casualty records of fallen and wounded service members in the Iran War, prohibit cuts to benefits for troops and civilian personnel, and restore benefits to personnel supporting the Iran War. Momnibus Act: This legislation is a comprehensive package designed to address the nation's maternal health crisis and disparities in maternal health outcomes, including those affecting Black mothers. The Momnibus Act is composed of 14 bills. Human-Wildlife Conflict Reduction Act of 2026: This legislation would codify a pilot program at the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and expand the Department's development of nonlethal methods, such as range riding, guard dogs, and electric fencing, to reduce human-wildlife conflicts across the American outdoors. RECOVER PII Act: This legislation would provide lifetime identity protection coverage to federal employees whose personal information was compromised in the 2015 Office of Personnel Management (OPM) cyberattacks. This bill would also reimburse affected federal employees and contractors for privacy software and other eligible tools used to reduce their personal information online. Lori Jackson-Nicolette Elias Domestic Violence Survivor Protection Act: This legislation would restrict those under temporary restraining orders from purchasing or possessing a firearm and extend protections to domestic violence survivors who have been abused by dating partners. Comprehensive Paid Leave for Federal Employees Act: This legislation would expand federal paid leave to include 12 weeks of family and medical leave. Therapeutic Fraud Prevention Act: This legislation would ban "conversion therapy," a practice claiming to change an individual's sexual orientation or gender identity. The practice has been opposed by major professional organizations in health, education, social work, and counseling. A bill to amend title 10, United States Code, and the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1994, to codify and clarify gender-neutral standards for members of certain Armed Forces, and for other purposes

A resolution expressing support for the designation of the week of September 19 through September 26, 2026, as "National Estuaries Week". Agreed to in the Senate. A resolution designating the week of August 22 through August 30, 2026, as "National Park Week". Agreed to in the Senate. A resolution celebrating the 35th anniversary of the independence of Ukraine from the former Soviet Union. A concurrent resolution expressing the sense of Congress that tax-exempt fraternal benefit societies have historically provided and continue to provide critical benefits to the people and communities of the United States. **In the Community **
Housing affordability is a challenge facing Marylanders in every corner of our state. In Garrett County, I met with local leaders at the Garrett County Community Action Committee to discuss how we can work together to sustain and expand affordable, accessible housing and help families thrive. I also had the opportunity to spend time with seniors in Garrett County. Marylanders deserve access to affordable housing, groceries, and health care--and the security they've worked a lifetime to earn. I'll keep fighting in the Senate to protect Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, and our civil liberties.

At Mountain Laurel Medical Center, I saw firsthand the vital care they provide to rural Marylanders. I'll keep fighting to protect Federally Qualified Health Centers and the Appalachian Regional Commission, which has supported Mountain Laurel Medical Center and communities across Mountain Maryland. Every Marylander deserves access to quality health care, no matter where they live.

In Hagerstown, I met with Mayor Bill McIntire, Councilwomen Anderson and Bell, and city leaders to discuss the priorities and opportunities facing the Hub City. From infrastructure and transportation to housing and economic development, I'll continue working to bring federal resources home and help Hagerstown thrive.

Thank you to President Quindella Fletcher and the Ladies of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority Incorporated®, Upsilon Tau Omega Chapter for a wonderful Crab Feast! For over 20 years, Southern Prince George's County Community Charities in conjunction with the chapter have poured into our community through scholarships, food, and service. This summer, I welcomed Senator Craig Zucker and the Maryland Democratic Senate Caucus Fellows to the Capitol. I enjoyed hearing about their conversations with Marylanders and what they learned about the issues that matter most to communities across our state. I was glad to meet with Liberian President Joseph Boakai to discuss the longstanding ties between Maryland and Liberia and opportunities to strengthen our partnership through trade, health care, education, and economic development. **Grant Spotlight **

I wanted to remind you of a few grant opportunities for nonprofits, public, and private institutions that will go a long way to help Maryland families. [**AmeriCorps - Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 AmeriCorps Seniors RSVP Competition Synopsis 8**](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15348.20213594.6402431.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.grants.gov%2fsearch-results-detail%2f363482&redir_log=413718875902340) is an opportunity for communities to apply for funding to engage adults ages 55 and older in tackling the community's most pressing needs through the AmeriCorps Seniors RSVP program. This is an open competition across all states and territories. (Posted August 20, 2026 - October 20, 2026 deadline)

[**AmeriCorps Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 AmeriCorps State and National Competitive Grants Synopsis 4**](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15348.20213594.6402431.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.grants.gov%2fsearch-results-detail%2f363696&redir_log=930344790435340) grants are awarded to eligible organizations that engage AmeriCorps members in evidence-based or evidence-informed interventions to strengthen communities. An AmeriCorps member is a person who does community service through AmeriCorps. Members may receive a living allowance and other benefits. After successful completion of their service, members earn a Segal AmeriCorps Education Award they can use to pay for higher education expenses or apply to qualified student loans. (Posted August 28, 2026 -January 13, 2027 deadline)

**[Institute of Museum and Library Services - Inspire Grants for Small Museums (2027)](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15348.20213594.6402431.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.grants.gov%2fsearch-results-detail%2f363771&redir_log=481277016698340)** is a special initiative of the Museums for America grant program designed to support small museums of all disciplines, including small rural or small remote institutions and small museums that have not previously received federal funding. The program funds project-based efforts to serve the public through educational programs and exhibits, community partnerships, and collections stewardship activities. (Posted September 1, 2026 - November 13, 2026 deadline)

[**Institute of Museum and Library Services - Museums for America (2027)**](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15348.20213594.6402431.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.grants.gov%2fsearch-results-detail%2f363768&redir_log=931811362514340) invests in museums of all sizes - from small to large - and disciplines in project-based efforts to serve the public through educational programs and exhibits, community partnerships, and collections stewardship activities. (Posted September 1, 2026 - November 13, 2026 deadline)

[**Institute of Museum and Library Services - National Leadership Grants for Libraries (2027)**](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15348.20213594.6402431.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.grants.gov%2fsearch-results-detail%2f363766&redir_log=782188500109340) program supports projects that: promote adult reading, and health and financial literacies; focus on programming and archival practices related to our shared American history; manage and preserve the national information infrastructure; serve the public's information and education needs; enhance library and information services through effective and efficient use of new and emerging technologies; improve community prosperity; provide emergency services to communities during disasters and emergencies; and build collaborative partnerships between libraries, archives, and museums that benefit the communities they serve. (Posted September 1, 2026 - November 13, 2026 deadline)

**[Department of Health and Human Services - Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health Title X Family Planning Services Grants Synopsis 2](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15348.20213594.6402431.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.grants.gov%2fsearch-results-detail%2f361754&redir_log=418125250289340)** is implemented through competitively awarded grants to a diverse network of public and private nonprofit entities. The program helps millions of low-income and uninsured Americans develop health literacy and access family planning and related health services, empowering individuals and families to make informed decisions and navigate chronic health conditions and pregnancy with confidence. clean_body: | Dear Friends and Neighbors, 13 times, I have voted to end this war. 13 times, I have voted to bring our servicemembers home, stop spending billions of taxpayer dollars on a war without a clear end, and refocus our attention on the challenges facing American families here at home. But this President has refused to change course. Now, American families are paying the price. Diesel prices have climbed to record levels, driving up the cost of moving the food we eat, the products we buy, and nearly everything else Americans depend on. Families who were already struggling with the cost of groceries, housing, health care, and other everyday necessities are being squeezed even harder. This President promised to lower costs. Instead, this war has compounded the economic pressures families are already facing. What began as a distraction from this Administration's failed policies at home has become a costly war with no clear end, and American families are being left to shoulder the financial consequences. Meanwhile, as this Administration remains consumed by a war overseas, we are facing serious challenges right here at home. Measles--a disease that was declared eliminated in the United States more than 25 years ago--is surging again. More than 3,200 cases have been confirmed nationwide this year. Here in Maryland, we now have outbreaks among unvaccinated individuals in Carroll, Cecil, and St. Mary's counties. Maryland has already reported 41 cases this year, compared with just three cases in all of 2025. These are the challenges that demand the attention of our federal government: protecting the health of our children and our communities, lowering costs for working families, strengthening our economy, and making sure Americans can afford their groceries, their health care, and the gas they need to get to work. Instead, this President and his enablers in Congress have embroiled our country in a costly war with no clear end or purpose, while American families are being squeezed from every direction. I have voted 13 times to end this war, and I will continue fighting to bring our servicemembers home, lower costs, protect the health and safety of our communities, and put the needs of Maryland families first. Fighting Through Legislation It has been a busy couple of weeks here on Capitol Hill, and I continue to fight for legislation that will help Maryland families thrive. I have worked on legislation from helping seniors age in place to providing greater support for family caregivers to addressing maternal health outcomes. These are the bills I have introduced: Senior Accessible Housing Tax Credit Act of 2026: This bill would create a nonrefundable tax credit for taxpayers aged 60 or older for expenses related to certain residence modifications on their principal residence or a qualifying second home. The credit would be equal to the cost of eligible expenditures, with an annual credit limitation of $10,000. Qualifying expenditures would also include certain labor costs related to the preparation, assembly, or installation of an eligible modification. Back-to-School Summer Tariff Exemption Bill: This bill would exempt school supplies and educational materials from most tariffs, including the latest Section 301 tariffs raising prices on goods from much of the global economy. The legislation directs the Secretaries of Commerce and Education to work together to create a list of tariff-free school supplies. These are the bills I cosponsored: End Trump's Tariff Tax Act: This bill would revoke and refund President Trump's newest tariffs and rein in the President's tariff authority by repealing the authorities he has used to continue his trade war. This legislation would apply to Trump's newest global tariffs of 10-12.5 percent and the 50 percent tariff on $20 billion worth of imports from Canada. Venezuela Oil Proceeds Transparency Act: This legislation would direct the Comptroller General of the nonpartisan Government Accountability Office (GAO) to conduct an independent audit of the Trump Administration's financial arrangement using offshore accounts for Venezuelan oil revenue. Lainie Jones Comprehensive Cancer Survivorship Act: This legislation would strengthen survivorship care by improving care coordination, expanding supportive services, advancing research, and addressing the long-term needs of people living with and beyond cancer. American Battlefield Protection Program Amendments Act of 2025: This legislation would reauthorize the American Battlefield Protection Program (ABPP) through 2035 at $20 million per year and increase federal support for nonprofit preservation efforts by increasing the federal cost-share from 50 percent to 75 percent. Ending Presidential Corruption in Banking Act: This bill would ensure that no President, Vice President, their immediate families, or other senior government officials can exploit their positions to own or control a bank, which could serve as a vehicle for corrupt dealings. Strengthening Coast Guard Communities Act of 2026: This bipartisan bill would allow the U.S. Coast Guard to collaborate with state and local governments through intergovernmental support agreements (IGSAs). HCBS Access Act: This legislation would make home- and community-based care a mandatory Medicaid benefit, gradually eliminate waiting lists for services, strengthen the home- and community-based care workforce, and provide greater support for family caregivers. Fit to Serve Act: This bill would support military readiness and national security by prohibiting discrimination against transgender service members. Insider Trading Prohibition Act: This bill would create a new federal ban on insider trading under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. It would make it illegal for a person to buy, sell, or otherwise trade certain financial instruments when they have material, nonpublic information and know, or deliberately avoid knowing, that the information is confidential and obtained or used wrongfully. Fairness for Farm Workers Act: This legislation aims to create a level playing field for farmers and consumers by weakening the hold consolidated interests have on the agricultural economy. The bill would require major food companies to provide decent wages and safe working conditions to do business with the federal government. Honoring the Sacrifice of Troops in War Act of 2026: This legislation would prohibit the Secretary of Defense from manipulating casualty records and jeopardizing benefits for military families. The bill would ensure accurate public statistics on casualties, prohibit unjustified recategorization of designated contingency operations, prevent the manipulation of casualty records, restore casualty records of fallen and wounded service members in the Iran War, prohibit cuts to benefits for troops and civilian personnel, and restore benefits to personnel supporting the Iran War. Momnibus Act: This legislation is a comprehensive package designed to address the nation's maternal health crisis and disparities in maternal health outcomes, including those affecting Black mothers. The Momnibus Act is composed of 14 bills. Human-Wildlife Conflict Reduction Act of 2026: This legislation would codify a pilot program at the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and expand the Department's development of nonlethal methods, such as range riding, guard dogs, and electric fencing, to reduce human-wildlife conflicts across the American outdoors. RECOVER PII Act: This legislation would provide lifetime identity protection coverage to federal employees whose personal information was compromised in the 2015 Office of Personnel Management (OPM) cyberattacks. This bill would also reimburse affected federal employees and contractors for privacy software and other eligible tools used to reduce their personal information online. Lori Jackson-Nicolette Elias Domestic Violence Survivor Protection Act: This legislation would restrict those under temporary restraining orders from purchasing or possessing a firearm and extend protections to domestic violence survivors who have been abused by dating partners. Comprehensive Paid Leave for Federal Employees Act: This legislation would expand federal paid leave to include 12 weeks of family and medical leave. Therapeutic Fraud Prevention Act: This legislation would ban "conversion therapy," a practice claiming to change an individual's sexual orientation or gender identity. The practice has been opposed by major professional organizations in health, education, social work, and counseling. A bill to amend title 10, United States Code, and the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1994, to codify and clarify gender-neutral standards for members of certain Armed Forces, and for other purposes A resolution expressing support for the designation of the week of September 19 through September 26, 2026, as "National Estuaries Week". Agreed to in the Senate. A resolution designating the week of August 22 through August 30, 2026, as "National Park Week". Agreed to in the Senate. A resolution celebrating the 35th anniversary of the independence of Ukraine from the former Soviet Union. A concurrent resolution expressing the sense of Congress that tax-exempt fraternal benefit societies have historically provided and continue to provide critical benefits to the people and communities of the United States. In the Community Housing affordability is a challenge facing Marylanders in every corner of our state. In Garrett County, I met with local leaders at the Garrett County Community Action Committee to discuss how we can work together to sustain and expand affordable, accessible housing and help families thrive. I also had the opportunity to spend time with seniors in Garrett County. Marylanders deserve access to affordable housing, groceries, and health care--and the security they've worked a lifetime to earn. I'll keep fighting in the Senate to protect Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, and our civil liberties. At Mountain Laurel Medical Center, I saw firsthand the vital care they provide to rural Marylanders. I'll keep fighting to protect Federally Qualified Health Centers and the Appalachian Regional Commission, which has supported Mountain Laurel Medical Center and communities across Mountain Maryland. Every Marylander deserves access to quality health care, no matter where they live. In Hagerstown, I met with Mayor Bill McIntire, Councilwomen Anderson and Bell, and city leaders to discuss the priorities and opportunities facing the Hub City. From infrastructure and transportation to housing and economic development, I'll continue working to bring federal resources home and help Hagerstown thrive. Thank you to President Quindella Fletcher and the Ladies of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority Incorporated®, Upsilon Tau Omega Chapter for a wonderful Crab Feast! # THE AARON DAY SHOW
Defending Free Will in the Age of Technocracy
S3E24 • Sep 24
## We're Costing the GOP the US Senate.
[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/cOHfPdCkoU0?e=938a87a89b&c2id=c1b996ddd6cdaaf4cddb384f099ac837)
Aaron here.
In 2016, a New Hampshire Senate seat was decided by 1,017 votes. I took 17,742, running as an independent. For the first time since 1854, New Hampshire sent no Republican to Congress. It hasn't sent one since.
Today StarkFreedom named the five races that complete our slate: Texas, Kansas, Michigan, Ohio, and Iowa. Combined with New Hampshire, that's six U.S. Senate races where a third-party candidate can take more votes than the margin between the two major parties.
StarkFreedom is organizing to deploy up to $2.5 million in independent expenditures across all six, for the candidate it endorses and against the Republican in each.
Kansas: Roger Marshall's Kalshi price dropped from 84 cents to 77 after the New York Times reported he sued 700 patients over medical debt through his former practice. Iowa: Ashley Hinson still hasn't taken a position on the pipeline bill that passed 85-10 in the House and 27-22 in the Senate before Governor Reynolds vetoed it. Michigan: Mike Rogers is down seven points, two years after losing his last Senate race by three tenths of a point. Ohio: nearly a quarter of Ohio Republicans disapprove of Trump, and Libertarian Bill Redpath is already pulling from Republicans and independents. Texas: Ted Brown set a state Libertarian record in 2024, and he's polling at 3 percent in a race where the top two are separated by one point.
We are costing the GOP the US Senate. I'm laying out the full strategy live tonight at 6 PM ET.

# On the Blog: The Rising Cost of Having a Place to Call Home
---
Parents shouldn't have to choose between going to work and making sure their children are well cared for.
For too many South Dakota families, finding affordable, reliable child care is a daily challenge.
The cost is significant. South Dakota's own cost-of-care analysis estimates that full-time care at a child care center costs between $14,000 and $16,000 a year for infants and toddlers, and between $9,000 and $12,000 for preschool-aged children, depending on location.
For South Dakota’s working families, this can be simply unaffordable. In some communities, families struggle simply to find an available spot for their kids. This could mean they may have to reduce their hours, turn down a job, leave the workforce, or make other difficult choices.
This isn't just a family issue. It's an economic issue.
