### Today, LGBTQ veterans are helping lead the country they once had to serve in silence

Fifteen years ago this month, I helped repeal "Don't Ask, Don't Tell." But before I led the fight to overturn it, there was a time when I blindly supported it. As a young Army cadet, I accepted the argument that allowing gay and lesbian troops to serve openly could undermine cohesion and readiness. Like [many Americans at the time](https://substack.com/redirect/b629489d-b732-4f7c-8394-ed89106080bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), I initially thought it made sense. That began to change while I was a student at King's College, when an administrator challenged me for the first time to think about gay rights as part of the broader American struggle for civil rights. I wasn't convinced on the spot, but his argument stayed with me.
The more time I spent in uniform, the harder it became to square the policy with the people I actually served beside. Over time, I came to understand how destructive the policy was. Gay service members that I served shoulder-to-shoulder with did everything their country asked of them and still had their careers ended simply because of who they were. Some lost years of service, professional opportunities and, depending on the circumstances of their discharge, access to benefits they had earned honorably. Meanwhile, our military was losing capable people it had invested in training. Eventually, I came to see that this was not only unfair to the people being forced out; it was bad for the military as well.
By the time I entered Congress, I was determined to help repeal it.
[| | | | | Patrick J Murphy
---
@PatrickMurphyPA
Fighting to repeal the discriminatory "Don't Ask Don't Tell" policy is one of the proudest moments of my Congressional career. We guaranteed that everyone who loves their country and wants to serve has the chance to do so. Signed on this day 11 years ago by @BarackObama .
| 1:34 AM * Sep 21, 2022175 Replies * 41 Reposts * 197 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/8948eea8-5c0a-46c6-9071-296b5bdf44a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
As I said on the [House floor](https://substack.com/redirect/bdfa93f7-79ed-4a61-9a64-cec0754bd8ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2010, "Already dozens of other nations allow their troops to serve openly, including our greatest military allies, Great Britain and Israel, with no detrimental impact on their unit's cohesion. It's an insult to the troops I serve with, and to all our service members fighting in Iraq and Afghanistan, to say that they are somehow less professional or less mission-capable than the members of these foreign militaries."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/7cc00ea9-e4d2-4a39-8497-de0341b71148?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Much of the debate at the time centered on whether the military could absorb the change without sacrificing readiness or discipline. In the end, gay and lesbian Americans were able to serve openly without the disruption critics had predicted.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/5402f044-feae-427e-a8aa-2f345d6573df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Fifteen years later, some of the most important consequences of repeal can be seen outside the military. A generation of LGBTQ veterans has carried that service into public life as elected officials, advocates, community leaders and neighbors. They no longer have to choose between being known as veterans and being known fully as themselves.
Earlier this month, Alaska state Rep. Andrew Gray, an Army veteran, stood before the Anchorage Assembly and asked the city to recognize Sept. 20 as [LGBTQ Veterans Day](https://substack.com/redirect/afdb9014-e699-4333-81c8-34d89c84c7a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
His former commander, Mike Grunst, followed him to the microphone. A 35-year veteran who had served in combat, Grunst called troops who served while hiding who they were "the bravest I have ever served with."
One of the false assumptions behind "Don't Ask, Don't Tell" was that being openly gay somehow made it harder to be fully accepted as a soldier. Fifteen years later, a scene like this almost feels wonderfully ordinary. Gray could stand there as a gay man, a veteran and an elected official, with the commander who once led him standing beside him. None of those identities diminished the others. They were simply all part of who he was understood through shared service.
Fifteen years after repeal, its legacy is showing up across the country. Kansas is recognizing LGBTQ Veterans Day for the first time this year, while New York and Virginia are pursuing broader efforts focused on LGBTQ veterans. Veterans who once served under "Don't Ask, Don't Tell" are now serving in public office, leading organizations and advocating in their communities.
The choice to establish it on Sept. 20 is a deliberate and symbolic way to honor the day the bill was repealed in 2011.
The repeal was a landmark victory for gay and lesbian Americans, but it was also a victory for the military and the country. We gained more veterans we could be proud of. That is patriotism and American pride at its best.
The enduring legacy of "Don't Ask, Don't Tell" repeal isn't just about who was finally allowed to serve openly, but in what those Americans are now able to build after coming home.
_Lucas F. Schleusener is the CEO and co-founder of Out in National Security, a professional and advocacy organization for LGBTQ national security professionals. His work focuses on national security, public policy, and expanding opportunities for LGBTQ Americans in public service._

Annual paid subscribers will receive a digital copy of my 2008 memoir, . * Today, LGBTQ veterans are helping lead the country they once had to serve in silence | | and | Sep 24 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | Fifteen years ago this month, I helped repeal "Don't Ask, Don't Tell." But before I led the fight to overturn it, there was a time when I blindly supported it. As a young Army cadet, I accepted the argument that allowing gay and lesbian troops to serve openly could undermine cohesion and readiness. Like , I initially thought it made sense. That began to change while I was a student at King's College, when an administrator challenged me for the first time to think about gay rights as part of the broader American struggle for civil rights. I wasn't convinced on the spot, but his argument stayed with me. The more time I spent in uniform, the harder it became to square the policy with the people I actually served beside. Over time, I came to understand how destructive the policy was. Gay service members that I served shoulder-to-shoulder with did everything their country asked of them and still had their careers ended simply because of who they were. Some lost years of service, professional opportunities and, depending on the circumstances of their discharge, access to benefits they had earned honorably. Meanwhile, our military was losing capable people it had invested in training. Eventually, I came to see that this was not only unfair to the people being forced out; it was bad for the military as well. By the time I entered Congress, I was determined to help repeal it. As I said on the in 2010, "Already dozens of other nations allow their troops to serve openly, including our greatest military allies, Great Britain and Israel, with no detrimental impact on their unit's cohesion. It's an insult to the troops I serve with, and to all our service members fighting in Iraq and Afghanistan, to say that they are somehow less professional or less mission-capable than the members of these foreign militaries." Much of the debate at the time centered on whether the military could absorb the change without sacrificing readiness or discipline. In the end, gay and lesbian Americans were able to serve openly without the disruption critics had predicted. Fifteen years later, some of the most important consequences of repeal can be seen outside the military. A generation of LGBTQ veterans has carried that service into public life as elected officials, advocates, community leaders and neighbors. They no longer have to choose between being known as veterans and being known fully as themselves. Earlier this month, Alaska state Rep. Andrew Gray, an Army veteran, stood before the Anchorage Assembly and asked the city to recognize Sept. 20 as . His former commander, Mike Grunst, followed him to the microphone. A 35-year veteran who had served in combat, Grunst called troops who served while hiding who they were "the bravest I have ever served with." One of the false assumptions behind "Don't Ask, Don't Tell" was that being openly gay somehow made it harder to be fully accepted as a soldier. Fifteen years later, a scene like this almost feels wonderfully ordinary. Gray could stand there as a gay man, a veteran and an elected official, with the commander who once led him standing beside him. None of those identities diminished the others. They were simply all part of who he was understood through shared service. Fifteen years after repeal, its legacy is showing up across the country. Kansas is recognizing LGBTQ Veterans Day for the first time this year, while New York and Virginia are pursuing broader efforts focused on LGBTQ veterans. Veterans who once served under "Don't Ask, Don't Tell" are now serving in public office, leading organizations and advocating in their communities. The choice to establish it on Sept. 20 is a deliberate and symbolic way to honor the day the bill was repealed in 2011. The repeal was a landmark victory for gay and lesbian Americans, but it was also a victory for the military and the country. We gained more veterans we could be proud of. That is patriotism and American pride at its best. The enduring legacy of "Don't Ask, Don't Tell" repeal isn't just about who was finally allowed to serve openly, but in what those Americans are now able to build after coming home. Lucas F. Schleusener is the CEO and co-founder of Out in National Security, a professional and advocacy organization for LGBTQ national security professionals. I have some exciting news. As many of you know, I am passionate about our country, and over the last several years I have worked with many different groups (Principles First, Republicans, Democrats, and now the Forward Party) to make it a better place. Today I am announcing that I am joining Project No Cap as part of their board. Project No Cap is an organized movement to repeal the Permanent Apportionment Act of 1929. The original design of the House was to grow with the population, but since 1929, the number of representatives has been limited to 435. Since then, the population has tripled. A representative in 1929 represented about 220,000 people; today, a representative represents nearly 800,000 people. This structural flaw has concentrated power in the executive and separated the people from those designed to represent them.
I have worked in construction for nearly my entire adult life, spending time speaking with everyday Americans in their driveways and garages about the issues that matter most to them. One constant theme in those conversations is that they don't feel anyone represents their values of hard work and responsibility. They look at Washington and feel disconnected from those who lead us. They want leaders who take their responsibilities seriously, listen to the concerns of their constituents, and solve the problems we face today. That's why I joined No Cap; it's an organization focused on responsibility, not power. Those Americans I speak with are intelligent and thoughtful people who deserve a voice in our government. We need to do more than win the next election; we need to make structural updates to our republic to ensure it endures for the next generation.
If you would like to learn more about Project No Cap, go to **[projectnocap.com](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/68a86d9c-4d4c-40c6-be3e-bab4db5556da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and check out the **[Why 435](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/13c84f0b-9e99-4fe0-af49-518e16ea7d00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and **[FAQ](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/f03b2092-8070-460b-9c6d-7ab6818d6490?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **page. clean_body: I have some exciting news. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more | | | Sep 24 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- I have some exciting news. As many of you know, I am passionate about our country, and over the last several years I have worked with many different groups (Principles First, Republicans, Democrats, and now the Forward Party) to make it a better place. Today I am announcing that I am joining Project No Cap as part of their board. Project No Cap is an organized movement to repeal the Permanent Apportionment Act of 1929. The original design of the House was to grow with the population, but since 1929, the number of representatives has been limited to 435. Since then, the population has tripled. A representative in 1929 represented about 220,000 people; today, a representative represents nearly 800,000 people. This structural flaw has concentrated power in the executive and separated the people from those designed to represent them. I have worked in construction for nearly my entire adult life, spending time speaking with everyday Americans in their driveways and garages about the issues that matter most to them. One constant theme in those conversations is that they don't feel anyone represents their values of hard work and responsibility. They look at Washington and feel disconnected from those who lead us. They want leaders who take their responsibilities seriously, listen to the concerns of their constituents, and solve the problems we face today. That's why I joined No Cap; it's an organization focused on responsibility, not power. Those Americans I speak with are intelligent and thoughtful people who deserve a voice in our government. We need to do more than win the next election; we need to make structural updates to our republic to ensure it endures for the next generation. If you would like to learn more about Project No Cap, go to and check out the and page. If you want to do more to help mend our representative democracy, you can sign up to or . And follow the to keep up to date on a movement of the people, by the people, and for the people. | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Kyle Sweetser 548 Market Street PMB 72296, San Francisco, CA 94104 ? ?

**My name is Joe Males, and I’m running for United States Congress in California’s 25th district.** [**This is a longer email, but I humbly ask you to read it and consider donating to my campaign at the end.**](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=202dba501d9d44a0afc04b8323f1c8fe&_e=amElOvFeX3IT6MM-h_wsMd0wZs7_48fcWi6OZW663smI6UfsqnS9aQUX7g5BOcE9S3GpRECbETh10utPy0V1RV4DpIG_VzEKiCCfFrR2GfbCgyaIOA3iJH-vEOayZIJZNIiQn5VwQpH36a2LuXilzwgJY9eMiaw1L-WXQkXFiy-57shSlsm8fqdS_FzvE_PWF1txWKFIOcx1DJwcpIuvQ8jR8Vk0JHl2uL6ZrRgRKdU5RMg3klka15B0aMY7JdcdAwGA2q4izzRXkV7-wGXQf3i1AVKvjlGJCzY_8dLK3YIqIRyF8BDMF0qTMT3MnCU2YO3L2M5W5Jh_zvQxTzeHythHFyC7y7isD8p7FTIDt_NPdWhCMkN-flBtEqp2ms3VJABKdijqqMMzLy2spmK5bg-g7K3xlqjOkh1DO-qAn2fMqNGrLAybqqBXxggpx6aFFRAQRxccg7kc05X0boBVWOGFUpjLeZ3RHlmy-KTDIXLUM8r2wR7EJBQ9g7oZxlZcHl4iZwKaEq8uh25_ErzREnCctSSfZ7tGsS_vRh_Yhxs%3D)

**WHO AM I?** [](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=202dba501d9d44a0afc04b8323f1c8fe&_e=amElOvFeX3IT6MM-h_wsMd0wZs7_48fcWi6OZW663smI6UfsqnS9aQUX7g5BOcE9S3GpRECbETh10utPy0V1RV4DpIG_VzEKiCCfFrR2GfbCgyaIOA3iJH-vEOayZIJZtk0MiDY3a5HRxFLbOZVGSPCqPCRDJ2XAArNJDl6IgohbP0AdDQx-WfnEEYF4rOr9pDDbzrJOmrsZVJHMY1KCvSoC56Z9gjJ4EvCnIFf95zt_NftoK9O4w28KY4GeqMnILwcCaGkTaLN2ixfiKgZq7uZRfwEyhnno-3byQI_UeGwKajep4pScScljXj9GAEj-Y3GkEHh3MKK67KW6zzWzFl-7EENbHpDXIGE6nkb15Q0s-xcx8t1kho3wSuoM03pmPi3Ip6Dnnt04mX7McpJ34SOHCJeG0gWIk5o0tL1LyrKTpkIeeKEmtoXFS1_uMJP92PgMBn53AGqIEFVucnTbWpIp-VyF94HMw09-1A8lQtd7_jClmFotB2LtBIERMjrSc8EMFFRaQ6C4fFxPhK-lzg%3D%3D)

_Like I said, I’m Joe Males. I’m a Mexican-American who was adopted by two wonderful parents when I was four years old._

**At a young age, I joined the United States Marine Corps to defend our country and ultimately earned the rank of Sergeant before my discharge.** Once I entered civilian life, I started my entrepreneurial career owning a successful small computer business until my son took over the family business.

**Since the Democrats will want to use this to attack me, I will tell you: I was a former Democrat.** I switched over to the Republican Party during the Reagan era once I saw what the Democrats truly stood for. I’ve seen firsthand how today’s Democratic Party has abandoned working families. Every single day, I hear from constituents who are struggling with everyday challenges. I hear them, and I fully agree with them. It’s time for change in California.

**WHY DID I ENTER POLITICS?** [](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=202dba501d9d44a0afc04b8323f1c8fe&_e=amElOvFeX3IT6MM-h_wsMd0wZs7_48fcWi6OZW663smI6UfsqnS9aQUX7g5BOcE9S3GpRECbETh10utPy0V1RV4DpIG_VzEKiCCfFrR2GfbCgyaIOA3iJH-vEOayZIJZtk0MiDY3a5HRxFLbOZVGSPCqPCRDJ2XAArNJDl6IgogWCjVl0nrIKQFeXTr8QEucpWAeE6wzkoKwf8hoMAVe09s7Bxf1yM3IExCFIrF2ZwGYUoQ7wE7Y95nBpX-5h_GR4AWoR-qVisFr5qTXk36UFYZxENE1ZQw2ULQTnEfRXufY1dvpOMNT2Xeo1jpxNOGdpHTmF7F32G3TNZnmqcwKm7JSem8s-0Rn_wvL47RFF_YqnJNKH89gdq8dKeUGRyStemdI_JtrvAyDVe_nh5NnKqH5wmyatGBmUpHvGFsdJpBULML7cicP7HgYoaFgq-YW1OmogFoJ7lejVZZKgnM-WogNr_Ypt0ZE4Xl-uFLsTmtj-HHF3hTt9YiO69KFQQ1eobNSk5zCOCKCwkWFTxhZfA%3D%3D)

**In short, my son, Nicholas, was tragically stabbed to death and murdered in 2016.**

If you’re a parent, I’m sure you could imagine how devastating this was for me. Nicholas was only 28 at the time and did not deserve what happened.

He had followed in my footsteps and joined the Marine Corps. He was a father to two children – my grandchildren. When it happened, no one came forward with any information, and the case to find the killer went cold.

**I decided to take a stand, to fight for the rule of law and public safety so that no other family has to experience the same tragedy.** Five years later, I ran for City Council in Hemet. I won, and just a few months later, our amazing law enforcement found the killer and arrested him.

**WHAT ARE MY PRIORITIES AS YOUR NEXT CONGRESSMAN?** [](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=202dba501d9d44a0afc04b8323f1c8fe&_e=amElOvFeX3IT6MM-h_wsMd0wZs7_48fcWi6OZW663smI6UfsqnS9aQUX7g5BOcE9S3GpRECbETh10utPy0V1RV4DpIG_VzEKiCCfFrR2GfbCgyaIOA3iJH-vEOayZIJZtk0MiDY3a5HRxFLbOZVGSPCqPCRDJ2XAArNJDl6IgohsJ_gFmYLj0p1OCnOYRyQImY3NyTHHBajGfYhA_hG33UMhI-RpKRjw6zXOi3s-5jpomFq1kyKIM8lVU84Gmo_5OTU4rxlWJYmHmy3zzb86z9e5sEjef_E66zudDApnx25KcKcuURB2u4q_ymAzbyro1JrixTgpaLGrJ338gzevnMlQ6C-ovSCEEy2nQ-Q3RBZhB-MGLzKzLW3zHRq-MrqguaurtTxp4eEyXdXosURiY4ivA74TMJ_cFU0ASW9SJ7FUUAdN6WGe0OSQnyBROKwk99VmikD9xCpSlroyPdBaZXzrrUuwuJGORYbcJQ5okfF20xBOa0-trF_E_uZEW0xx7fQGP3ihvtIKKjzs-KM9qA%3D%3D)

_**As a former Democrat turned Republican, I know what the Democrat Party is supposed to represent. But ever since the Reagan era, they’ve continued to move farther and farther to the extreme left. Now, they stand for DEI, wokeness, putting Americans last, and doing everything they can to fight against President Trump.**_

**As a Hispanic American who lives in a border district and who was adopted by American parents, I fully believe in LEGAL immigration.** America is THE BEST COUNTRY IN THE WORLD! Millions of people around the world want to move here for the American Dream, for the opportunity of a better life, but they must do it THE RIGHT WAY.

**Our Southern Border has been porous under Joe Biden’s Administration.** Living in a border district, I’ve seen firsthand millions of illegal immigrants entering the country with the help of the dangerous Mexican Cartel, many through my hometown, bringing dangerous drugs like fentanyl, trafficking women and children, and committing heinous crimes on our side of the border. This needs to END, and I’m grateful for President Trump’s leadership on this. In Congress, I’ll always defend strong border security.

**On top of that, I am a firm believer in the America-First Movement.** After four years under Joe Biden’s leadership, America has become weak in every aspect. I already mentioned our border security, but our military, social life, and economy have all become weakened under the rule of DEI and wokeness.

**As a military veteran, it pained me to see the way Joe Biden withdrew from Afghanistan, giving the Taliban millions of dollars worth of high-level American military equipment, which they parade around.** Our weakened military presence allowed Russia to invade Ukraine and Hamas to launch terrorist attacks on Israel. **Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission.

Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy.

During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met.

# Trump flexed America's might for Xi, Bessent got the China truce extended
President Donald Trump **[greeted Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews](https://substack.com/redirect/c1fe5b32-a33d-4aac-8531-3eb5f548cf9b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on Wednesday after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S.-China t**[rade truce will run two months to Jan. 10.](https://substack.com/redirect/3bacd06c-7f4e-43ce-87f8-7d64ec4f61ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/17f60f75-8aad-43bd-a161-73c94cd76128?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **First Andrews tarmac greeting:** Trump met Xi at the airplane stairs after a red carpet, his first trip to Andrews to welcome a foreign leader. Obama last did so for Pope Francis 11 years ago.
* **Truce lasts two months:** The South Korea pact from last October was set to lapse in November. Bessent said Beijing still needs more deliverables. Cutler said China hoped it would last Trump's term.
* **AI talks, no rails:** China's Commerce Ministry c**[onfirmed first U.S.-China AI talks](https://substack.com/redirect/1bbb6fe5-14c2-471e-8551-d8e42f820a18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after Bessent met He Lifeng. Trump said Super Intelligence stays "exactly where it is. Our guardrail is the DOJ!"
* **Stocks slip, dinner set:** The CSI 300 fell 1.7% overnight. Thursday's East Room state dinner includes Nvidia's Jensen Huang, Tesla's Elon Musk and OpenAI's Sam Altman. Xi's expected CEO entourage did not appear.

# Iran just named the next oil front: the Indian Ocean
Brent crude j**[umped to $106.35 a barrel](https://substack.com/redirect/414ba447-5599-45c1-ac85-fdc524e84ac7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/414ba447-5599-45c1-ac85-fdc524e84ac7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Thursday after an adviser to Iran's supreme leader said the war **[could spread to the Indian Ocean if](https://substack.com/redirect/6d9acbee-86aa-40f8-ab5d-57b42003888b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** U.S. attacks resume.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/42dbc4b9-4b8d-453f-a64a-09e37abbc28b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Pezeshkian takes hard line:** At the U.N., President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran would fight "until our last breath" and answered Trump's terrorist label by calling Iranians "victims of terrorism."
* **Safavi warns Indian Ocean:** Yahya Rahim Safavi, advising Mojtaba Khamenei, said the front already moved from the Persian Gulf and Hormuz into the Red Sea and could reach "**[the Indian Ocean and perhaps beyond."](https://substack.com/redirect/6d9acbee-86aa-40f8-ab5d-57b42003888b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **Aramco maps extra routes:** Amin Nasser told Nikkei Asia Aramco is studying a fourth and fifth crude export path, locations undisclosed, and said "the situation will get worse."
* **Trump weighs dual track:** He called a three-hour U.N. sideline meeting "very good" and said he faces a "big decision" on a deal with Tehran or to "annihilate" the country.

# Big business warns Trump: a diesel export ban raises prices
America's largest business groups told President Trump **[a diesel export ban would tighten supplies](https://substack.com/redirect/456271e3-2d13-418a-b3d7-2f79126e04ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and raise costs for families, farmers and truckers, as U.S. diesel averaged $6.51 a gallon.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c2c61f3d-a724-46dd-9605-1ddff4623166?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Industry letter lands Wednesday:** The Chamber of Commerce, Business Roundtable, National Association of Manufacturers and American Petroleum Institute said banning or limiting diesel exports would do the opposite of cutting prices.
* **Farm states apply pressure:** Republican lawmakers in states including Iowa are pushing for action before the elections. AAA put the national average $2.82 above the same period last year.
* **Trump already pushing ban:** At the U.N. on Tuesday Trump said, "I've said let's not send out the diesel. We make a lot of diesel," and that he called for it "within my people."
* **Wright rejects blanket ban:** Energy Secretary Chris Wright told the New York Times "nobody wants a full blanket ban or zero exports of diesel" and "that's not being discussed."

* * *
# Amodei: AI could cure most diseases in 5 to 10 years
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said Wednesday that AI could h**[elp cure most diseases within 5 to 10 years](https://substack.com/redirect/df7a7ec0-3398-4403-a226-3caa94bc0890?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after Claude found a molecular machine that may be a new gene-editing tool.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fb2369b0-9110-4332-83fc-b771b4b210d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Claude led the discovery:** Anthropic said Claude read literature and genome data, then proposed experiments the team ran. Amodei said it was work he would have been proud to do as a Ph.D. student.
* **Machine function still unclear:** The company said the machine's precise biological role, utility, or significance is not yet clear and that it may represent a new gene-editing mechanism.
* **Math sets biology pace:** Models went from high-school math in 2023 to top open problems in late 2026. Amodei said biology is on a similar curve, with humans still running lab tests.
* **No clinical trial shortcut:** Faster discovery would not shorten clinical trials. Any treatment would still need standard testing. Claude is not autonomously running lab equipment today.

# Starbucks just took a $300 million knife to 250 cafes
Starbucks will c**[lose about 250 North American coffeehouses later this week](https://substack.com/redirect/08e050f7-6e06-4da9-a281-b1ac916c9aa6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after COO Mike Grams said a small share of more than 18,000 locations has no path to acceptable financial performance.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b30659d1-740b-4ff5-965d-3814aea11b40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Portfolio review is done:** Grams told Partners most of the 18,000 North American stores are profitable, but some cannot consistently deliver the experience the company wants for customers and partners.
* **Closures equal one percent:** The 250 coffeehouses are about 1% of the North American system. Grams said the cuts hit locations with no acceptable financial path.
* **Grams calls it difficult:** "Closing any coffeehouse is a difficult decision, and we know today's news will be hard for the partners, customers and communities affected," the letter said.
* **Florida deal sits separate:** Last week Starbucks paid Florida $1 million and agreed to drop race- and sex-based hiring goals nationwide, with four years of chief-legal-officer certifications.

# Chip stocks slip after a six-day, 14% SOX rally
The Philadelphia SOX index fell 1.2% Wednesday **[after a six-session 14% climb,](https://substack.com/redirect/334b2e3b-3063-441c-8f18-ee4243b14d50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/334b2e3b-3063-441c-8f18-ee4243b14d50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)as UBS kept a $1,625 **[Micron target](https://substack.com/redirect/25c67033-1990-450a-b39f-2618d4005dd9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/25c67033-1990-450a-b39f-2618d4005dd9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)and **[Michael Burry added semiconductor shorts.](https://substack.com/redirect/ebce5115-abbf-48a2-b1e6-f34a8e76e0cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c35680e5-ea48-4eeb-a55b-c3106a30b71e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **UBS holds $1,625 target:** Timothy Arcuri reiterated a Buy rating and $1,625 price target Wednesday ahead of Micron earnings next week. Shares were $1,046.37, down 2.4% in Thursday premarket trade.
* **Rally snap hits SOX:** Nvidia, AMD and Micron led the prior six-session advance. Micron has more than tripled this year and gained nearly 600% over the past 12 months.
* **Street targets now split:** Citi's Atif Malik kept a Buy and raised his Micron target to $1,300 from $1,150. Wells Fargo's Aaron Rakers kept Overweight but cut his target to $1,400 from $1,525.
* **Burry adds chip shorts:** On Tuesday he added shorts in Micron, Nebius, Palantir and the iShares Semiconductor ETF on Cassandra Unchained, extending a chip short begun at the end of last year.

# McDonald's stock is down 20%. Now comes an $8.5B makeover
McDonald's said Wednesday i**[t will provide about $8.5 billion in NEXT partnering support for franchisees](https://substack.com/redirect/b9dbbcdf-6b1f-40d3-8090-2fd286a5a532?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** through 2036, with roughly $5 billion through 2030, to speed restaurant upgrades and technology.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/296eae3f-03cb-4273-8151-c15a9c32f357?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Capital plus rent relief:** The NEXT aid mixes capital support and rent relief so franchisees can modernize stores, deploy technology, and change operations faster than they could alone.
* **Efficiency cash-flow target:** The company wants about 250 basis points of gross restaurant-level efficiency, or about $100,000 a year in cash-flow benefit for the average restaurant.
* **ArchIQ hits the restaurants:** The plan includes generative AI-enabled ArchIQ at scale and a multiyear "Make it Golden" service program that starts on Founder's Day, Oct. 5.
* **Chicken share, unit growth:** McDonald's wants 1.5 percentage points of chicken and beverage share by 2030, to keep beef leadership, and unit growth adding nearly 2.5% to 2027 systemwide sales.

* * *
# Nvidia, Amazon and Microsoft fall as yields smash 5.13%
Nvidia **[led semiconductor stocks lower](https://substack.com/redirect/7306c173-60ee-45eb-91ec-a1a08f965a08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Thursday as the 10-year Treasury yield sat near 5.1% and the 30-year yield climbed to its highest level since 2004.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/85077014-dbee-4a1d-80b6-d6520b35eae1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Radical safety fallback:** Huang is a vocal opponent of new AI regulation, but Barron's said he has an even more radical solution if there is no way to overcome the problem of unsafe AI.
* **Yields hit duration trade:** The 1**[0-year sat near 5.1% while the 30-year reached its highest level since 2004,](https://substack.com/redirect/b6277c66-25e6-47b5-8e8f-fc9eaef75fb9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/b6277c66-25e6-47b5-8e8f-fc9eaef75fb9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)extending Thursday's decline on worries about more Federal Reserve rate hikes.
* **Tech sector slips early:** The XLK technology sector fell at the open, with Amazon and Microsoft also declining as Nvidia pulled semiconductor stocks lower in the first minutes of trade.
* **Risk assets slip too:** Bitcoin dropped near $83,000 and gold slipped to hover near $4,300. November Brent hovered near $105 and WTI near $94 in the same early window.

body:
|
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139883206/648825804/-664395954?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS84OTkxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmOTdkZmFmNi0zZWI4LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=qAr8caadvBnhovpxmiITwintc2b2MNyJxkyCv2P8Qas=)
Folks, it’s Chelsey Wininger – Executive Director of DASS. Trump’s Department of Justice is investigating DASS Chair and Nev. Secretary of State Cisco Aguilar for failing to comply with federal voting laws. **They demanded him to save the state’s 2024 election records or face civil and criminal penalties if he doesn’t comply.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139883207/648825805/1071238059?refcode=em-9.24.26-all-1-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS84OTkxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmOTdkZmFmNi0zZWI4LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=qAr8caadvBnhovpxmiITwintc2b2MNyJxkyCv2P8Qas=) These records include Social Security numbers, driver’s license details, and home addresses of millions of voters. Trump and his DOJ have made it clear: they want a national voter database controlled by the federal government, and they’ll do whatever it takes to make it a reality. The same national liberal donor network that has been targeting this state all cycle is still writing checks because flipping a Senate seat in President Trump's home state would be the biggest symbolic victory the Left could claim in 2026. And in a state with multiple expensive media markets, a ground game that has to cover millions of voters, and an election that will be decided in the final weeks of October, running low on resources in the home stretch is not a risk we can afford to take. The voter contact operations. The final ad buys. The ground game turnout programs that move the needle in the precincts where margins are razor thin. We have the momentum. We have the candidates. **Getting the Purdue Pharma Gang Back Together**
_Opioid Lobbyist is Welcoming Purdue Pharma Colleague to New Hampshire_
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** September 24th, 2026
---
| | | **CONTACT** karina@nhrsc.com

---
| |

**CONCORD, N.H.** — Today, Opioid Lobbyist Cinde Warmington is welcoming Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear back to New Hampshire. Beshear has his own questionable associations with Warmington’s former client, Purdue Pharma.Warmington’s campaign has been dogged by her career of working for the opioid industry, including time lobbying for looser restrictions for OxyContin and lying on behalf of Purdue Pharma.
Last week, Warmington’s work for Purdue Pharma was put back into the spotlight in [resurfaced reporting from WMUR](https://us.list-manage.com/mVhzcIgOQWx?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=78UdE6po5QoF8GNZx9z1_7AXM36rjeNI9_JgezvVdDubcEbShA1Qjslt6Q==). In the articles and stories from 2002, it was made clear that Warmington was working directly against then-Governor Jeanne Shaheen’s efforts to restrict prescriptions of the addictive opioid OxyContin. At the same time, Shaheen’s husband and Warmington’s then-boss, Billy Shaheen, distanced himself from Warmington’s work on behalf of Purdue Pharma.
Fittingly, Andy Beshear was a partner at a Kentucky law firm that represented Purdue Pharma and he [later recused himself](https://us.list-manage.com/pp7srt6IZiB?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=Ifx8gIVmeuk0kU5aOY4VR-VeObxj7cOKExiJclH6T6zMFDFn-AWOwwXy_g==) from matters involving a settlement between the state and the company due to those prior connections.
“Warmington is getting the gang back together by welcoming her fellow Purdue Pharma alumni back to the campaign trail,” **said Chairman Scott Maltzie.** “Warmington’s campaign has failed to gain momentum at every juncture of this race, so it’s no surprise that she’s desperate enough to go back to her Purdue Pharma rolodex."

| Peter, it's Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield.

I know a lot of you already know me and know about our work, but it's been a while since I last reached out, so I thought it would make sense to start from the beginning again.

I was raised in Oregon. My mom was a Green Party activist and my dad was an insurance executive and colonel in the Air Force Reserve.

Their views often differed on issues, but that contrast helped me become who I am today, someone who focuses on the goals people hold in common, not what divides them.

As a former Linn County Peer Court Judge, State Representative for Oregon then later Speaker of the House, and now as Attorney General, I've made a commitment to further the common goal of protecting our state.

**And that's exactly what we've done.**
---
| Over the past year:
* We've protected $7 billion in federal funds for critical services that Oregon families rely on.
* We've held corporations (like Meta) and industries (like Big Pharma) accountable for knowingly making their social media platforms more addictive to kids and driving up the cost of prescription drugs.
* We took the Trump administration to court for their attempts to unlawfully deploy the National Guard in our state, withhold SNAP funding, and interfere in our elections.

---
| **Peter, I take my job seriously.**

My focus has always been to create a safer, healthier, and more just future for Oregon, and I'm proud to play a role in making that vision a reality.

**But I know there's still more work to do.**

[**Peter, we're building a grassroots coalition to continue fighting for justice in Oregon and I'm hoping you'll chip in any amount to join our team. Even if it's just $3, can you make a contribution today?**](https://us.list-manage.com/1ANUAeMYcvA?e=1768325bd4&c2id=0fcd3a526fabf816bd24466788989260)

| | | | Since taking office as Oregon’s Attorney General in 2025, Dan Rayfield has focused on protecting Oregon’s working families and homegrown small businesses by taking on pharmaceutical companies, polluters, and large corporations driving up costs for groceries and other everyday needs. He’s been fighting hard to block the Trump Administration from taking away the rights of Oregonians, suing Trump–and winning–dozens of times.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/11NXi99Vbh7?e=1768325bd4&c2id=0fcd3a526fabf816bd24466788989260)

Dan grew up in Oregon and is a product of the Oregon public school system. Following his graduation from Tigard High School, Dan attended Western Oregon University and then earned his law degree from Willamette University College of Law. In 2005, prior to his law school graduation, he clerked for the Benton County District Attorney’s office. During his time at the District Attorney’s office, he gained his first trial experience prosecuting DUIs and other misdemeanor charges. Dan has also served as a coach attorney for the OSU Mock Trial Team, a former Linn County Peer Court Judge, and Past President of the Linn-Benton Bar Association.

Since 2015, Dan served as the State Representative for Oregon House District 16, which encompasses the cities of Corvallis and Philomath, and Oregon State University. In 2022, he was elected by his colleagues to serve as Speaker of the House. Over that time, he helped lead the way on issues including a high quality education for our children, access to affordable and reliable healthcare, making sure families are able to earn a living wage while simultaneously nurturing innovation and supporting Oregon’s small businesses, and making our public safety system more effective and accountable. Dan lives in Corvallis with his wife Amanda and their son Adam.

**Where you start should never determine where you end up.**

For me, that's the American dream: any kid, no matter where they were born, who their parents are, or whether they had the right connections, can grow up, work hard, follow their dreams, and – like me – no matter how many tries it takes, pick themselves back up, start over, and make those goals real.

→ Virginians are facing skyrocketing prices at the grocery store and gas pump because of this president’s reckless war-of-choice in Iran and downright stupid tariff policies.

→ Americans are getting kicked off their health care and rural clinics are closing because this administration would rather give tax breaks to those at the very top than help working families.

→ Our president is using the office to enrich himself, his family, and his allies – while working families get squeezed.

I’m running for reelection because I believe every American deserves the same shot as success I had. They deserve leaders who will fight for them, work to make their lives better, and put some real guardrails on this administration run amok.

**But that work starts with winning this race – and electing VA Democrats in competitive elections across the Commonwealth.**

Let me be honest with you about something.
I'm not supposed to be in this race.
The grandson of a sharecropper? Not supposed to be a viable Senate candidate in Louisiana.
A Black farmer from rural Tensas Parish? Not supposed to compete statewide in the Deep South.
Someone without billionaire backers or a Rolodex full of Washington insiders? Not supposed to have a shot at flipping a Senate seat.
But here we are.
**And MAGA is absolutely shocked.**
They thought Louisiana was locked up. They thought they could focus on defending seats in swing states while the South stayed safely red. They thought a race like ours — a real populist challenge to their grip on power — wasn't possible here.
They were wrong.
Look at what's happening: Democrats flipping Trump districts across the South. MAGA candidates tearing each other apart in primaries. Republican retirements at levels not seen since the Great Depression. Trump's approval cratering over his failed Iran war.
This is a once-in-a-lifetime opening. The kind of moment that doesn't come around often in Louisiana politics.
**_And I believe — deep in my bones — that this is the campaign to meet this moment._**
Not because I'm the most polished politician. Not because I've been planning a Senate run my whole career. But because I understand what working Louisianans need because I've lived their struggles.
I know what it's like to watch costs rise while your income stays flat. I know what it's like to compete against corporations that rig the system against family operations. I know what it's like to worry about whether there will be anything left for the next generation.
That's the authentic economic populism that can win here. Not the fake MAGA version that delivers nothing but culture wars — the real thing that actually fights for working people.
And if we capitalize on this moment — if we show the political world that Louisiana is genuinely winnable — everything changes.
Not just for this race. For the entire map. For what's possible in the South.
But only if we have the resources to compete. And that counts on good folks like you stepping up.

body:
[ stdin# ][IMG]

HEADLINES: Battle for the Midterms | Record Breaking Progressives | Greg
Casar on Building Our Ranks | Jackson & Nixon on the Senate | Nina Turner:
Happy Birthday Our Rev! | & MORE!

★ ★ ★

THE BATTLE FOR THE MIDTERMS IS ON!

We are at an inflection point in American history — and the future hinges
on these Midterms.

On Monday, thousands of Our Revolution activists joined us for our 2026
Battle for the Midterms Kickoff, as we fired up our grassroots operation
for the final stretch to Election Day.

The opportunity in front of us is enormous: flip the House and Senate,
elect a record number of progressives, and fundamentally change the
balance of power in Washington.

After a decade of building progressive power from the ground up, Our
Revolution Executive Director Joseph Geevarghese is rallying our movement
to put our organizing into action:

“We’ve spent 10 years building the infrastructure, developing the leaders,
and proving that grassroots organizing can overcome Big Money and the
establishment. Now, we have an opportunity to put all of that experience
to work in one of the most consequential elections of our lifetime.”

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39761?t=1011&akid=11353%2E5885482%2EmWdOt9 ]WATCH THE MIDTERMS BATTLE KICKOFF HERE

★ ★ ★

FLIP CONGRESS — WITH 22 NEW HOUSE PROGRESSIVES!

Remember what a game changer it was to elect the Squad and grow it? Well
now we could send a massive wave of 22 NEW progressives to the House.

Rep. Greg Casar, Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, joined us
to talk about what it would mean to dramatically grow our ranks in the
House — and use that power to deliver for working people.

“We have to flip the House, flip the Senate, but flip it with people who
actually want to fight the corporate interests that have been screwing us
over for far too long and make sure we have a Democratic Party that is
pro-worker and anti-billionaire.”

He laid out the dynamics of key House races like firefighter Sam Forstag
in the red state of Montana, union teacher Randy Villegas in a red
district in California, and other working class fighters ready to take
seats in November.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39762?t=1012&akid=11353%2E5885482%2EmWdOt9 ]Chip in any amount ASAP to power Our Revolution’s proven voter turnout
machine in these exciting House races coast to coast!

★ ★ ★

THE BATTLE FOR THE SENATE

This November we could add SIX bold new champions to join Bernie Sanders
in the U.S. Senate! [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39762?t=1013&akid=11353%2E5885482%2EmWdOt9 ]Chip in to elect the Super Senate Six!
On Monday, we heard from two of these great candidates ready to shake up
Washington: Angie Nixon in Florida and Troy Jackson in Maine.

Angie won the primary after being outspent by the establishment Democrat
16 to 1! Now she’s mobilizing the grassroots to take on the Florida
Republican machine.

“Before I became a state rep, before I became a lawmaker, before I became
the Democratic nominee for United States Senate, I was an organizer.”

And she summed up the strategy behind her campaign in one powerful line:
“Organized people will beat big money each and every day of the week. We
just got to get the people organized.”

In Maine, Troy Jackson told us he’s seeing an extraordinary level of
grassroots energy as his campaign heads into the final stretch against GOP
Senator Susan Collins.

“Since 30 years ago, I’ve been waiting for the day that everyday
working-class people can rise up... Right now, people are showing up like
crazy.”

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39762?t=1014&akid=11353%2E5885482%2EmWdOt9 ]It’s Big Money versus people power. And we're betting on ALL OF US.
Chip in a donation today to power our 5 million voter contact operation
over the next SIX WEEKS!

★ ★ ★

PEOPLE POWER CAN BEAT BIG MONEY

Newly elected Rep. Aisha Wahab knows firsthand what it means to go up
against massive outside spending — and win.

After facing millions of dollars in the special election, Aisha told us
the answer isn't trying to match Big Money dollar for dollar. It's about
connecting directly with voters at the doors, on the phones, and
delivering a clear contrast to the opposition.

“Our Revolution was with us here on the ground. Real people telling
neighbors why they’re voting, what they care about, what they want to see
done — that’s really the biggest part of our campaign and how we were able
to push back.”

Our Revolution activists helped make tens of thousands of calls into
Aisha's district — exactly the kind of grassroots operation we're now
scaling up across the country heading into November. [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39763?t=1015&akid=11353%2E5885482%2EmWdOt9 ]Chip in here to
power our Phonebank Force.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39764?t=1016&akid=11353%2E5885482%2EmWdOt9 ]SIGN UP TO MAKE CALLS WITH OUR TEAM

★ ★ ★

BUILDING LOCAL POWER IN A RED STATE

Our Revolution Board Chair Megan Green joined us to show what building
progressive power from the ground up can accomplish — even in a red state.

Megan serves as President of the St. Louis Board of Alders, and together
we’re developing the next generation of leaders.

“We’ve been able to build a progressive majority here in the city of St.
Louis — in the middle of a red state. And now we’re taking that organizing
and building power at the state level.”

That's the progressive pipeline we've spent a decade building: organizers
become candidates, win locally, govern, and build upward and outward.

Campaigns come and go. Our movement marches ahead.

★ ★ ★

10 YEARS IN THE FIGHT — AND JUST GETTING STARTED

Few people have been closer to this movement than Nina Turner — former
president of Our Revolution and Bernie Sanders' 2020 national co-chair.

As we celebrate 10 years since Bernie founded Our Revolution, Nina
reflected on how far we've come — and the sustained organizing that made
it possible.

“Ten years is a big deal. We should celebrate what Our Revolution has been
able to accomplish — but understand that we have so much more work to do.”

That's the lesson of our first decade. Political power isn't built in one
election. It's built by organizing year after year, developing leaders and
creating a movement that doesn't disappear when Election Day is over.

Nina's prescription for the next decade? “Organize, organize, organize.”
Ten years down. And we're just getting started.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35232?t=1017&akid=11353%2E5885482%2EmWdOt9 ]If you can, invest a monthly donation to keep our movement marching
forward — through the Midterms and Beyond.

★ ★ ★

RIGHT NOW: FINISH THE FIGHT TO BAN DARK MONEY

Winning elections is only one part of building power. For 10 years, Our
Revolution has also been organizing inside the Democratic Party to change
the rules themselves.

Last year, that inside/outside strategy delivered a major victory: after
sustained grassroots pressure, the DNC passed a resolution to ban dark and
corporate money from the 2028 presidential primary process.

Now comes the real test: making sure it actually happens.

Our Revolution Founding Chair and DNC member Larry Cohen joined us to lay
out the urgency of the next two weeks as we push the DNC to put forward
the implementation plan:

“Our primaries should belong to the voters in the Democratic Party —
working-class people, Black, brown and white — not to the billionaires and
not to the corporations.”

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39765?t=1018&akid=11353%2E5885482%2EmWdOt9 ]ADD YOUR NAME: TELL THE DNC TO GET DARK & CORPORATE MONEY OUT OF THE
2028 PRESIDENTIAL PRIMARY

★ ★ ★

45 DAYS. 5 MILLION VOTER CONTACTS.

Now comes the work.

Our Revolution is activating our national voter turnout machine with a
goal of making 5 million voter contacts in key races before Election Day.

We’re making calls. Sending texts. Knocking doors. And mobilizing
volunteers across the country to help elect progressive champions from the
local level all the way to the U.S. Senate.

This is what 10 years of organizing has built.
Now it's time to use it.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39763?t=1019&akid=11353%2E5885482%2EmWdOt9 ]CHIP IN TO THE MIDTERM BATTLE FUND

It’s all hands on deck — and on the phones. We’re training up new
volunteers right now to expand our Phonebank Team. It’s a lot of fun and
it’s the best way to make the biggest impact on these Midterms. Sign up
today!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39764?t=1020&akid=11353%2E5885482%2EmWdOt9 ]JOIN OUR PHONE BANK FORCE

★ ★ ★

As Trump and his cronies attack our democracy, we’re organizing alongside
the No Kings Movement for Early Vote turnout and Election Protection.
[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39766?t=1021&akid=11353%2E5885482%2EmWdOt9 ]DONATE TO POWER OUR NO KINGS WORK HERE

October 17 will be a MASSIVE nationwide day of action: rallies, block
parties, walks to the polls, and helping neighbors get to their voting
stations. [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39767?t=1022&akid=11353%2E5885482%2EmWdOt9 ]SIGN UP TO HOST A NO KINGS EVENT HERE

When we organize, we win.
★ ★ ★

It’s time to Make Trump Cry in the Midterms.

Let’s take power back from Trump and the oligarchs who are entrenching us
in war, rigging our economy, and targeting our communities. Get your
[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39768?t=1023&akid=11353%2E5885482%2EmWdOt9 ]stickers and other merch to help power our organizing. Thanks for all
of your support!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/37510?t=1024&akid=11353%2E5885482%2EmWdOt9 ]GRAB YOUR MERCH!

★ ★ ★

I sat down with _The New York Times_ yesterday, and here’s what I had to say: [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139885431/648833201/-1768798733?refcode=em20260924&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjg4Y2VjZjJiLTQ0YjgtZjExMS1hNmE5LTAwMGQzYTU2ZDJmNyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=-Hum2HeCparjjVMOT1IWFDcNJ0u13ri66pBQll0DvQU=) The last few years have felt like a massive step backward in our fight for a livable future. We’ve never gotten legislation in Congress that’s truly commensurate with what science demands. And why can’t we get that legislation passed? **Because far too many politicians—Democrats and Republicans alike—take money from the fossil fuel industry instead of legislating for the people.** They are in the deep pockets of Big Oil, in a corporate government that seems to have a big ole’ for sale sign to whoever writes the biggest check. Enough is enough. This November, we have a real chance to vote out the leaders who’ve failed us — and replace them with climate champions who understand that a healthy planet and a healthy democracy rise and fall together. **You see, the forces driving our authoritarian backsliding are the same ones poisoning our planet.** That’s why I started the Jane Fonda Climate PAC. I realized years ago that my own inaction was no longer an option, and I’ve dedicated my life to this struggle. While I wish I had stepped up even sooner, there is no better time than right now to fight like hell for a world where our children and grandchildren don’t pay the price of our inaction. And in the next 40 days, we have a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to transform who holds power right in front of these oily executives and corporate lobbyists. **We can flip the House and secure vital state and local seats from Georgia to Michigan to Texas. But our endorsed candidates are being hit with dark money, vicious attacks, and outright lies. They need the resources to break through the noise before voters cast their ballots.** **[If we want to take back power for the people, we have to do it together. The many can beat the money _if_ we show up. clean_body: | I sat down with The New York Times yesterday, and here’s what I had to say: = The last few years have felt like a massive step backward in our fight for a livable future. We’ve never gotten legislation in Congress that’s truly commensurate with what science demands. And why can’t we get that legislation passed? Because far too many politicians—Democrats and Republicans alike—take money from the fossil fuel industry instead of legislating for the people. They are in the deep pockets of Big Oil, in a corporate government that seems to have a big ole’ for sale sign to whoever writes the biggest check. Enough is enough. This November, we have a real chance to vote out the leaders who’ve failed us — and replace them with climate champions who understand that a healthy planet and a healthy democracy rise and fall together. You see, the forces driving our authoritarian backsliding are the same ones poisoning our planet. That’s why I started the Jane Fonda Climate PAC. I realized years ago that my own inaction was no longer an option, and I’ve dedicated my life to this struggle. While I wish I had stepped up even sooner, there is no better time than right now to fight like hell for a world where our children and grandchildren don’t pay the price of our inaction. And in the next 40 days, we have a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to transform who holds power right in front of these oily executives and corporate lobbyists. We can flip the House and secure vital state and local seats from Georgia to Michigan to Texas. But our endorsed candidates are being hit with dark money, vicious attacks, and outright lies. name: KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION
subject: What Taxpayers Deserve to Know
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION * 6709 West 119th Street * Ste
body:
| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/9WlbGZvkgYP?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/4VnPd4QGaVb?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

Friends,I spend a lot of time digging through Johnson County agendas, budgets and transactions because sometimes the most important questions are buried in the details.**Recently, a $4.5 million real estate project in Gardner caught my attention.** Johnson County is moving forward with plans to acquire the former Gardner Family Care building at **18320 S. Center Street**. The County's proposed purchase price is **$2.8 million** , with approximately another **$1.7 million planned for improvements** , bringing the total project to roughly **$4.5 million**.The seller identified in the County transaction is **Frontier Investments**.Here is where the questions begin.The property was publicly listed for **$2.8 million in November 2025** and went under contract in June 2026. Publicly available records are not entirely clear about when Frontier acquired, or will acquire, title to the property.That raises a basic question: **What exactly is Frontier's role in this transaction, and why is the County purchasing the property through Frontier rather than directly from the original owner?** Additionally, the Johnson County Post reported the property's most recent county appraisal at approximately **$1.398 million**.Now, an appraised value is not the same thing as market value. A commercial property can absolutely sell for more than its tax appraisal.**But when taxpayers are committing millions of dollars, I want to understand exactly how we got from Point A to Point B. Here are just a few of my questions:**
* Who brought Frontier Investments into this transaction?
* When did Frontier become involved?
* What did Frontier pay, or agree to pay, for the property?
* Is Frontier receiving a profit, fee or other compensation as part of this transaction?
* If this property was publicly listed and the County had been looking for a Gardner location, why wasn't the County able to negotiate directly for the property?
* What independent appraisal, market analysis or due diligence did the County obtain before agreeing to the $2.8 million purchase price?
* What alternatives were considered before committing taxpayers to a roughly $4.5 million project?

The building is intended for expanded mental health services in southern Johnson County. **The need for mental health services is not the issue I am raising here.** The issue is stewardship.When the government spends taxpayer dollars, particularly millions of them on a real estate transaction involving an intermediary, the public should be able to understand **who is involved, what everyone is being paid, why the deal was structured this way and whether taxpayers received the best possible value.** Maybe there are perfectly reasonable answers to every one of these questions.**Then let's hear them.** Transparency shouldn't come after questions are raised. It should be built into the transaction from the beginning.We are **40 days from the general election.** With current leadership, I believe transactions that raise more questions than answers will continue. In order to deliver on my commitment to transparency and good financial stewardship, it is vital that I win this race.**Here is how you can help:**
1. Spread the word
2. Request a sign here: ****[**I want a sign!**](https://us.list-manage.com/APUKE54Alez?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)
3. Make a contribution: [**DONATE HERE**](https://us.list-manage.com/7VFV58CqYQy?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)
4. Volunteer! [**JOIN THE TEAM**](https://us.list-manage.com/19bZC3KHcVG?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)

Momentum is building, we can win! Thanks for your encouragement, support and vote.Fighting for you,Karen CrnkovichCandidate for Johnson County Commission Chair

| | | | | | Friend,

Every sign in a yard tells your neighbors something a TV ad never can: someone they know and trust is ready for new leadership in Santa Fe. That kind of support is contagious, and I want the whole state to see it.

[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
We hate to admit it, but we’ll be honest: John James talks a good game.

But the bottom line is it’s just talk. He’s shown Michigan what he’ll
actually fight for time and time again.

He voted not once, not twice, but three times to cut healthcare for
hundreds of thousands of Michiganders.

In Congress, he refused to stand up to Trump’s tariffs, instead proudly
backing them multiple times, and now Michiganders are paying the price.

When Trump tried to overturn a free and fair election that he lost in
2020, John James was right there parroting the very same attacks and lies.

Michigan doesn’t need a good talker — we need someone who will fight tooth
and nail for us, and get stuff done.

And Jocelyn’s the person for the job. When Donald Trump tried to
strong-arm her into turning over Michiganders’ private voting information,
she didn’t bend to his pressure.

She took him to court — and won.

That’s the question in this election: who will our governor fight for?

We know who’s going to fight for everyday Michiganders, lower costs, and
raise wages, and it’s not John James.

| | | I lost an election earlier this year, and I'm not going to pretend that didn't hurt. I put everything into that race. So did my family, friends, and supporters. And when it didn't go our way, I could have quietly stepped back, taken some time, and let someone else carry the fight forward. **_But that's not how I was raised._** My parents came to this country with nothing. They worked hard, and they did it without complaint, because they believed complaining wasn't going to change anything. What changed things was getting back up the next morning and doing the work again. I watched them do that for years. It's the single clearest lesson of my childhood: you do not get to wallow. You keep going. So not soon after that primary ended, I started Equal Opportunity Now. **It wasn’t because I had something to prove, it was because I still have something to give. ** I've spent nearly a decade in Congress learning how this fight actually works — how campaigns get won, how corruption gets exposed, how real change actually gets made instead of just talked about. I wasn't ready to set that aside, and honestly, I don't think this moment can afford for me to. Because here's where we are: In 40 days, we have a chance to deliver a real check on Donald Trump in the midterms. A Congress that will finally hold this administration accountable instead of rubber-stamping it. That is not a small thing. That may be the most important thing that happens in this country all year. I am not on the ballot this November. But I am not sitting this one out either. I am doing everything I can to help elect leaders who will fight for our values. [**Will you chip in $5 today to help us keep organizing in communities the national party has written off?**](http://clicksp.shawnharrisforcongress.com/f/a/e_zNvHJT8MW8QjUBZDGyFw~~/AAPPABA~/aL59Ywz8blhIcAz_yI4jzNzEwJ7nr_U8YqRM0Vy126FMi4w59deRNcDa2f-4P74r_LdUIQs24wDTmgKpiK9THzfpb-D2ZLIqgdaSwo3Pt3vr0LKpysJizk84pIq_AF4T4s1HWLNTbpW258GAmuIblko8qX9ZZuPBJ0cFV1ba10cG306WIR7r_-KoUPeyJ84y3l_MPDEQaLiNMo2aMlKgfRCJeYcgoZuaUsf7Y0nXIZplcB3d0eswalqgGfwxfzO_kb13YM3eywnzQ6VnWM_LhlK0nKw2VTf1D7ZIHuaFrdbmDu5N4-cWcJVMbyZmlQ4K) That progress did not come from a rescue by Washington. clean_body: | | A new profile of this race asked the question that Washington has avoided: can our grassroots campaign win in rural Northwest Georgia? | The answer is in the numbers. In the March special election, we finished first with 37% of the vote. In the runoff, we came within just 273 votes of winning Paulding County -- a nine-point improvement in a district Donald Trump carried by roughly 37 points. That progress did not come from a rescue by Washington. It came from volunteers knocking doors, making calls, holding town halls, and listening to voters who want a representative focused on them. " When I get to D.C., my focus is one hundred percent you, your kids and your grandkids." That is the kind of campaign we are building: local, accountable, and powered by people who believe this district deserves better than Trump-endorsed Clay Fuller. They wrote this district off, but voters are proving them wrong. But narrowing the gap is not enough. We have to close it, and that takes a field program strong enough to reach every persuadable voter across GA-14. ~~ ~~ Let's get the job done -- together. I want to be direct with you about what this really is. It’s not a bureaucratic mess. It’s not a technical glitch.

**This is a poison Donald Trump has been feeding the American people for years: make voters doubt whether their vote will even count.**

He and his allies have worked long and hard to cast doubt on our elections — because a public that distrusts its own elections is easier to control than one that shows up and makes their voices heard at the ballot box.

_It's coming from a president who grows more powerful when we stop believing our votes matter._

**There is only one antidote strong enough to counter that threat: turnout so large and so overwhelming that no purged list or rigged voting system can suppress it.**

That is the movement we’re building. Seat by seat, state by state. And there is no question that it requires each and every one of us to step up. **The Mississippi Miracle They Don 't Want You to See**
Five days ago, the OECD released the PISA 2025 results, and the headline deserved to be bigger than it was: American 15-year-olds posted a reading score of 490 -- the lowest ever recorded for the United States, a 14-point drop since 2022. That's roughly seven months of learning, gone. We now rank 13th in the world in reading and 27th in math. Globally, reading and math hit historic lows; for the United States, these are among the worst scores PISA has ever logged. The story ran for a news cycle and vanished.

#

Peter, I’m sorry.
Over the next few days, you’re going to get a few more emails than normal from me. But if you give me the chance, I’d like to explain why. This won’t take long.
You might already know this, but in 6 days on September 30th, we close the books on our quarterly FEC deadline. After that period ends we’ll be legally required to report our fundraising numbers to the public. What that means is everything we’ve raised — how much, how many donations, from how many people — is going to be public knowledge.
And, believe it or not, people do look at this stuff. The press, our allies, our adversaries — they’re all going to be watching to see what we report. Our foes will be sizing us up, and our friends will be looking to see how much we can bring to the table in the elections this year.
Now, here’s the truth: A lot of people think putting up a big fundraising number is what matters most. But what really matters is the amount of donations you receive, because that’s what shows the real strength of your team.
With so many eyes on us, showing strength really matters. That’s why this is important, and it’s why I’m asking you:

subject: Supporting a colleague in a tough fight
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Gillen for NY
body:
She's fighting for the right things

---
| | | | Hey Peter, it's Mark Kelly.
---
I'm writing today on behalf of my friend and colleague, Laura Gillen.

name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: Tom Perriello
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
If we want a Congress that actually fights for working people, we have to take back the House in November. That will come down to a handful of swing districts where the margins are razor-thin and every door knocked makes a difference.
Virginia's 5th district is one of them.
**So today, I am proud to endorse Tom Perriello for Congress.**
Tom flipped this seat before by showing up for working families, and he can do it again. But he is up against a Republican incumbent and he needs all of us to have his back. _[Will you split a donation between our campaigns today?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260924-perriello.Hk0K4A&refcode=em20260924-12345-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12345%2E2526796%2EPbBhDS)_
**Here is why I trust Tom to be a fighter in Congress:**
He does not take a dime from corporate PACs or lobbyists. Neither do I. When Tom walks into a vote, he answers to the people of his district. Tom has spent the last 25 years taking on corporate lobbyists, electric utility monopolies, and the Trump administration.
Tom has served in Congress before and proved that he will hold the line under pressure. He voted for the Affordable Care Act, which guaranteed coverage for more than 32,000 people in his district and made it illegal for insurance companies to deny coverage for pre-existing conditions. Corporate lobbyists leaned on him hard to vote no. He voted yes anyway, because it was the right thing to do. We need more of that kind of courage in Washington.
We also agree on something that is common sense: members of Congress must be banned from trading stocks. Members of Congress should not be able to abuse their position in Congress to make huge profits in the stock market.
I would be proud to work alongside Tom to fight for working people and to rid Washington of corruption.
With just 40 days until Election Day, the next few weeks will decide this race. Every donation lets Tom's campaign knock more doors and reach more voters across the district before ballots are cast.
[ Early voting is already underway in Virginia, so today I am asking: If you can afford it, will you please split a donation of any amount between our campaigns today? Since we both reject corporate PAC donations, every contribution will make a powerful difference.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260924-perriello.Hk0K4A&refcode=em20260924-12345-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=12345%2E2526796%2EPbBhDS)
[](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260924-perriello.Hk0K4A&refcode=em20260924-12345-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=12345%2E2526796%2EPbBhDS)
**[Contribute $5](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260924-perriello.Hk0K4A&refcode=em20260924-12345-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=24&akid=12345%2E2526796%2EPbBhDS)**
If you cannot afford to chip in today, I completely understand. Thank you for being here.
In solidarity,
Alexandria

**[Donate](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260924-perriello.Hk0K4A&refcode=em20260924-12345-P_FND_EGR_GRM&t=1&akid=12345%2E2526796%2EPbBhDS)** | **[Merch](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/9251?utm_source=em-footer-20260924-12345-P_FND_EGR_GRM&t=2&akid=12345%2E2526796%2EPbBhDS)**

body:
Money| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139889019/648845113/-619331744?refcode=260924&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjEwMzAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTQwOTlkYzktNGNiOC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=WjB1e_Rg_JFTefLvDfynjzLav0iSw2MNG1W_1ORVHyo=)

Peter,

I want to tell you about a story that ran in _The Bulwark_ , because it says more about this race than any ad I could run.

My opponent, Michael Alfonso, is 26 years old. He's never held office. His campaign website doesn't even mention transportation policy.

**But his father-in-law is Sean Duffy -- the U.S. Secretary of Transportation, and it turns out a remarkable number of people with business in front of the Department of Transportation have contributed to Alfonso's campaign.**
---
* A **trucking CEO who lobbies the Department of Transportation** on driver safety exemptions.
* Airlines**regulated by the FAA**.
* A liquefied natural gas company with **a permit sitting on Duffy's desk**.
* A **passenger-rail startup that needs federal approval** to launch.

---
**At least two dozen individuals who've lobbied Duffy's department, together writing checks totaling over $40,000.** Some of these donors had never given to a Republican before. Several of them won contracts from Duffy's department within weeks of writing their checks.

And Duffy himself has already transferred $1.5 million -- more than Alfonso's entire campaign has raised -- into a super PAC built to elect his son-in-law.
I've spent my career protecting our public lands and our water, not currying favor with contractors from Bethesda and Dallas. I don't have a cabinet secretary clearing the way for me.**I have you.**

**[If this makes you as frustrated as it makes me, I'd ask you to pitch in whatever you can today. We're not going to outspend a $1.5 million super PAC. But we can out-work it -- with a campaign funded by the people who care.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139889021/648845115/-619331744?refcode=260924&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjEwMzAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTQwOTlkYzktNGNiOC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=WjB1e_Rg_JFTefLvDfynjzLav0iSw2MNG1W_1ORVHyo=)**

Thank you,
Fred Clark

| | | | [](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=f024f5b0298a4d049009d16cd03b697b&_e=lpAZhZGdycXVa60R-K4opMVm_zLsglCS_VB-SYjCJM21t4-8oq8fs0Y0vjkwlgOX1bCTVlniBUDdxNIYcNycc6EkfLfJlpj7jL8lJ9yD-WyVZ_Cqj-wzIIdvKKqp7zeLUQ2AbyovwytAOJhoXhOullD_U6_2v1SFaIcsNXW_RbMITmqyXJ4YB3aLpNq6Nc_PIDhk3MbDnn29Roj3RsiWS7E8xHtYp_WXGsvuAu2BQMrpHKo2F7HTZp928oArG_azHXjgcKcltPlLsI_oetdBKlLWETtZy6EaNz1653_Sns7UfRbLaGSMO4q7JqUhHDN0fdUcjfMJBDtr6g6kWR4ej4DewGC9D_icxWuDPE1j_CmM_Bw6-zb5oC61rAtqLfGY2ZmDLFn0IGwB565slP_QbA%3D%3D)

Fellow Conservative: Texas is about to decide the fate of the Senate majority — and if we lose it, we won't just lose a seat. We'll hand Democrats their first statewide win in Texas since 1994, and the earthquake will be felt by Americans across the country. First, let's be clear about how we got here. The Republican establishment in DC spent over $150 million — the most expensive Senate primary in American history — trying to stop Ken Paxton from becoming the nominee. _They lost._ Paxton defeated Sen. John Cornyn by nearly 30 points. But the damage was done, and now Democrat James Talarico is within striking distance of flipping the seat. You'd think Cornyn would be all-in to stop him from turning Texas blue. Nope. Instead, he's trashing Paxton as lazy and a poor campaigner, while telling reporters the party shouldn't spend another dime on his race because of limited resources. That's rich. **Even worse, Cornyn is working with former President George W. Bush to pull money out of Texas to fund moderate Senate candidates in other states — many of whom are far bigger underdogs than Paxton.** With friends like these, who needs enemies?
