Ken Paxton has spent over a decade as Texas Attorney General doing what the GOP establishment only talks about. He sued the Biden administration more than any other AG in the country — on the border, on illegal mandates, on federal overreach — and won. While career politicians in Washington cut deals, Paxton has been on the front lines of the fight against the open-borders agenda. President Trump didn't endorse him as an afterthought — he called Paxton a "true MAGA warrior" because Paxton has earned it. That's exactly why the establishment tried to kill his campaign before it started and why they're throwing a temper tantrum now. A real fighter in the Senate threatens the comfortable do-nothing environment they've built in DC. They'd rather have an empty suit who plays along with their empty promises and endless excuses than a conservative who delivers. **Make no mistake: John Cornyn and the GOP establishment are working against Paxton because they want Texas to lose. They need it to lose, so they can point at the wreckage and say, _"See? Only RINOs can win."_ It's a self-fulfilling prophecy.** They know the game. Give conservative voters a choice between a Democrat and a RINO, and we'll hold our nose and vote RINO. But give us a choice between a Democrat and a real conservative, and the establishment would rather watch us lose than let us win on our own terms. It was never about winning a majority; it was about maintaining their control over the party. **Senate Conservatives Fund exists for exactly this fight — to back conservative candidates in the races the party committees have already written off, when the committees would rather protect their own than protect the country.** **[Please join us by supporting Ken Paxton today.](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=f024f5b0298a4d049009d16cd03b697b&_e=lpAZhZGdycXVa60R-K4opMVm_zLsglCS_VB-SYjCJM21t4-8oq8fs0Y0vjkwlgOX1bCTVlniBUDdxNIYcNycc6EkfLfJlpj7jL8lJ9yD-WzIeDzA-GmTnCeEgeJtGSizxxNBxgqbWvwk3TK0kpDoqOkE-jWoAS0ojkCXU-SluEl6ZKr1B_vCG0AACDmyCV4SUotwcmcRNYA9CjqLo7VVppYg4-5zKv1wmU38ABWx5K-H-OnIzz-tdQquxv7M9DanLdVCDZhUpmqN8PK8JgtvlSwjD7stCawVzxe9vgLmZ7i3VTOgwo9BnFNHVWmbHqpMD8tEEQeaByzT9GQmcjGqV3uAnoh3s2iaMTonyfyGrfUNr09DeCrfy9YVH18zPWpf1oH-9RJeExjQJfMcx-F2aQ%3D%3D)** You can donate to SCF to support our independent efforts to elect Ken Paxton, and you can contribute directly to his campaign. clean_body: The RINOs in Texas are still throwing a fit over losing to Ken Paxton. | | | | | Fellow Conservative: Texas is about to decide the fate of the Senate majority — and if we lose it, we won't just lose a seat. We'll hand Democrats their first statewide win in Texas since 1994, and the earthquake will be felt by Americans across the country. First, let's be clear about how we got here. The Republican establishment in DC spent over $150 million — the most expensive Senate primary in American history — trying to stop Ken Paxton from becoming the nominee. They lost. Paxton defeated Sen. John Cornyn by nearly 30 points. But the damage was done, and now Democrat James Talarico is within striking distance of flipping the seat. You'd think Cornyn would be all-in to stop him from turning Texas blue. Nope. Instead, he's trashing Paxton as lazy and a poor campaigner, while telling reporters the party shouldn't spend another dime on his race because of limited resources. That's rich. Even worse, Cornyn is working with former President George W. Bush to pull money out of Texas to fund moderate Senate candidates in other states — many of whom are far bigger underdogs than Paxton. With friends like these, who needs enemies? Ken Paxton has spent over a decade as Texas Attorney General doing what the GOP establishment only talks about. He sued the Biden administration more than any other AG in the country — on the border, on illegal mandates, on federal overreach — and won. While career politicians in Washington cut deals, Paxton has been on the front lines of the fight against the open-borders agenda. President Trump didn't endorse him as an afterthought — he called Paxton a "true MAGA warrior" because Paxton has earned it. That's exactly why the establishment tried to kill his campaign before it started and why they're throwing a temper tantrum now. A real fighter in the Senate threatens the comfortable do-nothing environment they've built in DC. They'd rather have an empty suit who plays along with their empty promises and endless excuses than a conservative who delivers. Make no mistake: John Cornyn and the GOP establishment are working against Paxton because they want Texas to lose. They need it to lose, so they can point at the wreckage and say, "See? Only RINOs can win." It's a self-fulfilling prophecy. They know the game. Give conservative voters a choice between a Democrat and a RINO, and we'll hold our nose and vote RINO. But give us a choice between a Democrat and a real conservative, and the establishment would rather watch us lose than let us win on our own terms. It was never about winning a majority; it was about maintaining their control over the party. Senate Conservatives Fund exists for exactly this fight — to back conservative candidates in the races the party committees have already written off, when the committees would rather protect their own than protect the country. You can donate to SCF to support our independent efforts to elect Ken Paxton, and you can contribute directly to his campaign. It's the best way to help conservatives win in Texas. We are running out of time, so please take action before it's too late. to help Ken Paxton finish this fight — and send the establishment a message they won't forget: their days of picking our nominees for us are over. The future of the Republican Party belongs to conservatives, and we're sending John Cornyn's replacement to Washington. I'm a proud husband and father of three, and I know firsthand what it's like to stress over groceries, healthcare costs, and gas prices. Working families are always the first to feel it when costs go up. I've dedicated my career to public service, as a State Representative, as the Milwaukee County Executive, and soon as Governor. clean_body: Allow me to reintroduce myself: | | | | Hey there, my name is David Crowley, and I'm running to be the next Governor of Wisconsin. Allow me to reintroduce myself: I grew up in one of Milwaukee's poorest zip codes with working-class parents who both struggled with mental health and addiction. I know what hard work looks like. I'm a proud husband and father of three, and I know firsthand what it's like to stress over groceries, healthcare costs, and gas prices. Working families are always the first to feel it when costs go up. I've dedicated my career to public service, as a State Representative, as the Milwaukee County Executive, and soon as Governor. I will never stop fighting for our communities. I'm up against MAGA Congressman Tom Tiffany in November, who is backed by far-right billionaire families, and according to polls, we're locked in a tie. Here is the thing: we know they're going to out-raise us. We just need enough to keep our message on the air until November. Somewhere tonight, a woman is sitting alone with her phone.

She's terrified. Her hands are shaking. She feels like there's only one way out.

And she's typing four words into the search bar that could end everything: _abortion clinic near me. _

[](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckb2u3CAQhZ8Gd7bMmMClcBFp5VQ3uUqTEo1h1kYx4PCz0X37yKt9grTzaT6do_Pr3byjP3zcvmOgeUvnaXIxn6nlkHL0cbPpfieyqR2u4MPACLIfdQ_CoK3-QUZg52aBUkgpO5q50iOoN-Bv3T7fJxCI0spVcLVapDsooZUSTgEHEp2fL-GoQXA9jVwOnGstnLLaSZqU_MLESM7XlIcrW6biHcXq8RhsCt0x77WehU1fGSwMlr0FjDbh4atPcXApplzaeaZcB5sYLCduxGAp-KC-7tSvuH72z6_CpqXVYGyKlWJl0-3bj4-Pn1yAkJqBvFgg51tg040C-uN1LKllS2y67Zgdlt8G7Z8XshhO9Fu8YLPJlLruJrTthSvlS9bl2Z1__XH4IhUT43bJn_Xq_w7ymOFfAAAA__9PS59i)

She doesn't know it yet, but she's about to make a decision she can never undo.

There's another path. But she has to find it first.

A nurse who will sit with her -- not judge her. A free ultrasound where she'll see her baby's heartbeat for the first time.

A single moment where everything shifts, because she stops seeing her baby as a "problem" to solve, but instead sees her baby as a precious life to protect.

That moment only happens if we can reach her before the abortion industry does.

**Since 2009, Human Coalition has rescued over 36,000 children from abortion -- one terrified young woman, one ultrasound, one decision at a time. **

Every single one of those preborn children was saved because a compassionate nurse was waiting before an abortion-determined mom ever picked up the phone.

_Will you help us reach the next mom and save her baby before she walks through the doors of an abortion facility? _

You can help oust him.

If you are unable to see the message below, [click here to view](https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM5Nzg0ODES1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjU0MDQ5NTI1MgS2&mt=1&rt=0).

## _**JON HUSTED: 45% **_
_**SHERROD BROWN 48%**_
_**Source: YouGov, Sept 1-10**_

### **Ohio’s Senate race will be CLOSE. Every voter we can reach matters.**
---
| | [**_Make a contribution to LCV Victory Fund today to help us flip Ohio and take back the Senate >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/ambdF6-)
---
| | Peter, the race for Ohio’s seat in the Senate is heating up — and we won’t sugarcoat this: **there’s a very real possibility incumbent GOP Sen. Jon Husted could win.**
---
| | He has a lifetime score of _just 3%_ on the LCV National Environmental Scorecard. His cozying up to Big Polluters cost Ohioans dearly: after a massive utility bailout, they paid an estimated $663 more a year in electricity.
---
| | He’s known as “the face of data centers in Ohio” and helped hand out tax exemptions to data center companies like candy on Halloween, to the tune of $2.3 billion. **This November,**_**he needs to go. **_
---
| | **Peter — Your contribution goes directly to reaching and turning out voters in swing states just like Ohio, where climate champions are up against some of the worst villains the Senate has to offer.**
---
| | We know a lot of groups will be asking you to pitch in $5 before Election Day, and the truth is that every bit helps. We have a real shot at winning these elections if we can scale up our voter outreach in a major way, but that only happens if some of our most dedicated members make a bigger commitment. So we’re asking:
---
| | [**_Please, rush your urgent contribution of $25 or more today. The impact of your gift will help scale up our work in key races ahead of November’s elections >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.)
---
| | | [LET’S FLIP OHIO >>](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/~)
---
| | We don’t have to wonder what will happen if Husted keeps his seat and MAGA Republicans remain in control of the Senate. They’ve already shown us what they’ll do:
* They will **keep weakening environmental protections** whenever and however they can.
* They will **sell out our public lands** to line the pockets of polluters.
* They will **reduce oversight for power plants, Big Oil, mining, and deepen our country’s dependency on fossil fuels** , at the cost of our environment, our communities, and our pocketbooks.

---
| | **We know we can beat him.** Our research shows that 42% of swing voters are “very concerned” about rising electricity bills, and that our messaging — focused on lowering costs with clean energy — moves them 7% toward supporting environmental champions.
---
| | _These “energy bill voters” will be decisive in close races this fall and these are the voters we need to reach._ **We** _**can**_**vote Husted out — but it requires resources. **
---
| | [**_And right now, your contribution of $25 or more is urgently needed to help LCV Victory Fund:_**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/k_ypT7-)
---
| | ✅ Mobilize the 51% of undecided voters who are fed up with their energy bills rising higher and higher while oil and gas companies are raking in record profits
✅ Elect pro-democracy, pro-environment candidates in federal, state, and local races that can provide a backstop against Trump’s unchecked federal power
✅ Reach voters by calling, knocking on doors, texting, and running ads to make sure people know what’s at stake in November
✅ Canvass as hard as we can to reach voters in key battleground races
---
| | [**_Rush your contribution today >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.)
---
| | We know that we can do this, but we have to do it together. Thank you, Peter, for everything you do.
---
| | The LCV Victory Fund Team

**Receipts 1.5: Access Denied**
The Iron Triangle's gatekeeping architecture narrows the field.
The harm of a curated field is not a private grievance. It is a public injury. The Lake Federated Republican Women's Club showed us how the "pretext of process" works within party infrastructures designed for exclusion. But what happens when that same mechanism moves into the public square, onto the airwaves we all share? What happens when the gatekeeper is not a club, but a television station licensed to serve the public?
## **WESH: The Public Trust, Betrayed**
The Iron Triangle does not limit its operations to the private halls of party clubs. Some of its most consequential work takes place in the open, on the public airwaves, under the banner of neutrality. The architecture of gatekeeping is not reserved for insiders; it affects voters.
On July 10, 2026, WESH 2 News televised the Republican primary debate for Florida's 11th Congressional District. Three candidates stood at their podiums. You may have watched. If you did, you saw a debate. What you did not see was the entire qualified field.
Five Republicans qualified for the ballot. Three appeared on stage. According to WESH, one candidate declined the invitation and one did not respond.
A viewer could reasonably conclude that two candidates themselves had forfeited the opportunity for exposure. But that conclusion would depend on the accuracy of WESH's account of whom it contacted and what happened next.
I was the candidate identified as having failed to respond. But how could I respond to an invitation they never extended to me?
I contacted WESH on July 11 and requested a correction. I received no acknowledgment, no correction, and no explanation. I set a deadline of July 18. WESH did not respond.
The result was that WESH presented viewers with information that, according to the record I subsequently obtained, was inaccurate.
**Viewers deserved a complete and accurate account.** Broadcasting that a candidate was invited when, in fact, the candidate was not invited **raises a serious question about the accuracy of the station 's account and the responsibility that comes with its public role.**
The consequences extended beyond my campaign. They affected you, the voter.
WESH owed its viewers a complete and accurate account: Five candidates qualified to be on the ballot. Three were invited and accepted. Another was invited but declined. One was never invited.
WESH did not correct the record before the vote. I am correcting it now by presenting the evidence.
## **The Paper Trail**
On July 22, twelve days after the broadcast, I filed a complaint with the Federal Communications Commission (FCC)--Ticket No. 8922909. The FCC forwarded the complaint to WESH on July 28. By the morning of August 5, no response had been received, so I submitted a status request to the FCC. That afternoon, at 4:24 p.m., WESH responded through its attorneys.
It was in that response that a fuller picture emerged--not from watching the broadcast, not from comparing notes with other campaigns, but from a regulatory inquiry that required the station to put its process on paper.
What they documented also made clear what had not been done.
## **What Their Response Revealed**
The record shows one unsuccessful contact attempt, then exclusion, then criteria that were stated after the fact. Those criteria were not disclosed to viewers at the start of the broadcast, and the station's response did not identify them with the specificity one would expect from criteria described as "pre-established."
The June 26 call they referenced--the call that the debate moderator characterized as an "invitation"--was placed to the wrong number. The voicemail at that number did not identify as a campaign. WESH left no message to Ivette Palomo. They did not call back. They did not try the email address listed on the same candidate qualifying form they had used to find the phone number. They made one attempt, to the wrong number, and stopped.
The station then excluded me from the podium. When asked to explain that exclusion, it cited "pre-established criteria" but did not name them. It referenced "contemporaneous internal notes" of the June 26 call. Those notes have not been produced.
They described what they found: no campaign social media accounts, no fundraising, no significant campaign activity.
WESH's August 5 legal response makes another significant claim. It states that its "research demonstrated that Ms. Palomo had not been hosting or featured during any campaign events." Yet Footnote 3 of that same response acknowledges that "Station personnel observed Ms. Palomo appeared at some public events involving other candidates."
Those two statements do not sit comfortably together. WESH's own response acknowledges that station personnel had observed me at public events, while its stated justification for excluding me relied on the assertion that I had not been hosting or featured at campaign events.
The distinction matters. WESH had information showing that I was publicly participating in campaign-related events, yet that information did not appear in the explanation it gave for my exclusion.
I had filed with the Federal Election Commission (FEC). I had maintained an active campaign bank account. I had qualified as a candidate with the State of Florida. Those facts established my status as a qualified candidate. They did not, by themselves, establish an entitlement to a place on WESH's debate stage. But that is not the argument I am making. The question is what standards WESH used to decide who would be included, whether those standards were established in advance, and whether they were applied transparently and consistently.
I had also participated in two forums and several other events before their broadcast. I had opened social media accounts specifically for the campaign. These were my methods of campaigning--grassroots methods, the methods of a candidate who builds from the ground up rather than from the top down.
When pressed for the basis of my exclusion, WESH cited the absence of social media accounts, fundraising, and significant campaign activity--criteria that, on the record available to me, were not disclosed to viewers before the debate and were invoked only after my exclusion.
That distinction matters. WESH had the discretion to establish editorial criteria for its debate. But discretion is not the same as transparency. If criteria determine who gets access to a public-facing political forum, the question is not merely whether the station may exercise editorial judgment. The question is whether the basis for that judgment was clear, consistently applied, and accurately described after the fact.
Consider the contradiction. The moderator framed this debate as a service to voters: "This is another in our series of debates to bring the candidates closer to you as we get closer to the primary election, August 18." Yet the very institution claiming to serve that purpose appears to have ended its effort to reach one qualified candidate after a single unsuccessful telephone attempt.
I submit all of this as a matter of record: the FCC complaint file, WESH's attorney response, phone records showing no call from WESH on June 26, campaign screenshots, Spectrum News correspondence, WESH's original on-air claim, and qualifying petition signatures. All submitted August 7 in a 17-section response with nine exhibits.
## **What Other Outlets Found**
The Sumter GOP contacted me via phone and email, then on July 3 included all five Republican candidates in the forum in Wildwood. Spectrum News reached me by email at two addresses, and I, along with Republican and Democrat candidates, participated in their televised Community Conversation on July 29. These were not extraordinary efforts. They were the minimum--a phone call to the right number, an email to a listed address, and a single follow-up.
The difference between WESH and these outlets was not that I was harder to reach. It was the effort made to reach me.
WESH also told you that District 11 "covers part of Volusia County and Seminole County." The district actually consists of all of Sumter County and parts of Orange and Lake counties. If WESH's standard was rigorous reporting, its own description of the district raises another question: where was that same rigor applied to its account of the candidates who were considered for its debate?
## **The Silence After**
By the 14th of August, 35 days had passed since the exclusion and the broadcast, seven days since WESH's response to the FCC, and four days remained before the primary.
I followed up with the FCC on August 10 and again on August 14. There was still no acknowledgment of the concerns I had raised, no correction from WESH, and no public clarification before voters went to the polls.
The timing matters.
The opportunity to correct the record existed before the primary. The information was on paper. The evidence had been submitted. Yet the record remained unchanged as voters prepared to make their choice.
That silence did not simply concern my campaign. It left voters with the same incomplete account they had been given on July 10.
## **What Was Lost**
The loss of the debate appearance exists for me as a qualified candidate. Yet you lost something greater, and it deserves to be named precisely.
What was taken was not a podium. It was an opportunity for voters to know that another qualified candidate was in the field--and that the reason given for her absence was disputed by the record. Three candidates were presented as the field. Five had qualified. One was not invited. And the public was not given a correction before the vote explaining that distinction.
And you lost something harder to name--the assumption that the institutions presenting you with information are operating in your interest, not their own narrative. The presumption that when a station tells you someone did not respond, they had actually tried to reach them. The trust that a debate is a service to voters and not a curated product.
The issue, then, is not whether WESH was required to invite every qualified candidate. It is whether the process by which it selected candidates--and the explanation it gave voters for one candidate's absence--was accurate, transparent, and consistently applied.
When the record is viewed in its entirety, that is the question the station's response leaves behind.
## **Silence Serves the Architecture**
At that point, the question is no longer simply whether a communication failed. The record shows a sequence: an unsuccessful contact attempt, exclusion from the debate, criteria invoked afterward, and no correction of the resulting account before voters went to the polls.
That is the mechanism of gatekeeping: the field is narrowed, the basis for the narrowing is difficult for the public to see, and the resulting field can appear complete even when it is not.
## **The Pattern of the Gatekeepers**
Consider the pattern:
* Qualified candidates are included or excluded.
* The criteria for inclusion or exclusion may not be visible to the public.
* The exclusion itself may be invisible to the public because the public sees only the resulting field.

The public is left to believe that WESH offered all qualified candidates an equal opportunity to be considered.
That is the pattern of gatekeeping: **control the selection, conceal or obscure the criteria, conceal the exclusion, and preserve the appearance of an open process.**
And this pattern is not limited to one election or one domain. It appears wherever the Iron Triangle operates.
Many who experience it do not speak out. Sometimes because they know retaliation is real. Sometimes because they lack the evidence to prove what happened. And sometimes because the process is designed so that the exclusion itself is difficult to see.
I spoke out because silence serves the architecture of the Iron Triangle.
## **The Cost of Defiance**
Retaliation is not some abstract idea either. For those who challenge institutions with power, the risk of retaliation can be real. Those who refuse to bend get pushed out of the very institutions that claim to serve us. As a whistleblower, I learned to end every communication with the portion of law that prohibits retaliation. Not as a formality, but as a reminder that retaliation is illegal--and that I knew it.
The law was my shield. The evidence was my sword. Without both of them, the silence would have won.
## **Reclaiming the Choice**
The field is shaped by those who decide who gets heard and who gets silenced. Our consent is presumed by those who never bothered to ask. Access is denied by those who claim neutrality. The information we needed as citizens was withheld. The choice we deserved was eliminated.
But I am naming it now--so you know what happened, so we can talk about it together, here at the kitchen table, without fear.
## **The Seizure of Sovereignty**
On August 18, voters in District 11 went to the polls with information that had been shaped before they ever had the opportunity to consider the full field. This was not simply a matter of what appeared on a ballot. It was a matter of what voters were given the opportunity to know before making their choice.
The voters still made their own decision. That decision was theirs. But the conditions under which they made it had already been shaped by information they were given--and information they were not given.
They were not alone. The same pattern can occur whenever a voter, member, or citizen is asked to make a decision from information that has already been filtered by an institution claiming neutrality. The decision may still be theirs, but the conditions under which they made it were not.
The Iron Triangle does not need your informed consent. It needs your trust. But trust is not consent. When you trust an institution to tell you the truth, you have not given it permission to disguise the truth. When you trust an institution to present you with the information you need to make a decision, you have not consented to having that information withheld.
Consent cannot be presumed simply because trust was given. And trust cannot be used to legitimize an action to which no one ever consented.
## **People 's Sovereignty**
The process is not the "process." The process is the pretext.
The Constitution rests on a framework of consent and accountability. The Iron Triangle operates outside that framework--a shadow system that can mimic the forms of governance while obscuring who is actually exercising control. It does not operate by the law of the land, but by the **law of the loop.**
Think about the family at the kitchen table. They are not merely a collection of voters. They are sovereign in the decisions that govern their own lives. The table is where decisions are made, values are taught, and fairness is defined. When an institution presumes to decide which candidates matter or which information reaches that family, it does not merely inconvenience them. It shapes the information from which that family must make its choice.
The Iron Triangle bets that the family will not notice the "process." It bets that exhaustion will substitute for consent. And when it does, it weakens the very values and familial bonds that allow a family to stand, to choose, and to resist. That is the greater harm.
But the family that gathers at this table has the capacity to see the pattern. The record exists. The right to refuse a pretext that was never authorized does not come from any institution. It belongs to the people before any institution claims the authority to take it.
The kitchen table belongs to the families who gather around it--not to party organizations that decide who gets a seat before the meal is served, and not to corporations that curate the truth.
The family that sees the deception can refuse the pretext. The family that refuses can hold these institutions to the standards they claim to uphold. And the family that holds them accountable can reclaim its right to choose.
The point is not that an institution must give us the choice we want. It is that no institution should quietly decide which choices we are permitted to see and then present that narrowed field as though nothing has been removed.
That is why the record matters. That is why the correction matters. And that is why the choice belongs to the people--not to the gatekeeper.
**Consent was presumed. Access was denied.**

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: I know it’s late, but I have to tell you something
body:
Hi Peter, it’s Gina.

I know it is late, but I couldn’t go to sleep tonight without writing to
you personally.

Recent polls show us leading Greg Abbott. NPR/Marist has us at 49% and
Abbott behind at 46%. This is the second poll in less than a week showing
us ahead, and I wanted you to hear it directly from me.

When we started this campaign, the pundits said flipping Texas was
impossible. But because of people like you, the electoral landscape in
Texas is shifting beneath our feet. We brought this race to a tie, and now
we’ve taken the lead.

I’d love to celebrate this moment, but I have to be completely honest
about what we are facing tonight.

Greg Abbott just unleashed a massive $12 million wave of attack ads
against our campaign. It’s his first negative ad spending of the entire
race, and it proves how terrified he is of losing. He has decades of big
donor money stored up, and he’s going to spend whatever it takes to try to
erase our lead.

Tonight at midnight is our official Texas Ethics Commission deadline.

This TEC deadline is our second to last official reporting deadline before
Election Day, and the numbers we report at midnight will show the whole
country whether we have the resources to hit back on TV and defend our
lead.

subject: My time is not up.

body:
|
#
---
_Peter, this is Mazie. My friend Cory Booker is running for reelection for the Senate in New Jersey to help us retake the majority. Please read his message below, and I hope you'll consider joining me in supporting his campaign._
* * *
Peter, part of my job as a senator is asking questions to make sure that the government is working in your best interest. _Recently, doing my job meant coming face to face with Donald Trump’s hand-picked crony to lead the FBI, Kash Patel._ Kash Patel has been using FBI resources — your tax dollars — to spoil himself, his friends and his girlfriend. Even worse, instead of impartially enforcing the law, he’s acting as Donald Trump’s henchman and harassing journalists who dare to hold them accountable. subject: Something I've learned in politics

body:
Nothing changes when everyone waits for somebody else to do it. |
#
---
Folks, One thing I’ve learned in politics is that it’s always easier to sit back. It’s easy to assume someone else will make the calls, knock the doors, run for office, or step up when it matters. But _nothing_ changes when everyone waits for somebody else to do it. Change happens when people decide to show up. I’ve seen it happen in Michigan — people organizing in their communities, fighting for reproductive freedom, standing up for working families, and refusing to give up when the odds are tough. **We don’t need everyone to do everything. name: Team Pou
subject: What winning here means for the House
body:
Control of the House could come down to this seat

| |
---
Friend, Control of the House of Representatives could come down to a small number of seats this November, and NJ-09 is one of them. If Democrats hold this district, it's not just a win for New Jersey. It's a seat in the column that could decide who sets the agenda in Washington for the next two years: who chairs committees, what bills get a vote, and whether there's any real check on the current administration. * **Losers?** Amazon's walled checkout, plus Schwab, LPL, Booking, and Expedia the middlemen the agent just walked around. The privacy tab printed up to $17 billion.

# The dollar parked at a two-month high and the 5-year just screamed 2007
The dollar clung to a two-month high at 101.1 after a hot PMI and a weak five-year auction shoved those notes through 5% for the first time since 2007. Euro $1.1378, a two-month low. Sterling $1.3231, a three-month nadir. Barr flagged more hikes. FedWatch now prices a nearly 70% October tightening, up from 50% last week.
* **Winners?** Dollar longs, money-market funds, and anyone sitting in cash-like duration while five-years clear 5%. Relative U.S. growth is still the bid.
* **Losers?** Euro, sterling, yen at 157.9, and every importer who priced a dovish Fed. Weak five-year demand just taxed the curve.
* **Next?** October hike goes live if oil stays bid after Iran's "never surrender" and Trump's diesel export ban. Watch the next coupon auction.

This is not a dead-cat bounce. Five-years just joined. Own the currency. Fade the cut choir

# Hyundai is about to outsell Ford because Detroit forgot how to build a hybrid
Cox says Hyundai will print 511,421 units in Q3, up 6.5%, against Ford at 504,172, down 7.1% -- first time Hyundai outsells Ford in a quarter. That puts Seoul third behind GM and Toyota. Gas is $4.48. GM's hybrid is a Corvette. Ford's are a Maverick and an F-150. Cox raised 2026 about 2% to 16.1 million.
* **Winners?** Hyundai, Kia, Genesis, and Toyota at 642,707, up 2.2%, now within 121,100 of GM's 671,706. Hybrids are eating $4.48 gasoline for lunch.
* **Losers?** Ford after two supplier fires, GM down 5.2% to 671,706, and Detroit's V8 swagger. The Sep 17 pack already flagged those Gen 6 Silverado and Sierra V8s.
* **Next?** Toyota can steal the annual crown for only the second time since 2021 if the hybrid gap stays open into Q4. Watch F-Series recovery.

Muñoz says beating Ford "isn't a goal." The scoreboard does not care. Cox just called Detroit's product choices "interesting" after they put V8s back in the Silverado and Sierra while $4.48 gas paid Hyundai's invoice. I flagged those Gen 6 V8s on the Sep 17 tape. Build the hybrid or lose the lot.

* * *
# Zuck wants $1,299 for VR glasses that still need a puck in your pocket
Connect handed you the hardware sequel. Meta VR Glasses at $1,299, spring 2027 -- slimmer than Quest, first VR box since the $299 Quest 3S in 2024. Compute and battery sit in an external Qualcomm puck. Eye and hand tracking, no controllers. Muse Charm talks to the agent without unlocking a phone. Holiday ship. No price.
* **Winners?** Qualcomm inside the puck, and Muse if the glasses become the interface Mizuho called the clearest consumer AI use case yet.
* **Losers?** Anyone who thought the metaverse died. Also the $299 Quest buyer who just learned the next pair costs $1,299 and still needs a brick in the pocket.
* **Next?** Charm ships for the holidays if they finish "laying out the components." Glasses are a spring 2027 SKU. Downloads were the teaser. Wear time is the print.

This is the ship-while-they-preach tape I called in **[The AI Extinction Circus is in town](https://substack.com/redirect/43786f91-ab9a-4087-9737-ec8c18e453ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).** Amodei and Altman want a slowdown. Zuckerberg put a $1,299 pair of glasses and a talking pendant on the table. Hardware is how he turns Muse from an App Store spike into a daily habit.

# Cracker Barrel is selling the land to pay the tab after the rebrand hangover
Deno, CEO since August after Masino's rebrand blew up, is upgrading chicken, hamburger, and steak because dinner is "the biggest opportunity." He sold 26 company-owned stores in a sale-leaseback for about $77 million, paid the $150 million 0.625% converts that matured in June, and cut debt to $337.2 million, $147.4 million below last year. Average check is about $16. Low-income guests still pinched.
* **Winners?** Lenders. Debt is $147.4 million lighter. Deno's "fewer things better" pitch beats another logo. The $16 check still works for squeezed wallets.
* **Losers?** The old real-estate stack, and Masino's $700 million overhaul that yanked the Old Timer then put it back. Low-income traffic is still the soft spot.
* **Next?** Food quality has to show up in traffic before the next sale-leaseback looks like a business plan. Fuel surcharges already sit in the FY27 outlook.

I flagged this endgame in **[Cracker Barrel's "Bud Light" disaster just got a whole lot worse](https://substack.com/redirect/bc5efc71-909c-45c7-9262-9e4feca76474?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** when I said the attraction was "liquidation of the real estate on which many CB stores sit." The 26-roof, $77 million sale-leaseback is that call on the tape. **[Cracker Barrel's woke hangover disaster continues](https://substack.com/redirect/5dea6f5f-686f-4ff2-816c-3e4ddea8fee3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** already had the customers walking. Deno is flipping steaks and dirt. That's the clean-up, not the all-clear.

Capital Rotation — September 24, 2026
The Yield Move Was Broad. That Makes It Harder to Reverse.
Five different Treasury maturities hit 52-week highs on the same day a new oil-supply risk emerged in Libya — a broad, structural move that looks less like a reaction to one headline and more like a genuine repricing.
|
---
| | What Moved
---|---
**Verified fact:** Wednesday was a broad risk-off session — the S&P; 500 fell 0.73%, the Dow fell 0.63%, the Nasdaq fell 1.11%, and the Russell 2000 led losses at 1.60% — as the 5-year Treasury yield touched 5.036% intraday, its highest since 2007, with new 52-week highs across the 3-, 5-, 7-, 10-, and 20-year maturities. WTI crude fell 0.97% to $89.64 and Brent fell 0.24% to $99.01, even as Libya's Sharara field disruption introduced a fresh, geographically distinct supply risk.
| | Rotation Signal 01 — A Broad-Based Yield Move Is a Different Animal Than a Single-Maturity Spike
---|---
**Our interpretation:** new 52-week highs across five different Treasury maturities simultaneously, rather than an isolated move at just the 10-year point this newsletter tracked two weeks ago, suggests markets are repricing the entire discount-rate environment, not reacting to one specific headline. This kind of broad move tends to be stickier and harder to reverse on diplomatic news alone than a single-point spike.
| | Rotation Signal 02 — Libya Adds a Genuinely Separate Supply Risk Just as Middle East Risk Was Easing
---|---
**Verified fact:** an armed group shut the pipeline valve connecting Libya's largest oil field, Al-Sharara, to its Zawiya export terminal, with the National Oil Corporation warning of a possible force majeure declaration. **Our interpretation:** this is worth tracking as its own line item, separate from the Hormuz and pipeline stories that have dominated this newsletter's energy coverage — a reminder that global oil supply carries multiple, independent points of failure, and that de-escalation in one region does not eliminate risk from another.
| | Rotation Signal 03 — The Selloff Preceded Two Major Catalysts Rather Than Following Them
---|---
**Current classification: PRESSURE, ahead of two unresolved events.** Wednesday's broad decline occurred before today's Trump-Xi summit and before any concrete outcome from the reported US-Iran back-channel talks — consistent with markets de-risking ahead of uncertain catalysts rather than reacting to bad news that has already occurred.
| | What to Watch Today
---|---
Whether Thursday's Trump-Xi summit outcome, and any further detail on the reported US-Iran talks, reverse Wednesday's broad risk-off move or confirm it as the start of a more sustained repricing.

subject: Wall Street should not own our hospitals
body:
Tonight, Chester is holding a town hall on the hospital crisis private equity left behind. Have their backs | |
---
Peter, **In Chester, Pennsylvania residents lost their trauma center, their burn unit, and thousands of health care jobs. Tonight, OnePA’s Chester chapter is bringing neighbors together at a town hall meeting to demand that elected officials stop selling off our hospitals.** We already lived the private equity playbook in Delaware County. Prospect Medical Holdings bought Crozer Health in 2016 while controlled by Leonard Green & Partners. Investors pulled hundreds of millions out. The hospital's real estate was sold. The system was loaded with more than $200 million in mortgage debt. **A promise to keep Crozer open for at least 10 years was broken. All 4 Crozer hospitals closed. More than 3,000 health care workers lost their jobs. A county of 576,000 people that once had 6 hospitals was left with just 2.** Now, a New York investment firm, Chariot Equities, has bought the empty Crozer-Chester Medical Center campus for $10 million. Chester members have already collected 500 signatures demanding a binding 10-year commitment to stay, open books on the company’s finances, and brick-and-mortar 24/7 trauma and specialty care units. **People are being forced to travel farther for emergency and specialty care, while hospitals sit in investors' hands. Chester is doing the work tonight. Our state capitols still have to pass the law that stops the next raid.** [**Tell your state legislators to pass a moratorium on private equity purchases of hospitals and protect community health care from corporate extraction.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39TyzbXIpOoq2iqzYMm8391MGwtxxepouc_6AYtC3AHXNCmTeS9sx6zodarSteAyKVv2UthW1sdHG9_QsaMld60T5aNmxLxhzRPY8OAEWY0b5wZ8Db_eilpZ_XKrCoLVOY5qq3BrrOynlcBhBzjhVpIG21ex0WuowTEVBFETXv1u3MBaiy0-CJJPvLkzzQY4Yk4IzQY0GI06P3K5n9iG3QSYw9LxpfwnJV-nXXSJP471WG3jj0Fmxt3qWaza8acCdpQ5Wu-fBqS-LxK0qT91ZHO38Iz28xphV1PLYlYMebpOM_vcbetq_2wVXThjVbYOsmtkdEXdXP9FGWfiHKam3mM8z5yq7E9tgL8vF4JzEh06NfdkAY7YbJXIm4lLu5Mb3PWjqpa2eof_sglpwoxWPixib28LR_aj83udC_0UHQuvYmBbS2zXUyxu8Uuf_PgiXw/4ub/qHi_h3m8Q7OwEB_fiHGKXw/h0/h001.t4Y5HOgaBnUBQk7-ze9tUvAnluneYfRdOENMkmHw824) | | [SIGN & SEND](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39TyzbXIpOoq2iqzYMm8391MGwtxxepouc_6AYtC3AHXNCmTeS9sx6zodarSteAyKVv2UthW1sdHG9_QsaMld60T5aNmxLxhzRPY8OAEWY0b5wZ8Db_eilpZ_XKrCoLVOY5qq3BrrOynlcBhBzjhVpIG21ex0WuowTEVBFETXv1u3MBaiy0-CJJPvLkzzQY4Yk4IzQY0GI06P3K5n9iG3QSX1-5p3_zmnLZUYkYXC-_fhzP7upYcetn7vBdqItST6aIxi4QInULq-WU2bGbLTqRyVh7CYLWd9Ab7VAUj2rsimL9Kj15zEASfpKCbbzrSKD2DwkVRbXSm-SP7FYUuQIVNjM4rsttcuQXdQ3y_9tzj6hGLZgjOMfZqfefc9RhecGKVp98qh9K36E-A6ag4SJn6BojzFSkwn21AysAdi0uvx5K-u5Yzk4tsfFAuIMXBaw/4ub/qHi_h3m8Q7OwEB_fiHGKXw/h1/h001.Rwvw9-4gLk5Y4w87fSH0k_TGp-jOiMSb9S8KCqa2Dho)

name: Chris Pappas
subject: My decision
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=9121%2E582294%2EVQdwSo ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=9121%2E582294%2EVQdwSo ]Chris Pappas for Senate

When I first ran for Congress, I made the decision that I wouldn't take a
dime of corporate PAC money.

Not because I thought it would make campaigns easier. And not because I
believed everyone else had to make the same decision.

I made that commitment because I wanted Granite Staters to know exactly
where my priorities would lie as their representative.

Granite Staters responded to that choice. They saw it was proof that I was
serious about changing the culture in Washington.

New Hampshire is a purple state. Every race here is competitive. And over
the years, I've heard more than a few people suggest that refusing
corporate PAC money meant competing with one hand tied behind my back.

But four tough congressional races later, we've shown something important:
You can build a winning campaign the right way.

I believe public service is about serving the public.

People deserve leaders who are accountable to the communities they
represent — especially in this current moment.

Now we are facing our biggest test yet: Control of the Senate could come
down to New Hampshire, and Republicans and their allies are already
preparing to spend millions of dollars to flip this seat.

Rhetoric Hit a New High. So Did a Claimed Private Breakthrough. Both on the Same Day.
Mutual UN walkouts, a claimed 'very productive' back-channel, a broad Treasury yield surge, and a new oil-supply shock out of Libya — four independent developments that all pointed toward caution within one 24-hour window.

| | The Setup
---|---
This newsletter's Tuesday and Wednesday editions each documented a widening gap between public rhetoric and the underlying trajectory of events. Wednesday sharpened that pattern further — the harshest rhetorical exchange yet, a mutual diplomatic walkout, and a claimed private breakthrough, all within a single 24-hour window, arriving the day before a second major summit with its own independent stakes.
| | Development One — The Public Exchange Escalated to Mutual Walkouts
---|---
**Verified fact:** Pezeshkian told the UN General Assembly that Trump “called us terrorists but we are the victims of terrorists,” and that Iranian resistance “will only grow in the face of sanctions,” displaying images including assassinated Supreme Leader Khamenei and children reportedly killed in U.S. strikes. U.S. and Israeli delegations walked out during his remarks, mirroring Iran's walkout during Trump's speech the previous day. **Our interpretation:** two consecutive days of mutual walkouts is a harder, more symmetrical signal of diplomatic rupture than anything this newsletter has documented in this conflict to date.
| | Development Two — The Same Speech Contained a Genuine Opening
---|---
**Verified fact:** in the same address, Pezeshkian said “Iran extends its hands towards the world” and suggested flexibility on a framework beyond the expired June ceasefire memorandum. Separately, Trump described ongoing U.S.-Iran negotiations as “very productive.” **Our interpretation:** holding a defiant public posture and a genuine private opening simultaneously is not new for this conflict, but Wednesday is the clearest case yet of both appearing within the same address and the same day — strong evidence that public rhetoric on both sides now serves a domestic and symbolic purpose distinct from the actual negotiating track.
| | Development Three — A New Supply Risk Entered From an Entirely Different Geography
---|---
**Verified fact:** an armed group shut the pipeline connecting Libya's largest oil field to its export terminal, with Libya's National Oil Corporation warning of a possible force majeure declaration. **Our interpretation:** this is a useful reminder that this newsletter's month-long focus on Middle East chokepoints should not be mistaken for the totality of oil-supply risk. body:
Three states are about to decide a lot more than 2026.

| | | |
---
Friend,
---
We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let me explain why they matter so much... _

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Here's why... Winning the presidency comes down to 270 electoral votes. Lose Arizona and most of the realistic paths to the White House in 2028 are gone. Lose Nevada and New Hampshire and the Left rebuilds the Blue Wall they lost in 2024.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.

Fellow Conservative: Texas is about to decide the fate of the Senate majority — and if we lose it, we won't just lose a seat. We'll hand Democrats their first statewide win in Texas since 1994, and the earthquake will be felt by Americans across the country. First, let's be clear about how we got here. The Republican establishment in DC spent over $150 million — the most expensive Senate primary in American history — trying to stop Ken Paxton from becoming the nominee. _They lost._ Paxton defeated Sen. John Cornyn by nearly 30 points. But the damage was done, and now Democrat James Talarico is within striking distance of flipping the seat. You'd think Cornyn would be all-in to stop him from turning Texas blue. Nope. Instead, he's trashing Paxton as lazy and a poor campaigner, while telling reporters the party shouldn't spend another dime on his race because of limited resources. That's rich. **Even worse, Cornyn is working with former President George W. Bush to pull money out of Texas to fund moderate Senate candidates in other states — many of whom are far bigger underdogs than Paxton.** With friends like these, who needs enemies?

| Peter,
I'm a farmer, so I know BS when I see it. So believe me when I say:
If I get my name ID up, we flip this.
A NEW POLL just dropped showing us trailing by 5. Here's what they buried in the fine print: less than 45% of Louisiana voters even know who I am.
Every time we get my story and our vision for a better Louisiana in front of a Louisiana voter -- at the door, on the phone, on their screen -- our numbers improve. When people learn what I stand for, they're with us.
My name is Jamie Davis. My grandfather picked cotton on this Delta soil as a sharecropper. My son and I farm those same fields today. When I win November 3rd, I'll be Louisiana's first Black Senator since Reconstruction.
But I can't win a race voters haven't heard of yet. That changes right now. We are launching a massive grassroots voter contact push -- 40 days, every parish, every door. But we need the resources to make it happen.

Peter,

Everyone pretends to be an influencer from their armchair. But here's the reality behind who influences elections the most. The answer may surprise you...
>>> It's not Taylor Swift.

>>> It's not celebrities giving Oscar speeches.

>>> It's not TikTok influencers.
Here's the answer:**It 's ballot chasers**. Real people, in real neighborhoods, knocking on real doors. Meeting voters. Getting to know them. Chasing every single ballot until it's cast.

That's how we won in 2024 for President Trump.

It's how we'll win in 2026, and it's how we'll win in 2028.

Young and energetic people knocking on doors works! It's the biggest influencer in elections.

So you may think to yourself: _" If it works so well, why isn't everyone doing this?" _

Good question. Here's the truth:

__This is hard work! It takes training. It takes time. And yes, it takes funding_._

body:
What Today’s Decision Means

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1NbA5hYazU7?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)
| |

Friends,
**Today the California Supreme Court made their ruling on our legal ballot investigation into voter fraud. Here’s what you should know.**
The Justices ruled that the **AG can terminate legal and warrant approved investigations** , conducted by elected Sheriff’s. In other words, the AG now has unchecked power over any investigation in the state of California.
---
| | | | | [Support Bianco](https://us.list-manage.com/5GiTOiYLCid?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)
---
| | **Here is what the ruling fails to address** : citizens in Riverside County found a 45,896-ballot gap between the certified tally and the records they pulled from the Registrar.
The Registrar said it was a paperwork error.**Bonta said stop looking**.
I got warrants from a judge and started looking anyway.**That is my job**.

They called it “unprecedented.” Good. Most people in power never get asked hard questions about an election. I asked them. For that, the Court handed Bonta the power to pause a local criminal investigation and lock the evidence behind the Registrar.
I will obey the writs. I will not obey the message behind them — that local law enforcement works for Sacramento, not for the people who elected us.
**My message to Bonta is simple** : you may have succeeded in burying the truth—for now. But nothing stays hidden forever. In time, everything comes to light.
Thank you,**— Sheriff Chad Bianco**

Somewhere tonight, a woman is sitting alone with her phone.

She's terrified. Her hands are shaking. She feels like there's only one way out.

And she's typing four words into the search bar that could end everything: _abortion clinic near me. _

She doesn't know it yet, but she's about to make a decision she can never undo.

There's another path. But she has to find it first.

A nurse who will sit with her -- not judge her. A free ultrasound where she'll see her baby's heartbeat for the first time.

A single moment where everything shifts, because she stops seeing her baby as a "problem" to solve, but instead sees her baby as a precious life to protect.

That moment only happens if we can reach her before the abortion industry does.

**Since 2009, Human Coalition has rescued over 36,000 children from abortion -- one terrified young woman, one ultrasound, one decision at a time. **

Every single one of those preborn children was saved because a compassionate nurse was waiting before an abortion-determined mom ever picked up the phone.

_Will you help us reach the next mom and save her baby before she walks through the doors of an abortion facility? _

Her hands are shaking. She feels like there's only one way out. And she's typing four words into the search bar that could end everything: abortion clinic near me. She doesn't know it yet, but she's about to make a decision she can never undo. There's another path. But she has to find it first. A nurse who will sit with her -- not judge her. A free ultrasound where she'll see her baby's heartbeat for the first time. A single moment where everything shifts, because she stops seeing her baby as a "problem" to solve, but instead sees her baby as a precious life to protect. That moment only happens if we can reach her before the abortion industry does. Since 2009, Human Coalition has rescued over 36,000 children from abortion -- one terrified young woman, one ultrasound, one decision at a time. Every single one of those preborn children was saved because a compassionate nurse was waiting before an abortion-determined mom ever picked up the phone. Will you help us reach the next mom and save her baby before she walks through the doors of an abortion facility? Friend, your gift of any amount to Human Coalition today claims your "Save the Baby Humans" mug. But, before you donate, you should know this... Every $26 you give today helps us reach another abortion-determined woman and connects her with one of Human Coalition's pro-life nurses. And if you are able to, a gift of $202 not only helps us connect with another mom, but also helps fully cover the cost of her appointment and ultrasound to see her growing child in the womb. Whatever amount you choose is up to you, and every little bit counts. But please know, your action today means a young mom will know there's more options besides abortion. Hey folks,
The midterms are getting closer, and the warning signs for Republicans are getting harder to ignore.
In this episode, I break down a stunning CNN polling segment on Donald Trump and independent voters, the Republican candidates suddenly distancing themselves from Trump and the Iran war, and what I'm seeing in races that weren't supposed to be competitive.
This one gets wild.
* [**00:01:51**] CNN breaks down Trump's numbers with "pure independents"--including an enormous shift from the 2024 election.
* [**00:03:33**] I dig into what these numbers could mean for Democrats in the midterms--and why I think the potential political environment could extend well beyond the usual battlegrounds.
* [**00:06:18**] The fractures get more serious as Republican senators call for an investigation involving Donald Trump Jr. and his dealings.
* [**00:08:36**] We go down ballot, where Republican candidates are distancing themselves from Trump--including changes to Byron Donalds' campaign website in Florida.
* [**00:10:13**] A reality check: encouraging polling doesn't win elections. There's still time left, and Democrats can't get complacent or stop doing the work.

There's a lot happening here: independents moving sharply against Trump in the polling discussed in the episode, Republican candidates changing their positioning, and increasingly competitive races across the map. But none of that means the outcome is predetermined. We still have to organize, stay engaged, and run through the tape. This is a real match. A small group of dedicated donors came together and pooled their resources to make this month's match possible. They believe so strongly in electing Democratic pro-choice women up and down the ballot that they put up the funds to triple your impact — dollar for dollar. But here's the thing: Their generosity only reaches its full power if grassroots supporters like you step up. We have a $500,000 goal to hit over the next week. That's the only way we can unlock the full $1.5 million in support of our entire slate of Democratic pro-choice women running to take back power. = | = Thanks for your support, the EMILYs List Digital team \-------------Original Message------------- Sent: Wednesday, September 23, 2026 From: EMILYs List Digital Team = Hey Peter, It's just over a month until Election Day. Our team has been watching EMILYs List women gain momentum all across the U.S. this past year — but right now, many of these races are too close for comfort. Republicans know this — it’s why they’re asking their megadonors to spend tens of millions in races up and down the ballot to try and drown our women out. We can’t let that happen. That’s why we’re launching an end-of-quarter 3X Match Fund that runs from today until September 30. Our goal is to raise $500,000 and unlock a full $1.5 million for EMILYs List women. This is a REAL match backed by the EMILYs List community and a REAL chance to triple your impact. And this fund is especially important because it’s our last end-of-quarter deadline before Election Day. = = Match campaigns like this one are only possible when the moment demands it — and when we know that our EMILYs List community will show up. This is crunch time, Peter. Our ability to take back majorities in the U.S. House, U.S. Senate, and state legislatures across the country will be decided by the voters who are just now tuning in to the midterms. And last week, Donald Trump’s personal super PAC reserved over $100 million in advertising to try and sway undecided voters toward Republicans. This has always been the Republican game plan: counting on millions in dark money to hide their record and smear our EMILYs List women. But while they’ve spent the cycle courting special interests, our candidates have shown up each and every day for their communities. EMILYs List women have laid the groundwork for real, grassroots change all cycle. Right now, they’re finalizing their budgets and GOTV plans to make sure they have what they need to win on Election Day. A federal whistleblower lawsuit was just filed against the Shapiro administration.**Every Pennsylvanians should take notice.**[ According to the Philadelphia Inquirer](https://us.list-manage.com/Besct8ZzOh5?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd), a career state employee with nearly 30 years of procurement experience — starting in the Army — says she repeatedly raised concerns about how taxpayer money was being spent inside the administration. She flagged purchases that skipped the required bidding process. She questioned contracts that didn’t follow the rules.**And they fired her for it.** The lawsuit paints a picture of an administration that spent first and asked questions later: bypassing competitive bidding, installing hundreds of thousands of dollars in luxury upgrades with no paper trail, and paying contractors who weren’t even providing services anymore. When someone on the inside tried to hold them accountable, they got rid of her.And the Governor’s response? He called her a “disgruntled former employee.”**Sound familiar?** It should. This is the same administration that covered up a sexual harassment scandal, settled it with taxpayer money, and deleted the emails. Here's something I didn't realize ...
When you're on the campaign trail, there are so many numbers:
* Polls (We're narrowly leading!)
* Expert political forecasters (our race shifted from "Safe Republican" -> "Likely Republican" -> "Lean Republican" -> "TOSS-UP")
* Grassroots fundraising totals (50,000 supporters strong and counting)

But when I'm out on the road listening to Kansans and answering their questions, those kinds of campaign numbers fall by the wayside.
The _real_ meat of this campaign is talking to folks. It's what I love the most. And for me, it's the absolute center of a successful campaign.
**That 's why I'm proud to share a few of the things I've been up to over the past few weeks. Yup, you guessed it: talking to Kansans.**
I spent weeks on a listening tour all across Kansas, meeting voters and answering the questions they have. I called it the Leading from the Middle Tour, because that's what I'm all about: putting an end to the chaos, extreme partisanship and cruelty in Washington and putting the needs of working families first. That's not a left or right issue. It's simply what Kansans deserve.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b319068b-58e8-4816-9154-568bf8eec746?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In Rexford, the McCarty family walked me through their dairy operation. From these conversations and more, it's clear that Washington isn't doing enough to help farmers and ranchers. In fact, Washington is actively making things worse. Tariffs are driving up input costs, and forever wars are making diesel more expensive. It's time to put our hard workers first.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b319068b-58e8-4816-9154-568bf8eec746?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now, don't go trying this at home -- especially not on swivel chairs -- but here's what I know: You can't represent people who never see you. I'll do whatever it takes to make sure every Kansan can see and hear what I'm all about. **Because leadership is a promise to keep showing up.**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b319068b-58e8-4816-9154-568bf8eec746?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Every day, I'm so impressed with the ingenuity of folks in this great state. I visited the incredible Kubota factory in Salina, where they're creating good-paying jobs for hardworking Kansans. I'll fight to keep these jobs in Kansas.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b319068b-58e8-4816-9154-568bf8eec746?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In Wichita, I spoke to James, a lifelong Republican who is voting for me. He's joining thousands of other Republicans and independents who are fed up with Washington insiders, like Sen. Marshall, who have put loyalty to their party over their commitment to Kansans.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b319068b-58e8-4816-9154-568bf8eec746?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
At the Kansas State Fair, I faced Sen. Marshall on the debate stage for the first time. While he defended his Medicaid cuts and extreme medical debt collection practices, I made it clear that I will be a champion for Kansans in the Senate, not a spokesperson for just a party or a president.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b319068b-58e8-4816-9154-568bf8eec746?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
All the while, I've been on national television -- from CNN and NBC to Morning Joe and ABC -- to discuss the reality Kansans are facing: Sky-high prices are hurting folks every single day, and leaders in Washington are not doing enough. I said the same thing to each news anchor: **I 'm running because Kansans deserve better.**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b319068b-58e8-4816-9154-568bf8eec746?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Look, from the moment I stepped up to run for this Senate seat, I knew I would be an underdog. No Democrat has won a Senate race in Kansas in over 90 years. But this grassroots movement -- all the folks I've met on the road, everyone who chipped in from near and far and everyone reading posts like these (yes, you) -- has built incredible momentum and helped turn a "Safe Republican" seat into a tight, competitive race.
I'm committed to running this campaign the right way: not finding corporate PAC donors to bankroll my campaign and not spending time in Florida, like Sen. Marshall has done so often during his term. From the beginning, I decided to do the nitty-gritty work of campaigning: meeting voters face-to-face.
For me, that's not just the right way to build a political movement; it's also a joy. _I love meeting Kansans all across this great state and hearing their passions and concerns_. I'm not afraid to talk to folks who disagree with me. And you have my promise that I will keep listening to those voices. That's how we start to address the deep divides in our country -- and that's also how we win.
But here's the deal (and I promise my finance director isn't writing this part): Meeting Kansans is only _part_ of what will take to get us across the finish line in November -- which is somehow just weeks away. We need resources to compete with Sen. Marshall, who is consistently outspending us (but never out-listening us!). [If you could contribute a few bucks today, it would make a massive difference at this critical moment in our campaign.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b319068b-58e8-4816-9154-568bf8eec746?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for reading. Thank you for being part of this movement. And I look forward to hearing from you, too.
Adam

Driving home from a packed town hall in Claiborne county last night, my deputy campaign manager said, "These are the stories told by campaigns that win unwinnable races. About the moment they knew it was possible. An evening when nearly a hundred people showed up in a rural part of the district, on a church night, with a thunderstorm brewing."
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8cab4916-20b7-4a70-9453-bfaa4ffa047d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Claiborne County Town Hall, September 23. Photo credit: Amelia Bartlett
As always, we didn't end on time so that I could answer every question. People were concerned about AI, education, healthcare, gas, the war, mental health and substance abuse, helping our veterans, and government accountability and corruption.
After I'd finished answering folks' questions, a line formed with people wanting to talk a little more. One young man shared, "I got a text message about this event, and I wasn't too sure. But I'm really glad I came tonight. I think you convinced me."
One woman shared that she didn't follow politics too much, but her husband did. In fact, he'd convinced her to register to vote so she could vote for Trump a few years back. "For him to say he's switching his vote from Republican to you - that's a big deal. He told me he agreed with just about everything you said tonight."
Another young man, an Independent voter who'd asked one of the first questions of the night about abortion, came up to me at the end of the night. "Thank you for listening to me. I think you're someone who cares about us, and I just ask that you remember me when you're in DC representing us."
I'm tucking away these moments with y'all from every event.
At our town hall in Karns last week, a Republican voter approached me and told me, "I agree with you on about 80%. That other 20% is tough, though." I told him I thought 80% was pretty good, and that I hoped I'd earned his vote.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6ecb2080-5a66-4ae0-b049-372b28621144?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Karns Town Hall, September 15. Photo credit: Emery Ball
In Blount county, I couldn't believe it when I turned the corner and saw a line 80-some people deep to get into our town hall. We ended up with about 140 people who came to learn about this movement and ask questions.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b3bb0c4d-9308-4a2b-9ec3-2616adb017bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Blount Town Hall, September 2. Photo credit: Amelia Bartlett
When we launched this campaign a year ago, I know there were plenty of people who thought this was a fool's errand. That this was a waste of precious time, money, energy, and resources.
I didn't think so. As I shared last night, I thought there might be enough people in TN-02 willing to vote for the person they thought might do the job best, not the letter beside their name. That there might be enough people who saw that the way things are going right now isn't serving our neighbors. That we can have better representation - we just have to make sure we don't talk ourselves out of the fight before it ever starts.
In gratitude and solidarity,
Michaela

Trump's new super PAC just reserved $1.7 million in TV ads against me. I'm not going to pretend we can match that. Honestly, we don't need to. Because every evening I walk into one of our volunteer hubs, and I see something no super PAC can buy. Retirees making calls after dinner. Parents knocking doors with a stroller. High schoolers who aren't old enough to vote yet but want to help anyway. People give up their Saturdays, their evenings, and sometimes their knees, all because they care about this community. **These folks are the heart of this campaign, and I want to take good care of them.**

clean_body: My volunteers mean everything to me| | | | = Trump's new super PAC just reserved $1.7 million in TV ads against me. I'm not going to pretend we can match that. Honestly, we don't need to. Because every evening I walk into one of our volunteer hubs, and I see something no super PAC can buy. Retirees making calls after dinner. Parents knocking doors with a stroller. High schoolers who aren't old enough to vote yet but want to help anyway. People give up their Saturdays, their evenings, and sometimes their knees, all because they care about this community. These folks are the heart of this campaign, and I want to take good care of them. = That means making sure they're fed after a long shift. Coffee in the morning, water for the road, and, yes, having some takeout. It means walk lists, clipboards, and flyers so they're never heading out empty-handed. Everyone pretends to be an influencer from their armchair. But here's the reality behind who influences elections the most. The answer may surprise you...
>>> It's not Taylor Swift.

>>> It's not celebrities giving Oscar speeches.

>>> It's not TikTok influencers.
Here's the answer:**It 's ballot chasers**. Real people, in real neighborhoods, knocking on real doors. Meeting voters. Getting to know them. Chasing every single ballot until it's cast.

That's how we won in 2024 for President Trump.

It's how we'll win in 2026, and it's how we'll win in 2028.

Young and energetic people knocking on doors works! It's the biggest influencer in elections.

| It's Patrick, and I'll cut to it: Crypto is spending against Sherrod – to the tune of $30 million. We are the only state they are spending in, and it’s a full-scale campaign emergency.

[I'm not exaggerating when I say that today needs to be our biggest grassroots fundraising day ever. Please step up with a contribution split between our campaign and the Voter Protection Project right now:](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/132635?t=6&akid=29094%2E878179%2El00yis) | [Rush $10 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/132635?t=7&akid=29094%2E878179%2El00yis)

I've got a million thoughts running through my head, but here's what this boils down to.

1\. This tactic worked for Republicans in the last election. In 2024, Sherrod was neck and neck in the polls (just like he is right now), so crypto spent millions of dollars to attack him. And it worked – he slid in the polls and ended up losing.

2\. Senate Republicans put out a cry for help a few weeks ago asking outside spenders to swoop in and bail out Jon Husted. Elon Musk, Peter Thiel, and Donald Trump have already sent in reinforcements and that now means Republicans are spending more in Ohio than anywhere else in the country.

3.**We're doing something right.** Look, the Senate map is ripe with opportunities for Democrats to flip seats, and Republicans are training their eye on Ohio. That is not a coincidence. That is not a mistake. The GOP is the most worried about the campaign Sherrod is running – and that's why they're doing everything they can to put up roadblocks.

**I won't pretend that this spending is nothing to worry about. It has the potential to crush us.** We won’t be able to match their spending 1:1, but we have to be able to stay competitive. If we can mount a strong response, Sherrod will be able to keep his narrow lead in the polls and swing back at Republican attacks.

[I'm authorizing a $1 million emergency response fund to help us fend off the first wave of attacks. Please, friend, Sherrod and I need you to split a donation between our campaign and the Voter Protection Project if you can.](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/132635?t=8&akid=29094%2E878179%2El00yis)

Jewish families across the U.S. and worldwide recently celebrated the Jewish High Holidays of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, the most sacred and widely observed time in the Jewish calendar. These days should offer time for connecting with loved ones - time for gratitude and reflection. **But for too many Jewish Americans, the High Holidays now also bring another feeling: fear.**
Before the High Holidays this year, I spoke with rabbis in southern Nevada, who all shared the same experience: In the moments when they should be preparing special messages for families in their congregations, their energy is being diverted toward security concerns. They're asking themselves questions like: Are our doors secure? How will I respond if someone threatens our congregation? Have we done enough to ensure we are not a target?
As the former president of the largest Reform synagogue in Nevada, I'm all too familiar with the reality that security plays a role in preparing for the Jewish High Holidays - and the funds diverted toward guards, barricades, bulletproof glass, and other precautions, just so American Jews can worship safely.
**Think about that: American families, forced to spend important family holidays behind locked doors, bulletproof glass, and armed guards.**
No Americans should need to worry about their safety just to gather and pray, but the data shows that these fears are well founded: An Anti-Defamation League report found 2025 was the third-highest year for antisemitic incidents in the United States since the ADL began collecting data, and FBI data has shown that Jewish Americans were the target of nearly 70% of religiously motivated hate crimes in this country in 2025 - despite making up just 2% of the population.
We've all seen the disturbing stories behind this data: arson attacks on historic synagogues, congregations defaced with hateful vandalism, and violent firearm attacks. These incidents are part of an alarming trend that underscores a disturbing truth: **Antisemitism is not a thing of the past, but very much still part of the fabric of our society**.
History has shown us what happens when antisemitism is allowed to gain ground - and I recently revisited one of the darkest chapters of history on a trip to Poland and the Auschwitz-Birkenau Memorial and Museum. The preserved grounds of the concentration and extermination camps remind us of the evil that can occur when we don't stop hate in its tracks. The Holocaust was the culmination of years of unchecked violence and marginalization - and we can't stand by and wait to see what might happen if we view the antisemitic trends in our own country with indifference.
**This is why I 'm advocating that Congress take critical steps to protect American Jews, including:**
* Fully funding and reforming the**Nonprofit Security Grant Program** , which helps synagogues and other houses of worship make critical security improvements.
* Passing**bipartisan legislation to nearly triple that program 's funding** and improve how it works, so the money actually reaches the communities that need it.
* Enacting my**Jewish American Security Act** - introduced with Senator Lankford and a broad bipartisan coalition - to create a new Department of Justice grant program to help state and local law enforcement increase security around at-risk houses of worship

These types of protections are about making it possible for families to send their children to Hebrew school without fear, to focus on worship and connection at synagogues rather than safety. **They 're about making sure our houses of worship remain what they're supposed to be: places of faith, places of community, places of peace.**
I keep coming back to something I believe deeply:**Antisemitism doesn 't stay contained. It's an early warning sign, and when we let hatred against one community take root, it eventually threatens everyone. That's the lesson history keeps trying to teach us, if we're willing to listen.**
We don't have the luxury of waiting for the next incident to act. Not after the year we've just seen. Not while rabbis are spending their time on security plans instead of sermons, and families are budgeting for bulletproof glass instead of celebrations.
The time to act is now, before another community pays the price for our inaction.
Thanks for reading, and for standing with me in this fight,
Jacky

##### `Now, I'm proud to fight tirelessly in the Senate to deliver progress for hardworking families like mine in Nevada and across our country. But with Donald Trump in the White House and Republicans in control of both houses of Congress, I need your grassroots support to keep up the fights that matter most.`
##### `Senate Democrats like me are the only thing standing in the way of Trump's extreme agenda that will hurt everyday Americans. That's why I need people like you on my side to help defend our progress and reclaim power from the GOP.`
