If you're on my Substack, you probably know that we just had an exciting election here in Providence, where a young progressive candidate defeated our centrist incumbent mayor. David Morales didn't talk much about Israel/Palestine during his mayoral campaign, but that hasn't stopped certain voices from trying to inject the same narrative of fear that's been pushed front and center in relation to other progressive candidates this year.
A _Jewish Telegraphic Agency_ [story](https://substack.com/redirect/ac55d720-9d72-4a0b-8d66-a30dc20ab64a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Morales's win features a quote from the founder of the Rhode Island-Israel Collaborative that Morales's campaign was fueled by "Israeli haters." The founder of the Rhode Island Coalition for Israel [called](https://substack.com/redirect/2ece933b-2476-41ad-ac18-084aa7c9a85b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Morales' stances "anti-Israel and anti-Jewish." Most recently, the _Boston Globe_ published a piece that many in our community felt was unfair. So I wrote a [response](https://substack.com/redirect/b7844980-e41c-4660-9094-d3ad3d547012?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (alongside two friends, Lex Rofeberg, a local rabbi, and Ruth Ben-Artzi, an Israeli-American professor who interestingly enough happens to be Benjamin Netanyahu's niece). It's maybe a bit parochial, for non-Rhode Islanders. But the themes we discuss are obviously similar to those playing out across the country, so I thought it was worth sharing.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eed816b6-6076-4efb-a1b1-1397be5065c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The _Boston Globe_ 's Sept. 22 piece, ["Providence is poised to have a pro-Palestine mayor, leaving its Jewish community at a crossroads](https://substack.com/redirect/c5a5f93d-1ad4-4305-8110-ea9ce9ae3d45?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," opens with a scene from David Morales's victory party [after the Democratic primary](https://substack.com/redirect/c1fdb462-50ef-4de8-b73c-efe0b3cd52df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It was quite a night. By coincidence, the three of us actually walked into that Sept. 9 event together--a rabbi in the midst of final Rosh Hashanah preparations, a Jewish former state representative, and an Israeli-American college professor.
Upon entering the party, one of us gave a big hug to Providence City Council President Rachel Miller, a prominent supporter of Morales and one of the highest-ranking Jewish elected officials in Rhode Island. Another walked over to congratulate Jenn Steinfeld, Morales's Jewish field director. We waved to Sam Eilertsen, the Jewish filmmaker who directed Morales's launch video, and high-fived [Ben Shanahan](https://substack.com/redirect/ac18efe1-e377-4500-9e23-24c74cf62e22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Morales's Jewish campaign manager. Throughout the night, there were frequent exclamations of Shanah Tovah (Happy New Year), in the midst of other celebratory wishes by Morales's supporters holding a wide variety of religious and racial identities.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=217250246&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE3MjUwMjQ2LCJpYXQiOjE3OTAyODYzNTksImV4cCI6MTc5Mjg3ODM1OSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.vqLuf8tmghZ8-qaKS9lQ4byASmgj-VOE8tJ-o8L3nhg)
Morales's victory party--like his other campaign events, and his army of volunteers, and his inner circle--was full of Jews. Not Jews exclusively, of course, because "Providence for All," Morales's campaign slogan, refers to Providence residents across all backgrounds. But he has seen significant support from Jewish voters--indeed, he won Providence's Third Ward, which encompasses multiple synagogues and has one of the densest populations of Jewish families in the state.
Many of us supported Morales because we were inspired by his commitment to rent stabilization and other policy solutions that can help make Providence a city all of its residents can afford. Some of us were additionally excited by his willingness to take a strong stance against what [countless experts](https://substack.com/redirect/9d48ea9c-b708-4aa2-b11c-61707244964d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and human rights groups--from respected Israeli organizations like [B'Tselem](https://substack.com/redirect/957ce67b-f2b2-4503-b575-9c450c4124f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Physicians for Human Rights Israel](https://substack.com/redirect/697362ac-f1df-4080-b267-e80718457dd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), to international organizations like [Amnesty International](https://substack.com/redirect/3c87cfda-c071-4fa6-87a7-aef08b6dd639?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Human Rights Watch](https://substack.com/redirect/dd450b0f-af11-450c-b992-9f25eebdc339?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), to scholars like Omer Bartov, an Israeli professor of Holocaust studies right here at Brown University--all [agree to be a genocide](https://substack.com/redirect/908bf4cf-81ef-4ca1-8b93-5f9848afd308?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
At least, he's taken that strong stance whenever Israel/Palestine has happened to come up. To be clear, Morales--as a candidate for municipal office--rarely, if ever, discussed these issues unprompted. We often hear that Israel is singled out for disproportionate criticism. But Morales primarily expressed his positions on Israel, [the genocide in Gaza](https://substack.com/redirect/44796ef8-b17a-43aa-b3a0-fd5da665ff37?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and ethnic cleansing [in the West Bank](https://substack.com/redirect/c2b54899-bc8e-4cda-bbb2-b084ab913d24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as a response to often-hostile questions. Morales's campaign focused on Providence and delivering for the city--for all its residents, including its Jewish ones.
Despite this reality, the _Globe_ 's story frequently invoked antisemitism in relation to Morales, quoting one Jewish resident of Providence who said, "[T]he impact of the constant rhetoric around Israel does feed into antisemitism, and into the safety of [Morales's] likely future constituents." We agree that [rising antisemitism](https://substack.com/redirect/7eccb348-225b-4024-979c-405cab8953fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), in this moment of resurgent fascism, is a very real concern. But the quoted perspective is a grave misdiagnosis of the problem. Naming and withholding support for atrocities does not exacerbate antisemitism--equating support for those atrocities with Jewishness and Judaism does.
Most Americans--and eight out of 10 Democrats--disapprove of Israel, [according to The Pew Research Center](https://substack.com/redirect/fe0195dd-78be-4bd6-a365-1040d4388a66?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). This isn't just because people are criticizing Israel for committing war crimes. It's because Israel is committing war crimes. Of course it doesn't reflect well on the Jewish community that the self-defined Jewish state keeps engaging in horrific violence, under a Star of David and ostensibly on behalf of the Jewish people. And that's particularly true when partisans of Israel claim that anyone who dares to speak out against these crimes is an antisemite--that is, someone who hates all Jews. The implication of these weaponized claims of antisemitism is that Israel's oppression of Palestinians is somehow a crime committed by all Jews, rather than the project of a specific far-right government and its supporters. And if you repeat that message often enough, some people are going to start believing it--which certainly does not make us safer.
In other words, to claim Morales's ([objectively mainstream](https://substack.com/redirect/69f2123f-0661-48c8-af40-9faac66e277d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)) criticism of Israel is somehow antisemitic amplifies the antisemitic trope conflating American Jews with Israel.
Some Jews in Providence support unlimited material support to Israel. That is their right. But it is offensive to argue that those who disagree with this position--or who support an upcoming [ballot initiative](https://substack.com/redirect/8ddc6d25-e8e1-46bd-869d-b5220633e098?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that would require the City of Providence to divest from foreign countries "[conducting ethnic cleansing, apartheid, illegal military occupation, or genocide](https://substack.com/redirect/a173cc12-88b9-476f-bdf5-76e3c0e9f89e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," as Morales and many members of Providence's Jewish community have--are either a small group of "dissenters" from a clear Jewish viewpoint, or that we are antagonistic to our own community. Neither is the case.
Our community faces real threats: Just a few years ago, dozens of swastika-brandishing neo-Nazis [rallied a block from one of our homes](https://substack.com/redirect/69e21908-02d6-4326-b31c-dd7bbe0a9004?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Every time stories like the Sept. 22 _Globe_ piece frame a disagreement over the best ways to respond to a foreign government's atrocities as the primary threat to Jewish safety, it minimizes the real dangers we face, making our community less prepared to respond to actual antisemitic threats. Providence, and the Jews who call it home, deserve better.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eed816b6-6076-4efb-a1b1-1397be5065c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Fellow Conservative: Texas is about to decide the fate of the Senate majority — and if we lose it, we won't just lose a seat. We'll hand Democrats their first statewide win in Texas since 1994, and the earthquake will be felt by Americans across the country. First, let's be clear about how we got here. The Republican establishment in DC spent over $150 million — the most expensive Senate primary in American history — trying to stop Ken Paxton from becoming the nominee. _They lost._ Paxton defeated Sen. John Cornyn by nearly 30 points. But the damage was done, and now Democrat James Talarico is within striking distance of flipping the seat. You'd think Cornyn would be all-in to stop him from turning Texas blue. Nope. Instead, he's trashing Paxton as lazy and a poor campaigner, while telling reporters the party shouldn't spend another dime on his race because of limited resources. That's rich. **Even worse, Cornyn is working with former President George W. Bush to pull money out of Texas to fund moderate Senate candidates in other states — many of whom are far bigger underdogs than Paxton.** With friends like these, who needs enemies?

Ken Paxton has spent over a decade as Texas Attorney General doing what the GOP establishment only talks about. He sued the Biden administration more than any other AG in the country — on the border, on illegal mandates, on federal overreach — and won. While career politicians in Washington cut deals, Paxton has been on the front lines of the fight against the open-borders agenda. President Trump didn't endorse him as an afterthought — he called Paxton a "true MAGA warrior" because Paxton has earned it. That's exactly why the establishment tried to kill his campaign before it started and why they're throwing a temper tantrum now. A real fighter in the Senate threatens the comfortable do-nothing environment they've built in DC. They'd rather have an empty suit who plays along with their empty promises and endless excuses than a conservative who delivers. **Make no mistake: John Cornyn and the GOP establishment are working against Paxton because they want Texas to lose. They need it to lose, so they can point at the wreckage and say, _"See? Only RINOs can win."_ It's a self-fulfilling prophecy.** They know the game. Give conservative voters a choice between a Democrat and a RINO, and we'll hold our nose and vote RINO. But give us a choice between a Democrat and a real conservative, and the establishment would rather watch us lose than let us win on our own terms. Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Troy Jackson was caught on camera fleeing questions about clients who paid money to his son's lobbying firm and subsequently benefitted from actions Jackson took as Maine Senate President.
In a video posted by the NRSC, Jackson can be seen fleeing a mob of political activists and media in Washington, D.C., where the former Democratic lawmaker is reportedly spending time raising campaign cash.
An unnamed activist asks questions about payments made to Resurgam Group, a lobbying firm founded by B.J. McCollister, Jackson's former chief of staff, and Chace Jackson, one of the sons produced through Jackson's consanguineous relationship with his second cousin.
Public lobbyist disclosures and State House records show that Jackson was integral in advancing -- or killing -- legislation related to candidates who paid major contracts to Resurgam Group, including contracts in which Chace Jackson was the primary lobbyist.
This Substack is reader-supported. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..lw5Y-BB6DBBrp2BQZDYzDfdgwp7Noj45yzXMxbjbdoU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=217280302)
As the Bangor Daily News first reported, Jackson shifted his position on three key gun control policies less than a month after Chace Jackson began a $50,000 contract with the Maine Gun Safety Coalition.
For more than two decades, Jackson had proudly held himself out as a pro-gun Democrat, opposing assault weapon bans, expanded background checks, and three-day waiting periods for firearm purchases.
Chace Jackson inked the Maine Gun Safety Coalition agreement in December 2023. Less than a month later, Jackson told a left-wing 501(c)4 dark money group (which happened to be Jackson's employer) that he was changing his position 180 degrees to support assault weapon bans, expanded background checks, and three-day waiting periods for firearm purchases.
Neither Troy Jackson nor Chace Jackson have ever [commented](https://substack.com/redirect/8409e8d8-409f-44d7-8445-d8c8f0626ddd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) publicly on the appearance of a pay to play arrangement with Resurgam and the Maine Gun Safety Coalition.
The Maine Gun Safety Coalition wasn't the only advocacy group that sent money to Resurgam specifically to lobby for gun control prior to Troy Jackson's flip on gun control. Public records show the Maine Public Health Association paid $17,500 to Chace Jackson before Troy Jackson voted in favor of the very gun contorl policies he'd long opposed.
But the gun control flipflop isn't the only instance where industry players and activist groups funneled money to Jackson's son while simultaneously seeking favorable legislative outcomes from the Senate President.
The clearest client-specific financial benefit is $8.5 million in the 2024 supplemental budget for Covenant Health's St. Mary's hospital. As Senate President within a state government completely controlled by the Maine Democratic Party, Jackson would have had totalitarian control over what went into a spending bill and what was left out.
Lobbyist disclosure documents from 2024 identify Chace Jackson as principal lobbyist and McCollister as associate, with $24,000 in compensation reported from St. Mary's. While the lobbyist disclosure ties the contract to a separate piece of legislation, the pattern is clear: Chace Jackson got paid by a client, then Troy Jackson oversaw the flow of money to that client.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2246936&post_id=217280302&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE3MjgwMzAyLCJpYXQiOjE3OTAyODY4MjIsImV4cCI6MTc5Mjg3ODgyMiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTIyNDY5MzYiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.t0DistjKqTs08cj8w5tCANtOB3ex4Sck1cwMjNKilf4)
In another instance of Chace Jackson's lobbyist clients benefitting from Troy Jackson's control of the State Legislature, Resurgam landed the Maine Service Employees Association - SEIU Local 1989 (aka the state government employees union) as clients in 2024. The disclosures list LD 2032 among the bills Jackson and McCollister were paid to lobby, and Troy Jackson voted in favor of the collective bargaining bill in April 2024.
In yet another case, Troy Jackson backed off-shore wind legislation and carveouts for union laborers that were advocated for by Resurgam client Maine Labor Climate Council. According to Resurgam promotion documents, the client was well pleased with the outcome.
"Hiring Resurgam is crucial to building a winning campaign in Maine, and we owe them a lot for our coalition's big win on offshore wind legislation in 2023," Francis Eanes [said](https://substack.com/redirect/f94e0926-aefe-46c4-beec-1365d1a9957d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "Their strategic advice was central to knowing where to shift limited campaign resources, when and how to escalate pressure on decision makers, and when to negotiate."
When the national media began exploring the connection between Chace Jackson's clients and Troy Jackson's official actions as the most powerful Democratic lawmaker in Maine, Jackson the Younger appears to have deleted his LinkedIn profile. But archived images show him describing himself as a partner at the firm, which McCollister started in 2021.

Maine's ethics laws for state lawmakers are notoriously weak. With the exception of a few lawmakers getting caught forging signatures on petitions to collection Maine Clean Elections Act petition signatures, lawmakers almost never get in trouble for even obvious self-dealing.
For example, in its March 12, 2010 opinion concerning Rep. John Hinck, the Maine Ethics Commission allowed him to vote on wind-permitting legislation although his wife represented wind-power companies.

In a video posted by the NRSC, Jackson can be seen fleeing a mob of political activists and media in Washington, D.C., where the former Democratic lawmaker is reportedly spending time raising campaign cash. An unnamed activist asks questions about payments made to Resurgam Group, a lobbying firm founded by B.J. McCollister, Jackson's former chief of staff, and Chace Jackson, one of the sons produced through Jackson's consanguineous relationship with his second cousin. Public lobbyist disclosures and State House records show that Jackson was integral in advancing -- or killing -- legislation related to candidates who paid major contracts to Resurgam Group, including contracts in which Chace Jackson was the primary lobbyist. This Substack is reader-supported. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. As the Bangor Daily News first reported, Jackson shifted his position on three key gun control policies less than a month after Chace Jackson began a $50,000 contract with the Maine Gun Safety Coalition. For more than two decades, Jackson had proudly held himself out as a pro-gun Democrat, opposing assault weapon bans, expanded background checks, and three-day waiting periods for firearm purchases. Chace Jackson inked the Maine Gun Safety Coalition agreement in December 2023. Less than a month later, Jackson told a left-wing 501(c)4 dark money group (which happened to be Jackson's employer) that he was changing his position 180 degrees to support assault weapon bans, expanded background checks, and three-day waiting periods for firearm purchases. Neither Troy Jackson nor Chace Jackson have ever publicly on the appearance of a pay to play arrangement with Resurgam and the Maine Gun Safety Coalition. The Maine Gun Safety Coalition wasn't the only advocacy group that sent money to Resurgam specifically to lobby for gun control prior to Troy Jackson's flip on gun control. Public records show the Maine Public Health Association paid $17,500 to Chace Jackson before Troy Jackson voted in favor of the very gun contorl policies he'd long opposed. But the gun control flipflop isn't the only instance where industry players and activist groups funneled money to Jackson's son while simultaneously seeking favorable legislative outcomes from the Senate President. The clearest client-specific financial benefit is $8.5 million in the 2024 supplemental budget for Covenant Health's St. Mary's hospital. As Senate President within a state government completely controlled by the Maine Democratic Party, Jackson would have had totalitarian control over what went into a spending bill and what was left out. Lobbyist disclosure documents from 2024 identify Chace Jackson as principal lobbyist and McCollister as associate, with $24,000 in compensation reported from St. Mary's. While the lobbyist disclosure ties the contract to a separate piece of legislation, the pattern is clear: Chace Jackson got paid by a client, then Troy Jackson oversaw the flow of money to that client. In another instance of Chace Jackson's lobbyist clients benefitting from Troy Jackson's control of the State Legislature, Resurgam landed the Maine Service Employees Association - SEIU Local 1989 (aka the state government employees union) as clients in 2024. The disclosures list LD 2032 among the bills Jackson and McCollister were paid to lobby, and Troy Jackson voted in favor of the collective bargaining bill in April 2024. In yet another case, Troy Jackson backed off-shore wind legislation and carveouts for union laborers that were advocated for by Resurgam client Maine Labor Climate Council. According to Resurgam promotion documents, the client was well pleased with the outcome. "Hiring Resurgam is crucial to building a winning campaign in Maine, and we owe them a lot for our coalition's big win on offshore wind legislation in 2023," Francis Eanes . "Their strategic advice was central to knowing where to shift limited campaign resources, when and how to escalate pressure on decision makers, and when to negotiate." When the national media began exploring the connection between Chace Jackson's clients and Troy Jackson's official actions as the most powerful Democratic lawmaker in Maine, Jackson the Younger appears to have deleted his LinkedIn profile. But archived images show him describing himself as a partner at the firm, which McCollister started in 2021. | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- Maine's ethics laws for state lawmakers are notoriously weak. With the exception of a few lawmakers getting caught forging signatures on petitions to collection Maine Clean Elections Act petition signatures, lawmakers almost never get in trouble for even obvious self-dealing. For example, in its March 12, 2010 opinion concerning Rep. John Hinck, the Maine Ethics Commission allowed him to vote on wind-permitting legislation although his wife represented wind-power companies. ? You 're receiving The Robinson Report for free. Peter,
254 counties in Texas — more than in any other state in the country.
254 counties where over 30 million Texans live, making us the second most populous state in the country.
Every dollar of this campaign goes to fighting for each and every Texan across these 254 counties.
And $1 is all it takes.
$1 goes a long way in getting our message out to voters all across the state, fighting back against Abbott’s attack ads, and powering our organizing program. We know — 254 is _a lot_ of counties to reach with _a lot_ of voters to mobilize, so we need all the support we can get in these final 6 weeks.
$1 may not seem like a lot, but when you chip in, and your neighbor chips in, and your family member chips in, it adds up quickly. And it puts us within reach of the governorship, but only if we keep fighting for it.
With a grassroots movement as strong as ours — _with nearly 200,000 individual donors_ — people power is all we need.
A Texas whose government works for all its families is within our grasp. But we need to continue building momentum every day until November 3rd.

| | | **_“When I launched my campaign for Congress last December, I committed to not bringing up the topic for the first few months. I wanted to focus on the skyrocketing costs of groceries, health care, rent, and childcare to build the trust needed to raise concerns about AI. _** **_“I was wrong. In my first week on the trail, voters asked me about AI at every single event we held. And it hasn’t slowed down in the past nine months.”_**
---
This is the start of the piece I published this week in _The New Republic_ , entitled “AI Preemption Is the New NAFTA.” It summarizes hundreds of conversations from the campaign trail about how the people are far more ready than the parties for a national conversation and agenda on AI. This gap is not just because of the corrupting power of Big Tech’s money on public debate. Rather, it is because the powerful treat AI as something fundamentally new (which it is), while the people are treating it as a massive accelerant of problems our politics have failed to solve for decades (which it also is). I hope you’ll read [the whole thing](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139896822/648870235/1269056589?refcode=260924em_tp_ai&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjIxMDkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTEwZTA0NDYtNjNiOC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=6cBGfz3fgy_W3u5vggLkWCgWl7Aq2TNuPc5Uy8Gpx6U=&emci=4569cfbc-47b8-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=910e0446-63b8-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=18671963) (sorry for the length!) and share it with friends and share any feedback with me. Thanks for all of your support that has put me in a position to win this race and to be part of an urgent effort in January of 2027 to establish immediate guardrails and liability and begin a longer conversation about the role of human agency and employment. AI is shaping this election well beyond conversations about data centers, and will dominate 2028. With your continued support, I believe that my district and my voice can be part of propelling us towards national urgency on these issues. Here’s the full column: [https://newrepublic.com/article/215663/ai-preemption-new-nafta-working-americans](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139896823/648870236/1269056589?refcode=260924em_tp_ai&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjIxMDkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTEwZTA0NDYtNjNiOC1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=6cBGfz3fgy_W3u5vggLkWCgWl7Aq2TNuPc5Uy8Gpx6U=&emci=4569cfbc-47b8-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=910e0446-63b8-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=18671963) Thanks for reading. –Tom

I wanted to focus on the skyrocketing costs of groceries, health care, rent, and childcare to build the trust needed to raise concerns about AI. “I was wrong. In my first week on the trail, voters asked me about AI at every single event we held. And it hasn’t slowed down in the past nine months.” This is the start of the piece I published this week in The New Republic , entitled “AI Preemption Is the New NAFTA.” It summarizes hundreds of conversations from the campaign trail about how the people are far more ready than the parties for a national conversation and agenda on AI. This gap is not just because of the corrupting power of Big Tech’s money on public debate. Rather, it is because the powerful treat AI as something fundamentally new (which it is), while the people are treating it as a massive accelerant of problems our politics have failed to solve for decades (which it also is). I hope you’ll read (sorry for the length!) and share it with friends and share any feedback with me. Thanks for all of your support that has put me in a position to win this race and to be part of an urgent effort in January of 2027 to establish immediate guardrails and liability and begin a longer conversation about the role of human agency and employment. AI is shaping this election well beyond conversations about data centers, and will dominate 2028. Say, Peter – just who exactly is Michael Whatley, our Republican opponent in North Carolina’s U.S. Senate race?

[**_If that’s all you need to hear, chip in $5 now to help Roy Cooper defeat him_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1417&amount=5&t=9&akid=3841%2E124072%2EtViot1) – but if not, here are four more things you need to know about Michael Whatley that explain everything:

body:
Join our volunteer zoom meeting at 8:30 PM tonight!

| | | | | |

---
| | Good Afternoon Team Demuth!
**Zoom Meeting**
I want to remind everyone that we will have our regularly scheduled grassroots volunteer meeting tonight at 8:30 PM. We will talk about yard signs, volunteer efforts, updates on Right Insight, some events coming up, and much much more! Hope to see you there!!
https://us06web.zoom.us/j/87316568944 pwd=vs7Gxvi65GvxFCyOYbtOFX8SLTOutp.1
**Update on Right Insight**
We are officially launching our Right Insight efforts out far and wide. Call lists have been updated and are ready to roll as is door knocking. To win, we need everyone’s help! It is absolutely crucial that we all participate and invite more to join our team as well. **Even five minutes of phone calling, or door knocking even just your neighbors goes an incredibly long way!**
All of you that have previously been volunteers already have accounts. Simply download the app and sign in using the email address you received this message at. You will be sent a six-digit code to verify your identity, then you’re all logged in and ready to roll!For door knocking, we are utilizing a feature called Near Me. This will allow volunteers to go out and door knock houses that are nearby them. That list will change as you move around, so you can use it anywhere.Calls will be broken down by Congressional District. When we add you to Right Insight, we will assign you to calls specific for your area so you are talking to people who you may know, or share more common issues. Most of you will likely see all of them until we are able to organize you into Congressional district teams, so please just call into the CD you are from. For example, if you are from CD 1, call CD1.**If you do login and are told you do not have an account, please fill out the form below and we will get you added!**[ Sign up for a Right Insight Account.](https://us.list-manage.com/S4b3Ubt5wYW?e=422536b04e&c2id=3f96188058f7a1407b5cde0c924e7fd7)Both calls and door knocking projects are live and ready for volunteers. We are very excited to get everyone started! If you have technical questions or are unsure of how to get started, please call Caleb at 612-300-4202 or email him at Caleb@mngop.com**Signs and Literature** We currently have around 750 people who have requested signs for their property. This is a high priority for getting out! If you would be willing to deliver lawn signs to others, please let Logan know by emailing or calling him at the number below.Additionally, if you’d like to do some door knocking or phone-calling, contact Caleb at 612-300-4202.We look forward to seeing everyone on the call tonight! Thank you for joining us. With your help, we will elect Lisa Demuth as our next Governor and restore common sense to Minnesota.
---

subject: Ukraine's Order of Merit for Reps. Golden and Fitzpatrick | UNGA Recap
body:
| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/11eNi26myhm?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720)
| | | | |

| | _Congressmen Jared Golden (left) and Brian Fitzpatrick (right) receive the Ukrainian Order of Merit from President Volodymyr Zelenskyy._
---
| | Dear Peter,
Yesterday at the United Nations, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy awarded Ukraine's Order of Merit to Rep. Jared Golden (D-ME), former Co-Chair of the [For Country Caucus](https://us.list-manage.com/MZfw3m770xM?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720), and Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA), Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus, two cross-partisan leaders who have stood with Ukraine since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion and are profiled in [_Courage Can Save US_](https://us.list-manage.com/iKi9QHeuI5l?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720).
Last week, Reps. Fitzpatrick and Golden played consequential roles in passing the [Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026](https://us.list-manage.com/W7HyHvm8IcH?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720), which Rep. Fitzpatrick discussed the next morning on [With Honor’s call](https://us.list-manage.com/RX0nbQcr0wG?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720) with four other Members of Congress, including Rep. Don Bacon, the Founding Co-Chair of the For Country Caucus and a participant on With Honor’s fourth bipartisan delegation to Ukraine two weeks ago. You can read more about the delegation trip [here](https://us.list-manage.com/kJe6spXgvq9?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720), along with perspectives from delegation members Gillian Tett in the [_Financial Times_](https://us.list-manage.com/yzg7jo19inN?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720) and With Honor Action Advisory Board Member Elliot Ackerman in [_The Free Press_](https://us.list-manage.com/uI4cdlMDsYt?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720).
On Tuesday night, [With Honor](https://us.list-manage.com/nFc2MO00oMy?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720) gathered with members of the U.S., Ukrainian, and British delegations during the U.N. General Assembly. Ukrainian MP Sasha Ustinova, who has worked alongside With Honor since the first days of the war, spoke about being pursued by a Russian drone while traveling near the front with Rep. Fitzpatrick, and about Rep. Golden’s leadership bringing the Russia sanctions bill to the House floor.
You may watch a highlight reel of our event by clicking [here](https://us.list-manage.com/FB1COMNZBuS?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720) or by clicking on the image below, including remarks from cross-partisan veterans in the British Parliament, the Rt Hon Tom Tugendhat MP, Shadow Foreign Secretary, and Al Carns MP, former Minister for the Armed Forces.

To give you a sense of how this all fits together, Wisconsin, Minnesota, and Washington are three of the 15 priority states in our overall plan to defeat Donald Trump’s gerrymandering and protect our democracy.
These are places where our endorsed Democracy Defenders can hold the line against new attempts to manipulate the maps. And where we can secure strong pro-democracy trifectas this November, leaders can draw responsive new maps that counter Republican gerrymandering across the country and help make sure the will of the people is heard at the ballot box.
Here’s what that looks like state by state:
In Wisconsin, we need to hold the governor’s seat and flip the slim Republican majorities in the state assembly and senate — control of these chambers is finally within reach now that our movement helped win fairer maps in the Badger state.
In Minnesota, we need to win a majority in the state house. It’s currently TIED, so just one race could decide the whole ball game. And we’ve got to expand a pro-democracy majority in the state senate.
And in Washington State, we need to grow our majorities in both chambers in order to put the state in a position to fight back against Donald Trump’s national redistricting crisis.
Having more incredible candidates to support is a good problem to have — but it also means we need to have a budget that can be helpful in every critical race. So with a larger playing field right now, I have to ask:

We just announced a new round of endorsements for our Democracy Defenders program — each election year, we support candidates for state-level offices we believe are most critical to safeguarding and strengthening democracy. Here is the latest round of candidates we think you should know and join us in supporting: Wisconsin: David Crowley for Governor and 22 candidates for state assembly and senate Minnesota: 23 candidates for state house and senate Washington State: 19 candidates for state house and senate = | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = To give you a sense of how this all fits together, Wisconsin, Minnesota, and Washington are three of the 15 priority states in our overall plan to defeat Donald Trump’s gerrymandering and protect our democracy. These are places where our endorsed Democracy Defenders can hold the line against new attempts to manipulate the maps. And where we can secure strong pro-democracy trifectas this November, leaders can draw responsive new maps that counter Republican gerrymandering across the country and help make sure the will of the people is heard at the ballot box. Here’s what that looks like state by state: In Wisconsin, we need to hold the governor’s seat and flip the slim Republican majorities in the state assembly and senate — control of these chambers is finally within reach now that our movement helped win fairer maps in the Badger state. In Minnesota, we need to win a majority in the state house. It’s currently TIED, so just one race could decide the whole ball game. And we’ve got to expand a pro-democracy majority in the state senate. And in Washington State, we need to grow our majorities in both chambers in order to put the state in a position to fight back against Donald Trump’s national redistricting crisis. Having more incredible candidates to support is a good problem to have — but it also means we need to have a budget that can be helpful in every critical race. It's Coach. I need your attention for a few minutes.

Today, I want to talk to you about the gender confused individuals destroying our Christian values and our beautiful nation.

**These people are not normal. They are sick. They have a mental illness. AND we need to stop accommodating them NOW. Here 's why.**

These gender confused individuals are not only hurting themselves, but also other people. A study in 2022 showed that gender confused individuals are at the highest risk of becoming violently radicalized.

**We have a recent example of this violence.**

In 2019, a gender confused individual walked into their high school, killing one classmate and injuring eight others.

In 2022, a person who identified as non-binary killed five people at a nightclub in Colorado.

In 2023, a transgender person shot up the Christian School in Tennessee, killing three children and three adults. This lunatic was a woman who identified as a man.

In 2024, Thomas Crooks, the lunatic who shot President Trump, was involved with the online furry culture and apparently used they/them pronouns.

In 2025, a transgender person shot up a catholic school in Minnesota.

In 2025, a transgender person in Utah shot and killed my good friend Charlie Kirk. The bullets were engraved with phrases praising the transgender movement. The assassination was celebrated by these mentally ill people.

I'm always going to reject Socialism.I'm always going to fight against the anti-American way of life.And this has enraged a lot of people in the media, in my party, and even former staffers --- disgruntled leakers who are viciously and anonymously attacking me. They want to...Abolish our bordersAbolish the electoral collegeAbolish IsraelAbolish the Senate and the Supreme Court (no, seriously, this is in the "DSA!" platform)That bad news is the "DSA!" crazies have gone from the political fringe to controlling one of America's major political parties—and onto ballots across the country.The good news is the hardworking, common-sense Americans I talk to every day still aren't buying it.I mean, a recent Rasmussen poll kind of proves it:71% of Americans reject socialism67% of Democrat voters reject socialism While 82% of Republican voters reject socialismBut here's the thing. The loudest voice in the room is often the one that looks the most powerful.And I've got to say, the "DSA!" voices in Washington are loud and getting louder. The media is their megaphone. Which is why you may be under the false impression that people really do want the "DSA!" and their extreme policiesNothing could be further from the truth. But sadly I'm pretty much alone on this side of the aisle.So, can I ask you a favor? Whatever your party affiliation is, can I ask you to stand with me against the daily barrage of hit-pieces But it will also send a message. It will show the truth that the "real numbers" are on our side here in Pennsylvania, as well as around the rest of America. A brave christian student **[called out far-left Michigan senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed](https://substack.com/redirect/4e8aacf4-d5cc-4c26-acbc-d9f7797dfa2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for refusing to condemn Iran's Ayatollah after the Trump administration killed him with military strikes earlier this year.
"My cousin was hunted in the streets of Iran by the IRGC because her hijab wasn't on right," the student told El-Sayed. "I want to ask if you regret your silence!"

# **El-Sayed headlines Dearborn fundraiser alongside pro-Hamas activist**
Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed spoke at a low-profile Wednesday fundraiser in Dearborn, featuring Osama Siblani, head of the Arab American Political Action Committee, who has previously called Hamas and Hezbollah "freedom fighters" and said Israeli Jews should be sent "back to Poland," **[The Washington Free Beacon reports.](https://substack.com/redirect/4a1b4492-dc81-4ad5-a65f-aecf4eb6a052?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

* **Speakers also included Amer Zahr** , a Dearborn school board member who has praised late Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah as a "hero," as well as Imam Mohammad Ali Elahi, who has eulogized Iran's late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, reflecting the event's deep ties to Dearborn's Arab-American political base.
* **Many attendees reportedly expressed hostility toward Kamala Harris,** who El-Sayed campaigned alongside earlier this week, over the 2024 "Uncommitted" movement's boycott of the Biden-Harris ticket due to the administration's pro-Israel stance.

# **Butler, PA Trump rally shooting survivor James Copenhaver dies, dealt with permanent injuries**
James Copenhaver, wounded during the 2024 assassination attempt on Trump in Butler, Pennsylvania, **[has died in his mid-70s,](https://substack.com/redirect/dcdcb328-8594-4d0a-b461-60e6372954a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** according to family confirmation and a House Republican Conference statement mourning his loss.

| 11:15 PM * Sep 24, 2026 * 3.13K Views5 Replies * 14 Reposts * 59 Likes

* **Copenhaver was shot twice that day,** later describing the moment in a 2025 interview, and had continued dealing with permanent injuries, including bullet fragments still in his body, prompting a lawsuit against the U.S. government over required surgeries.
* **Slippery Rock Mayor Jondavid Longo, who spoke at the rally, mourned Copenhaver alongside victims** Corey Comperatore, who was killed, and David Dutch, who survived. The attack later led to Secret Service Director Kimberly Cheatle's resignation and a bipartisan finding that the shooting was preventable.

# **Denmark warns Russia could launch limited NATO attack within months**
Denmark's Defense Intelligence Service warned of a "low but growing risk" that **[Russia could send troops or fire long-range weapons at a NATO country](https://substack.com/redirect/327a0e92-7cc8-493b-99e4-d7aa2db58919?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in the coming months, framing it as a desperate move amid Russia's struggles in Ukraine.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/327a0e92-7cc8-493b-99e4-d7aa2db58919?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Officials said Russia might justify an incursion by claiming to protect Russian minorities abroad,** potentially using unmarked troops or staging a false-flag attack with Ukrainian-made drones -- tactics aimed at dividing NATO rather than seizing territory.
* **The agency also expects intensified Russian hybrid warfare,** including sabotage and cyberattacks with a higher risk of casualties, following incidents like undersea cable damage and a drone incursion near a German airport. Denmark estimated Russia could pose a regional threat within two years and be capable of large-scale war in five.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: I need to talk about New Hampshire
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/221?c0=em_ms_cp_20260924_3.0jDkz4&refcode=em20260924-3&t=1001&akid=9117%2E582294%2EWlwBYa ]Elizabeth Warren

I recently visited New Hampshire, where I spent time on the trail with
Chris Pappas. And I'm writing to you today because the general election
fight is officially here – and the stakes could not be higher.

Look – if
we’re going to take back the Democratic Senate majority and put our
government back on the side of working families, winning in New Hampshire
is absolutely critical.

We know what we’re up against in this general election fight. Donald Trump
and right-wing billionaires are getting ready to flood New Hampshire with
dark money to elect John Sununu.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260924_3.HXI2p-&refcode=em20260924-3&t=1002&akid=9117%2E582294%2EWlwBYa ]Can you make a $5 donation – or whatever makes sense for
you today – to help Chris Pappas stand up to corporate special interests,
defeat John Sununu, and keep New Hampshire blue?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260924_3.HXI2p-&amount=5&refcode=em20260924-3&t=1021&akid=9117%2E582294%2EWlwBYa ]Donate $5 »

Let’s be clear about who John Sununu is: He’s spent his entire career
cozying up to corporate donors and selling out to Big Oil and Big Pharma
at the expense of regular people. If Sununu gets to Washington, we know
exactly what he’ll do: serve as a rubber stamp for Trump's dangerous
agenda, greenlight more corporate tax giveaways, and push the exact kind
of corruption that rigs our economy against working families.

We cannot let John Sununu back into the U.S. Senate.

Chris Pappas is the exact opposite. As a small business owner, he knows
how the economy should work: fair, honest, and transparent. In Congress,
he’s taken on Big Pharma to lower drug prices, stood up to corporate price
gouging, defended reproductive freedom, and fought for our veterans.

And here’s the thing: Chris doesn’t take a dime of corporate PAC money.
Not one single cent.

That means he relies entirely on people-powered grassroots support to win
tough fights like this one.

Polling shows this general election race is a dead heat. With corporate
special interests getting ready to buy this seat for Sununu, we need to
show the GOP right now that we have what it takes to win.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260924_3.HXI2p-&refcode=em20260924-3&t=1022&akid=9117%2E582294%2EWlwBYa ]That’s why I’m asking for you to step up and chip in right
now –
will you give $5 to boost Chris’s campaign and show the GOP
that New Hampshire isn’t for sale?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260924_3.HXI2p-&amount=5&refcode=em20260924-3&t=1023&akid=9117%2E582294%2EWlwBYa ]Donate $5 »

I’m in this fight because I believe in what’s possible when Washington
works for working families, not billionaires and corporate lobbyists.
Chris Pappas is in this fight for the exact same reason.

Let's stand with him today and get this done.

Thanks for being in this fight,

Elizabeth

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.chrispappas.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=9117%2E582294%2EWlwBYa

name: Grant Goldberg
subject: Hi Peter, let me introduce myself - Johnny Garcia's Organizing Director
body:
| Hi Peter,

I just wanted to introduce myself real quick. My name is Grant Goldberg, and I'm Johnny's new Organizing Director.

I'm here to be a resource for you no matter how you want to help; Whether that's blockwalking, phone banking, putting up signs, or writing postcards–whatever you want to do, I'm here to help make it happen.

I won't take up any more of your time talking about myself, but I do want to take a moment to tell you about some of the things we have coming up:

On Sunday 9/27, we have a [blockwalk in the Windcrest area](https://votejohnnygarcia.org/l/sWgYXarQAOUF). I know the district is huge and that might not be in your backyard, but if you're able to make it out we'd love to have you.

On Wednesday 9/30 we will have our first [in-person phone bank](https://votejohnnygarcia.org/l/Mju5SYxhUjbo) calling voters who might not know they've been redistricted. There will be an option to join virtually as well.

Next Saturday 10/3, we have a [blockwalk with Johnny](https://votejohnnygarcia.org/l/yGkQ0GxkTGFk), and looking further out we have a [blockwalk with Johnny, Zack Dunn, and Ron Nirenburg](https://votejohnnygarcia.org/l/y5Tp9cD8LT0A) on October 11th!

That's just the beginning. Over the next couple of weeks I will be building out our full October schedule where we will be hitting the pavement hard. I will add new events to our [Mobilize page](https://votejohnnygarcia.org/l/K5A7ZChEcQrm) as they are locked in and will keep you in the loop with new opportunities as they come up.

If you have an idea for an event or would like to host a phone bank or blockwalk, just let me know!

Click here to [unsubscribe](https://votejohnnygarcia.org/l/yFp0Ku6XAjr0)
